It hung in the air with its feet just above the ground, a gaunt, elongated humanoid of matte charcoal-black whose limbs, far too long for the torso, tapered to fine points. In place of a face, the skull opened into a crown of jagged spines that split upward and outward like antlers of molten metal, running white-gold at their tips. Molten seams glowed through cracks in the black body, veins of gold that poured down both arms into white-hot fingers and traced the ribs and the insides of the thighs. At the sternum, where the tamed form now carries its single contained orb, a raw star of light blazed outward in five uneven rays, too bright to look at directly. Ragged black plates jutted from its shoulders and back at broken angles. It appeared against a vast black sun ringed in fire, with debris drifting upward around it and everything nearby lit gold from below.

APPEARANCE (tamed form · current, from Season 3 onward): Pyrois manifests as a tall, faceless knight, human only in outline. The armour is polished silver chased with hairline gold, fitted over a matte black underlayer that shows at every joint, from the throat and waist to the insides of the elbows and knees. The helm is a smooth full visor crowned with three long backswept spikes, and the eye slot shows only darkness. From under it falls a great mane of dark violet-black hair, longer than the whole body, streaming into a ragged black mantle that breaks up into torn ribbons at its ends. A single blue-white orb ringed in gold glows in the centre of the breastplate, sealed behind a plate. This is its Ethereal Core, the naturally formed core every Ethereal carries, and it is also the armour's only source of light. The pauldrons are angular and bladed. The gauntlets end in claws, and the greaves taper to points sharp enough to stand on. The left arm is sheathed to the elbow in cold blue radiance, its fingers ending in black talons. The right holds a slender longsword whose blade is translucent violet-blue, needle-fine at the tip, a matching orb set in the crossguard. It speaks rarely and moves faster than its size would lead anyone to expect.

**On the two forms and the colour of its light:** Pyrois kept its nature through the taming, and every element of the untamed shape survives in the knight in a closed-up form. The cracked molten seams were sealed under white plate. Its crown of spines became the three-spiked helm, and the blazing sternum-star shrank into the single blue-white Ethereal Core. The heat moved inward and the colours turned cold, with a violet-blue blade, blue radiance on the left arm and gold reduced to hairline chasing on the armour, though the heat is still there. In heavier combat exchanges the sword floods with shining gold and its arcs turn gold, and for those few strokes, the untamed form shows through the knight. Default to cold blue and violet when rendering Pyrois in combat, and use the gold only for its heaviest strikes.

**Combat Style (Ether · Attack, S-Rank):** Pyrois is the playable combat manifestation of Phaethon's hidden Helios Academy power, the Etheric Other given a body, fighting on-field as searing Ether. Render it as the Proxy's buried power breaking out in searing strikes, coloured cold blue and violet by default, with gold kept for the heaviest blows. (S-Rank; the gifted Season 3 launch reward.)

43.comment: S3 Ch1 · Another One Bites the Dust (9th Victim)
43.content:
# ANOTHER ONE BITES THE DUST · THE 9TH BANGBOO VICTIM

Arriving there, they discover a duo of worried and scared Bangboo. There, we get to know that Velina is nicknamed the "Death Witch" by the Bangboo and that Bangbookind absolutely hates her guts for handing out retirement notices to them. Because Phaethon Squad is with Velina and are operating under the supervision of the ESD, the Bangboo are not telling anything to them; in fact, they are doubling down on the lies and they lie to the squad they got Ether corrupted. In order to get info out of them, Velina scares them with the promise of getting sent into Norma's lab as convenient little corrupted Bangboo test subjects as a joke; they immediately interpret this a threat to their existence and they start speaking up. They say that Norma was hanging around the Energy Dispatch Station. Then, they were on patrol nearby when a big quake hit and they got eaten by a shiny rift (a Singularity Leakage) and barely made it out of it. Their combat equipment got corrupted, but the Bangboo themselves are fine.

Phaethon and co. then bump into the Singularity Leakage on their way and want to avoid it. Pyrois touches it anyway, and they get transported into it. Desperate for solutions, the Proxy, whose mind is as sharp as ever, recognises that this is basically a Hollow: much like a Fissure is the way out of a full Hollow, another Singularity Leakage is a way out of the Leakage. With the help of Fairy, they find one and leave the Leakage. They realise it's a clever shortcut for getting from A to B faster and harnessing the power of Pyrois, it is not entirely crazy to think about it.

Eventually, the squad finds Norma and rescues her. On their way out, they find Energyboos who are also scared of the recent events. One of them, Simon, got corrupted pretty badly and needs help ASAP. This is also where they meet Director Edward, a high-ranking ESD officer and colleague of Velina and Norma.

Norma tells everyone the reason why she got there in the first place: her instruments have detected a massive Ether particle surge below everyone. She was planning to go up and report back, but then, she ran into an injured Bangboo on the way. By the time she managed to bring everyone back, the elevator had already lost power. Same goes for Edward. He also felt three small tremors before the whole island started shaking, which means the source of the Singularity Leakage is right underneath it.

After this, Sigrid reports back to Velina from Shiyu Pillar 3 that things are going smoothly on her end. Shiyu Pillars 3 and 4 got overloaded and shut down, though, and both of them need to go back online before anyone can continue moving forward. Pillar 3 is already on, but the path to Pillar 4 is blocked, meaning that the Airspace Patrol cannot reach it by themselves. That's when the Proxy harnesses the abilities of Pyrois to reach the pillar alongside Velina and Norma and reboot it. Cissia and Billy stay behind for the time being to calm the Bangboo down.

After coming back, Norma figures out that the victims of the previous Bangboo incidents were all found near the source of the Singularity Leakages, although she feels like she misses another piece of the puzzle to find out what corrupts the Bangboo so fast. That's when the big Energyboo and colleague of Simon notifies the team about Simon's incident and tell them to find him before Cissia and Billy drop off the intact Bangboo.

As they go down to the core of the hub, Norma's Ether level detector (this world's equivalent to the Geiger counter) shows that the Ether particle levels are low in this area. Strangely, they find Simon there anyway, his body dropped dead on the ground and his Logic Core already corrupted beyond repair, which means the incidents have claimed their ninth victim.

44.comment: S3 Ch1 · A Mysterious Visitor in Blonde (Carinus)
44.content:
# A MYSTERIOUS VISITOR IN BLONDE

Bringing back Simon's lifeless corpse to the dispatch station, several officers from Airspace Patrol arrive to handle procedures related to witnesses. It's already dusk by the time the Proxy and co. return to Booastrum's residential district.

Meanwhile, Billy reports back to Belle (or Wise) that a suspicious blonde-haired person has showed up at Aurelia Academy. Turns out, that person is Carinus. He is the second in command of Lady Eldreda Sunbringer at the Administrative Affairs Department (AAD) and his task as a representative is to pass along the legitimate concerns of Roscaelifer's residents to the ESD. Worried about what Billy and Cissia might do to him, the Proxy heads to the Academy together with Velina and Norma. Carinus explains his role within the AAD, which clears up the misunderstanding with Billy and Cissia. That's when the Proxy arrives, telling Billy and Cissia to check in on the Bangboo from the Energy Hub that are healing well.

Carinus also tells the Proxy and Velina that not long ago, the Bangboo representatives have formally submitted a request to the AAD to investigate the safety of Logic Cores and that the hearing is expected to happen 3 days later. Per protocol, all three Lady Sunbringers have approved the interpellation. People keep thinking that Norma's Logic Core upgrades and the Bangboo deaths are connected, but Velina tells Carinus that there is no evidence for a link. Then, the Bangboo made another inquiry shortly after the previous one, complaining about prioritising the "transfer students" and Mayor Mayflower's orders over their safety.

On the walk back from the dispatch station, Norma wonders aloud whether Simon could have been saved if they had got there a little earlier, and the Proxy apologises for being no help when it counted. Velina cuts them both off, since dwelling on it changes nothing, and tells them to take a hot shower and go to bed early. Billy's call interrupts her. Cissia is audibly baffled by the stranger's formal way of talking, and Velina guesses at once that the Energy Hub has drawn Carinus' attention. Norma assures everyone that Carinus may be trouble but would never harm Cissia and the others.

At the Academy, Carinus speaks for the Administrative Affairs Department and Sigrid for the Airspace Patrol. Carinus opens by reminding the guests that Bangboo in Roscaelifer hold equal rights with humans and Intelligent Construct citizens. Cissia decides the visitors have come to thank her team in person for the rescue and announces that she accepts snacks as thank-you gifts, and Sigrid commends the rescue before steering back to business. After Billy and Cissia leave, Carinus greets the guest the mayor personally vouched for, and the Proxy notes privately that Eldreda's second in command hardly looks older than they do.

His case goes like this. Over half of Booastrum already knows about the new victims. An interpellation of the Five Central Departments can't be granted by Lady Eldreda alone, so he and Sigrid are delivering the joint decision of all three Sunbringers. Simon is the ninth victim, and every victim was a Bangboo whose logic chip had been replaced, which he can't accept as coincidence. Bangboo make up over sixty percent of Roscaelifer's population, so their mood decides the stability of the whole region. With Scamall Hollow under the Creator's influence, he also has to think about the safety of the Airspace Patrol's Combatboo, where the same failure would be a disaster. He asks Norma, the pillar of Roscaelifer's Bangboo research, to treat the decision as a way to reassure the public and leave any sense of reprimand aside. Sigrid adds that she is personally grateful for the help but finds the Bangboo's demands reasonable. On the second complaint, Carinus explains that the conflict between the city administration and TOPS has kept Roscaelifer in hiding for a long time. The Bangboo have paid for that secrecy with their memories, and he won't let them pay with their lives as well. Velina accepts the interpellation as justified and promises every resident a proper explanation. On her way out, Sigrid slips Norma another lollipop, and Lady Dracaene appears right after (see "S3 Ch1 · Lady Dracaene's Report").

45.content:
# LADY DRACAENE'S REPORT

When Sigrid and Carinus leave, Lady Dracaene shows up to thank the team for bringing the corpse of Simon back and to clarify things about the interpellation Carinus has mentioned. Dracaene trusts Norma's abilities, but forebodes to things they can't always foresee. She tells Velina and Norma to put a report together in three days, then leaves. Unfortunately, Bangboo Core testing is rigorous: all 8 parts of the core have to be tested thrice before the data is verified twice. Fortunately for Norma, Belle (or Wise) is good at things like these and offers their help. This is when Norma has to leave again to fix Bangboo from the Energy Hub.

The three-day deadline comes from the interpellation itself, and Dracaene's own message is a warning. She thanks them for bringing Simon back so that he wasn't left alone down there. The interpellation is meant to blame nobody, she explains, and although she trusts Norma's logic chip, she reminds everyone that some things can't be foreseen. When Norma protests that the Bangboo are her creations and she must understand them best, Dracaene answers that even parents can't fully understand their children, and that she thinks of the Bangboo as younger siblings with ideas of their own, which she respects. Then comes the warning: if the ESD fails to convince the residents, every Bangboo Logic Core will most likely be rolled back to a more stable version from a few years ago. Norma's dismay tells Dracaene why she pushed the new Logic Core architecture so hard in the first place, an earlier incident the scene leaves unnamed. Dracaene replies that ideals and the Bangboo's hope of holding on to their happiness mean nothing if their lives are at risk. She apologises to Belle (or Wise) for dragging them in, since the Proxy's treatment on the island now depends on the outcome, too. Velina admits the worst case is the Proxy being sent back to New Eridu, then promises it won't come to that. After praising Velina's composure and repeating that she has never doubted the ESD, Dracaene leaves.

Norma's test schedule is brutal. A Logic Core has eight units, and each needs at least three rounds of tests before the data is verified twice, with any error margin that runs too large meaning they have to start over. The Proxy offers to start on the most critical units first. Velina tells Norma to keep her usual workflow and leave the scheduling to her, because a problem never has only one solution, a remark Norma takes to heart that same night (see "S3 Ch1 · Today's Play: Bangboo Drama!").

Once Norma is called away, Velina lays out her plan to the Proxy. Lady Sunbringer set the date herself, so it can't easily be moved. If they can't solve the problem in time, they can still appease the people who raised it. Votes at an interpellation extend beyond the Five Central Departments to Roscaelifer's secondary administrative organisations, such as the merchant association and the Energy Management Center. Velina keeps a sizeable collection of leaks caused by certain people's negligence. Within acceptable bounds, she means to use them as leverage and make a few strategic concessions, enough to get through the first round and buy Norma time. When the Proxy can't hide their surprise at what that means for the Bangboo, she admits she is unlike Norma, whose care for the Bangboo is wholehearted. The ESD is one of the island's departments, yet its core staff are appointed by the city administration, which makes it an extension of the city's authority, so as its head, she has to put the ESD's position in Roscaelifer ahead of the Bangboo's feelings. In her words, TOPS is circling like jackals, and one hit to the ESD could flip the whole game. She promises to protect the Proxy and Norma and asks for one thing in return: help Norma, because Velina can only buy time, and the answer the interpellation needs is something only Norma can deliver. She adds that she will be away from the department that night and may not pick up her phone, so anything urgent should go to Norma first. Afterwards, Fairy connects to the local network and its "Interboo" system, which keeps the Special District Archives on everyone the Proxy meets.

46.comment: S3 Ch1 · Today's Play: Bangboo Drama!
46.content:
# TODAY'S PLAY: BANGBOO DRAMA!

After a quick chat with the Proxy's sibling, along with Billy and Cissia, about today's events and about putting trust into Velina's judgement, everyone heads back to their room first. Just then, a strange noise seems to come from downstairs.

Turns out, it was just Norma; her Bangboo-like hat got stuck to her head and needed some help to get it off. After helping her, she tells her real reason she came for: she's on a secret operation she's trying to hide from Velina to find the real culprit behind the Bangboo Corruption incidents, based on the legend of the "Angel".

Norma Hollowell: "Lately, there's been a spike in Corruption cases, and more Bangboo are turning to the Angel for comfort. There's a good chance the Angel is taking advantage of that trust to harm them!"

In order to find more clues, they head out to the Spotlight Theatre, a theatre BY Bangboo, FOR Bangboo only, to track down the movement of Archy, the Bangboo who was handing out flyers about his role as the main character, the foolish King Laer in his play. There, Belle hacks into the surveillance system Watch Dogs-style to keep tracking Archy for breadcrumbs of information and gathers that Archy is indeed manipulated by that mysterious Angel. This is where they find a poster with a strange symbol drawn onto it.

The late-night talk before the noise has more to it. Fairy has looked up what an interpellation is, a council proceeding built around accountability, and Billy worries about the Proxy's treatment and Norma's research. Cissia suddenly remembers overhearing talk of leverage and an exchange while eavesdropping on one of the Demon Lord's calls (see "Agent BG · Severian Lowell (Public Security)"), which makes Velina scarier to her than ever. Billy reminds her that Velina is doing all of it for the Proxy and Norma. Once Billy and Cissia go to bed, the sibling admits to being unwilling to leave everything to Velina and turns Simon's last word over until it points at Remielle Dan. She once attacked Lady Sunbringer and left without finishing the job, and now, she has her weapon back. Then, something thumps downstairs. In the dark first-floor hall, an orange rolls across the floor, and Belle remarks that the last time she lived under a lights-out rule was at Helios Academy. Wise throws the orange at a shadowy figure, who yelps in Norma's voice and begs the twins to rescue her stuck hat. She later grumbles that nobody warned her the dorm was booby-trapped.

Once the hat is free, Norma explains why the operation has to stay hidden from Velina. She doesn't want Velina carrying everything alone again. Velina once said that if someone in the department has to play the bad guy, it will be her. That is how she ended up delivering retirement notices to Bangboo at the end of their service and earning the "Death Witch" nickname for a decision that was never hers (see "S3 Ch1 · Another One Bites the Dust (9th Victim)"). Norma wants to protect Velina the way Velina has always protected her, and she has taken Velina's line about problems having more than one solution to heart: if they trace the corruption to its source and name the real culprit, nobody will need to prove the ESD innocent.

The Angel legend is recent. A Bangboo close to retirement, unwilling to forget its friends, wished to the Angel to keep its memories. The wish came true, and after retiring, it even sent word back to Roscaelifer that it was doing well and missed everyone. With corruption cases spiking, more Bangboo turn to the Angel for comfort, which is exactly what makes Norma suspicious, although few Bangboo seem to have met it. The Proxy remembers **Archy**, the Bangboo seen telling the Tin Master about his troupe's plans for the Completion Anniversary: a casting call and rehearsals for an epic play about the Angel, "Angel's Aria", meant as a tribute to the "Chief Angel". The sibling stays at Amber Hall with Fairy as backup, since three people would draw too much attention. The Proxy and Norma slip out the back door.

At Spotlight Theater, the security Bangboo turns them away because only Bangboo may enter, and the chatter in the queue explains why: Bangboo would be mortified if humans caught them imitating humans on stage. Norma unlocks camera access for the Proxy, and the surveillance turns up three leads. Archy usually works in Scamall Hollow, a dangerous job, and he has been low for days. He is already in costume for the lead in tonight's King Laer (a Bangboo adaptation of a famous human play), wearing a feathered bicorne and a formal suit. The scribbles on his poster are said to be the work of **Flutie**, who was jealous of Archy's lead role. After the two had a huge fight over it, Flutie was corrupted at the Energy Hub the very next day, and Archy has kept the poster ever since out of regret. Norma goes quiet when she hears it. Finally, the cameras catch Archy alone on a remote call, frightened of dying with so much left undone, while a calm voice promises to protect him and help however it can. Archy tells the "Chief Angel" to use the **cognitive security key** he has just handed over if anything happens to him, mentioning that the other Bangboo on his team gave theirs as well. The voice promises his secret is safe.

(Narration note: King Laer stands in for Shakespeare's King Lear.)

47.comment: S3 Ch1 · Return of the Fallen Angel (Remielle)
47.content:
# RETURN OF THE FALLEN ANGEL · REMIELLE COMES BACK

Outside the theatre, Belle (or Wise) orders Fairy to locate that "Angel". After a while, Fairy geolocates them inside the CCD's building. Since their presence would alert the guards and the building has been under renovation for a while, they have to use the back door and use rail carts to get in. (Rail carts is the way materials are getting in and out of the CCD.) Norma requests one from Fairy and she obliges with her request.

Unfortunately, once they are inside, Norma is so sure they can't get caught, since she designed the security system herself, that all the Patrolboo in the area get alerted, and the pair have to run away from them.

After running away from the Patrolboo, they run into a **special guest**: it's none other than **Remielle Dan**, first-generation Void Hunter and Fallen Angel of Roscaelifer. She first gets accused of taking advantage of the Bangboo and killing them, but with solid evidence, she manages to clear her name from this **specific** criminal action (the Proxy introduces her to Norma by her attempt on Lady Sunbringer's life, and Remielle lets that stand without explaining herself). That evidence is that the signal is coming from a different room in the building, more specifically from the info Fairy gathered, in the Airspace Control Tower. She then tells the Proxy and Norma that she's trapped there and that her mind that got stuck in the past is unable to comprehend modern Roscaelifer tech.

This is when Remielle offers two options: they either cooperate and create a temporary truce, or they keep the beef going, in which case she escapes while the Proxy and Norma get turned in for trespassing the CCD building. The two of them reluctantly agree and they set on going to find the real culprit.

Fairy has to work through a call relayed across numerous servers under several encryption keys before the source resolves to Booastrum's CCD. Norma can't believe any of Lady Dracaene's people would hurt Bangboo, and the Proxy points out that anyone could be borrowing the CCD's equipment. The Proxy objects to sneaking into the CCD at night but gives in when Norma begs.

Inside, the alarm goes off the moment Norma finishes boasting that she designed the Bangboo security system herself and that no patrol passes the main hall at that hour. The patrol Bangboo hit far harder than expected because Norma raised their firepower "just a little" for dealing with criminals, a detail missing from her project proposal. After the fight, she apologises to the stunned Bangboo and edits their memories so that they never saw the intruders. With the elevators shut down by the alert, she leads the Proxy up a secret route: a ring of lights around a Node Stele hides a code, and once Eous lights them all with a borrowed drone, the stele turns into a staircase. Fairy reports the Angel's signal stable on the upper floors, and more patrols keep appearing although the pair haven't touched anything, until a door full of patrol Bangboo sends them sprinting into the room where Remielle is waiting.

Several smaller beats fill out the meeting. Norma panics on hearing who Remielle is, then declares she isn't afraid of her and demands to know why she poses as the Angel to hurt Bangboo. Remielle asks why being in the CCD makes anyone the culprit. Fairy, recalibrating on request, places the signal at the Airspace Control Tower, far from that room, while stressing that she is stating facts and has no intention of defending Remielle (Remielle finds her as cold as her master). Remielle's explanation for being there turns into a confession: she pressed a few buttons on Roscaelifer's unfamiliar tech and set everything blaring, so the patrols that hounded the pair were her doing. The Proxy apologises to Norma for doubting her system. Remielle then flatters Norma's expertise and compliments her custom-made hat, and Norma, insisting she isn't falling for it, offers to send her the link to the fabric. Asked what she will do once she's out, Remielle says she will probably go home and sleep, since her plan for the night is ruined anyway. Then, she lays out her two options and announces she has already decided to come along. The Proxy calls it no choice at all, and Remielle calls the Proxy a schemer who never meant to let her walk away either.

From here, Remielle fights beside them as a companion. She teases the Proxy about having made a full recovery (the Proxy and Norma both tell her to mind her own business) and admits to a poor sense of direction, which she pins on the Proxy, too. By the time they reach the bridge to the Airspace Control Tower's lower levels, Norma is calling her "Remie" and counting on her if things get messy. Remielle promises to show what a Void Hunter can do. Then, Fairy loses the Angel's signal to strong electromagnetic interference near the CCD. Moments later, the surroundings shift into the overlapping space of a Singularity Leakage. Remielle pulls Norma and the Proxy into cover as a swarm of Ethereals appears, with one imposing shape scaling the rooftops (see "S3 Ch1 · Girtablullu and Bashmu").

48.content:
# GIRTABLULLU AND BASHMU · YOUR WORST NIGHTMARES, FROM MESOPOTAMIA WITH LOVE

Going up to the tower, the Proxy and Norma enter a Singularity Leakage with Remielle and have to fight a big, menacing scorpion-like Ethereal named Girtablullu. After fighting it, they all stand confused as to why the CCD tower of all places is a place where a Leakage could appear. The three of them guess that the Ethereal **may** have been the one creating the Leakage, but they doubt themselves a little bit, since the monster's Ether presence was surprisingly weak.

Norma brings up the fact that Girtablullu appeared right after the Angel's signal disappeared, which might hint at a connection. To find more breadcrumbs, they decide to follow Girtablullu for even more clues for finding the Angel.

Along the way, they get to fight the Ethereal again. Afterwards, Norma quickly checks the Databoo that Girtablullu claimed, whose limp corpse lies on the ground with its Logic Core corrupted beyond repair: the 10th victim. Remielle warns Norma and the Proxy that they can't make judgements on that Ethereal based on their normal understanding and tells them that instantaneous corruption and destruction isn't unheard of, so makes an educated guess that Girtablullu is able to do all of that. Girtablullu slipped back into a nearby fissure and Remielle tells the rest of the team that they still have time to pursue them.

This is when Belle (or Wise) finds cargo there and realises that the cargo is covered in Ether, from top to bottom. Receiving this tip, Norma immediately starts measuring the Ether concentration with her Geiger counter-like device. She then realises that using these freshly coated pieces of cargo, they can determine the origin point of the Singularity Leakage and the cause of why the Bangboo victims got corrupted so fast.

Analysing the sample, the team determines that this is where the Leakage first erupted. There is also a Bangboo charging station nearby, so the Databoo killed earlier must've been on duty before its death. Ironically, this place has nothing unusual going for it.

Then, Belle (or Wise) finds an inventory list of the area on the ground, with garbled text, contradictions and a strange doodle drawn onto it, hinting at an unstable state of mind at the time.

Just before the solution of the mystery clicks into place, Velina calls Norma through her communicator that for their safety and keeping their criminal records clean, they must return to their places before the Airspace Patrol catches them. The Proxy starts haggling Velina about everything they've found out so far and tries to convince her to stay a bit longer, telling her that Girtablullu might be the culprit behind the corruption cases. (Besides, the reputation of the ESD depends on it.) They are about to enter Scamall Hollow to pursue the Ethereal, so they cannot go back now. Velina agrees with a sigh and reaches out to Billy and Cissia to be their backup and warns Norma and the Proxy to be cautious. Finally, she promises that she takes care of the trespassing charge and hangs up.

49.content:
# TOBY · SAVING A BANGBOO FROM THE BRINK OF DEATH

Going further into the Hollow, they find Archy and a group of other Bangboo gathered up and Archy telling his fellow Bangboo colleagues they are incompetent at their job. They are also discussing that Toby (another Bangboo colleague) has gone mad and started scribbling all over Archy. These incompetent coworkers also let Toby wander off without their supervision, which is very dangerous. Also, the Proxy gets to notice that the drawing on the poster and on the inventory list from earlier and the drawing on Archy's colleague are the same. The first two were drawn by Bangboo victims, including that Databoo from earlier; this suggests that the drawing is always drawn by the victims of the Ethereal. Finally, the spot where the Singularity Leakage erupted at the CCD is both where they've found the paper and the place where the Databoo was stationed. The final realisation comes after this: the Bangboo themselves triggered the Leakages because beforehand, their Logic Cores got tampered. Also, the monster got lured in by the Leakage. Based on these clues, the Proxy and Norma go deeper into the Hollow with Remielle to find Toby and catch the real culprit behind the incidents.

This is the moment when the three of them go into the Hollow and fight Girtablullu for one last time. The fight is tough and exhausting and they have to do it fast in order to save Toby from certain death, but eventually, they manage to kill the Ethereal. After its death, they are taking Toby with them when Bashmu appears, a massive, even bigger Ethereal that looks like a giant centipede. They have to flee the area by harnessing Pyrois' powers to create a Singularity Leakage, which gets them out and pushes the Ethereal back to where it came from.

Now that they are in a safe place, Norma can start doing an emergency repair on Toby. Turns out, to successfully repair him, she needs the cognitive security key to enter Service Mode, where she can separate the Logic Core and fix it. She has no access to the cognitive security key, but Velina comes in with the APD rescue team and gives the code to her colleague, which saves Toby. The Proxies are also joining in, aiding Norma at increasing her success rate. Eventually, Toby gets fixed up enough to carry him into a repair centre in a stable condition. Before the APD team arrives, Remielle flees the area, becoming free as a bird again. The delivery of the code reveals that in turn, Velina was the Angel all along.

50.comment: S3 Ch1 · Mission Complete? (End of Chapter 1)
50.content:
# MISSION COMPLETE (?) · END OF CHAPTER 1

The interpellation finally begins in the company of Lady Dracaene and Norma is able to gather solid evidence about her innocence (artificially implanted, highly volatile form of Ether, then the Bangboo erupted Ether like magma from a volcano, killing the host Bangboo almost instantly from severe corruption; if the eruption happens outside a Hollow, then it attracts Ethereals to the area and causes havoc). The reputation of the ESD and her abilities gets saved and things return to a state of calm again, although the identity of the murderer is still not clear.

By the orders of Lady Dracaene, the team decides not to share the information to the public that there is a murderer involved in the Logic Core incidents. The publicly released version of the story involves high-risk Ethereals within Scamall Hollow as the culprit (Girtablullu and Bashmu). She also orders Norma to develop a so-called "vaccine plug-in" for the Bangboo Logic Cores to monitor anomalies and monitor the enemy's movements and designates Sigrid to hunt down Girtablullu and Bashmu.

The Proxy then returns to Aurelia Academy with Norma and Velina to have a more personal chat with them. Velina tells the Proxy and Norma to keep everything they've discussed and witnessed strictly confidential. To that, Norma answers in a way that also confirms she is an adult woman in a very clear-cut way.

Norma Hollowell: "No need to worry about that. We're not kids anymore."

Velina also talks about her human side, how as the Angel, she does her best to retain the cherished, non-confidential memories of certain Bangboo that leave an impression on her. She didn't tell the Bangboo about her secret identity because she feared this would devalue her kindness into a bargaining chip. Norma, meanwhile, is talking about her passion to keep making better Logic Cores so that she could help Bangboo retain their memories better.

After the events in Scamall Hollow, the Bangboo finally started trusting the ESD more. They even sent their kind regards and a bouquet of flowers to Velina, their Angel, and to Norma, their always-so-reliable nurse. This is when the reserved side of Velina comes through, trying to humble everyone about the title of the "Great Angel".

At the end of the day, the Proxy heads back to Amber Hall to see their sibling again, along with Billy and Cissia. Before sleep, they celebrate another small victory and coordinate their next moves, like trying to visit Lady Eldreda and ask her about the past of Helios Academy.

51.comment: S3 Ch1 · But Wait, There's More! (Remielle Q&A)
51.content:
# BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!!! (ANOTHER Q&A SESSION WITH REMIELLE)

Remielle sneaks into the room of the Proxy again, letting them play another fun session of their Q&A game. The rules are the same: two turns per each person asking, unlimited time and word count to fully give out the answers the other needs.

First, Belle (or Wise) asks Remielle how she knows where he/she lives. Remielle's answer is that she has friends and connections in Roscaelifer, too.

Then, the Proxy asks if they've been in there before. She says that it's now exactly breaking news, and that she gives this one answer for free.

Then, Remielle's turn begins and she asks the Proxy what caused the Bangboo corruption. Belle/Wise answers back with deflection and changing the topic.

Finally, the Proxy asks their last question to Remielle for the day: who planted the Ether into the Bangboo? Remielle's final answer for the day is a question about what someone would even want to do with Bangboo and gives this question out for free, too.

The real, truly last question, for real from the Proxy is if she has ever come across such a unique Ethereal like Girtablullu before (scorpion-like silhouette, very faint Ether signature). Her answer is why he/she asks this. The Proxy answers back with the observation that she was not surprised when it and Bashmu showed up. One last time, the Proxy asks a question based on this observation: are they **just** Ethereals? Remielle answers back with "it depends entirely on your definition of an Ethereal" and tells the Proxy to think about their understanding. She then asks if the Proxy has ever heard of the word "Enchainer".

Meanwhile at the CCD, Carinus is consulting with Lady Dracaene about the CCD's damage report. Dracaene is also worried about Lady Eldreda doing a frowny face again after letting the trespassing incident of the ESD slide. Carinus reminds Dracaene about the warmer side of Eldreda, telling her she surely would be forgiving towards the ESD's mishaps during their mission, while Dracaene raises the point that Eldreda being strict with the other Sunbringers technically constitutes as "self-discipline". Lady Dracaene then tells Carinus that she couldn't be happier about the ESD gaining the Bangboo's trust before he leaves her office. After the meeting, she walks up to the window of her office and thinks about not having seen her other selves in a very long time before she gets swallowed whole by a Singularity Leakage.

key: The Genius and the Miracle Chip
52.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Long Goodbye (A Rough Morning)
52.content:
## SEASON 3 CHAPTER 2 · THE LONG GOODBYE

# A ROUGH MORNING

In the next morning, the Phaethon siblings wake up well-slept and energised. Cissia and Billy, however, had a rough night, because Norma put alarm clocks into their rooms that got triggered many times throughout the night. Cissia didn't sleep well, and Billy wasn't able to fully charge his batteries and complete his Sleep Mode, which annoyed the ever-living hell out of the snake girl and the otherwise chill robot guy. (This led to the funny antics of Cissia mixing up Billy's motor oil with ketchup and almost pouring it on her fried egg, her breakfast.)

After this, Billy asks the Proxy about why Dracaene disappeared all of a sudden and if their secret operation got compromised. Belle (or Wise) tells him that he or she doesn't think so because only Lady Dracaene and this friend group know what happened, although this would be the perfect time to make a move for the culprit, as they have been thrown off by multiple false leads before.

The Proxy: "They seem to have vanished into thin air, or maybe they're just waiting for the perfect moment?"

Suddenly, the other Phaethon sibling brings up the arrival of other outsiders into Roscaelifer, which makes Billy wonder if the culprit is going to use the crowd and the confusion at that day's tea party to launch an ambush. Cissia doubts it because both Velina and Norma will be there, along with the three Sunbringers. The second sibling (whichever of Belle or Wise is not {{user}}'s Proxy) says that it's a fair point, although things still don't line up and they have to play by ear for now.

That same Phaethon sibling is also asking if Toby, the Bangboo they saved earlier with Velina's security key, is fine or not and if his memory data got restored. This is when Billy says that Toby might be the key to the identity and intentions of the culprit. The acting Proxy says that he or she didn't hear anything either. All he or she knows is that Norma has been drowned in tasks after the completion of the vaccine plug-in (whose arc was shown in the event titled "The Genius and the Miracle Chip") and is unable to respond to the Proxy's messages.

After this discussion, they decide to get going and get some groceries (to which Billy gets excited about discounted motor oil and Cissia about discounted pudding [which is her favourite food]). The Proxy in the focus, however, tells Billy and Cissia they're staying behind to process some data with the HDD system, which the other Phaethon sibling confirms. Cissia quickly picks up on the lie, but Proxy #2 drifts her attention away by warning her about the pudding selling out.

53.comment: S3 Ch2 · Remielle's and Velina's Swift Visit
53.content:
# REMIELLE'S AND VELINA'S SWIFT VISIT

Now that Amber Hall is all to Belle (or Wise), he or she's waiting for a girl upstairs to show up. Instead, it seems like at first glance that Mr. Roar (?), the bear Thiren Intelligent Construct who makes pancakes in front of Amber Hall showed up, but then, the proxy immediately recognises from the voice that it's Remielle stuck inside a costume of the same design as Mr. Roar, asking for help get her unstuck from it.

After the Proxy helped her out, she reveals that the real Mr. Roar is still wandering around in a Hollow (kidding, he's not in danger).

This cuts back to Remielle's question a week ago: "Have you heard of the word 'Enchainer'?" In the flashback, she then starts speaking about how Helios Academy kept the Proxy in the dark about everything that mattered and about Carole Arna, their teacher, only to then stop because she would be saying too much.

Remielle reveals that Enchainers are "emissaries of the Creator", the true rulers of the Six Great Hollows (Cretan, Lemnian, Pursenas, Hawara, Solove, and Papago Hollow). She also reminds the Proxy that they beat an Ethereal that was on the way of becoming one (with the help of Ye Shunguang, another Void Hunter) in Lemnian Hollow a short while ago, which was the Creator's Vessel (the one that had fragments of Sarah Floren and the original Lady Sunbringer in it). It only didn't become the Enchainer of Lemnian Hollow because they and Xiao'Guang have stopped it from absorbing the Qingming Sword's power, as an Enchainer larva can only become a full Enchainer when it gets hold of a Void Hunter weapon and its power (for example, Tailless or the Qingming Sword). (If it had gained full control over Lemnian Hollow, it would have gained the ability to bend the rules of Ether, Miasma and physics itself inside the Hollow, too.) The Proxy then questions Remielle about this being related to their discussion about Girtablullu, but then, she says that it IS related because Girtablullu will soon become an Enchainer if not put under control. This is where the flashback ends because Remielle ran away, thinking she said too much to the Proxy.

Back to the present.

Right now, the Proxy is standing in front of Remielle, angry and waiting for an explanation. As promised, she explains what Girtablullu and Bashmu are: Enchainer larvae with the potential to become Enchainers and rule over Hollows. She tells the Proxy that it might have been someone who figured out how to create an Enchainer larva that led to that big fight with Ye Shunguang inside Lemnian Hollow.

Remielle then tells the Proxy that the Void Hunter weapon is only the first half of the equation to larvae becoming Enchainers. The Proxy asks about the second ingredient for a larva to become a full Enchainer, but instead, Remielle reminds the Proxy that it's a whole separate question and it's her turn now, not theirs.

Remielle asks away in her turn of the Q&A about whether or not the Proxy can now reliably use their ability to get in and out of Singularity Leakages using Pyrois; Belle (or Wise) tells her that it's still not fully mastered yet (mainly because Lady Dracaene went missing). Her main reason to know is because she wants his or her help to find Girtablullu.

During all of this, the Proxy questions why Remielle showed up in Roscaelifer in the first place inside their head. After this, the Phaethon present tells her that the Airspace Patrol is searching everywhere for three targets, Girtablullu and Bashmu along with the wanted fugitive herself, Remielle, and asks whether those things are connected.

Suddenly, the conversation gets interrupted by a woman knocking on the door, and as such, Remielle has to hide. (The Proxy recognises that it's Velina's voice.) As soon as Velina comes in, Remielle is back in the Mr. Roar costume, helping Belle (or Wise) back up their "alibi" of wanting to order a cake for Cissia's birthday. After this, Remielle immediately left the scene in the costume. Velina notices that Mr. Roar is a bit unusual on that day and asks Belle (or Wise) about it. When things are cleared up, Velina requests the Proxy to accompany her to that day's tea party that she organised and invited surface dwellers to. She says that she needs the Proxy siblings there as the engineering collaborators recommended by Mayor Mayflower, because Toby's memory restoration has reached a critical stage and Norma is unable to step out of her lab. Velina needs someone to represent the engineering prowess of the ESD and Marcel Group at the party and to share their experiences of living in the floating city, Roscaelifer, with the guests, which will help them settle in faster. The Proxy agrees and they walk into Cuppa Moment for the tea party.

54.comment: S3 Ch2 · Meeting Lindverne Sunbringer for the First Time
54.content:
# MEETING LINDVERNE SUNBRINGER FOR THE FIRST TIME

Walking into the local Cuppa Moment, Belle (or Wise) gets to meet Lindverne Sunbringer, the leader of Airspace Patrol Department (APD), and Claret Flint, Director of Flint Workshop and the heir to the Flint family herself. The visitors coming from the HSO and TOPS are there, too. This is when they get to see a little bit of mischief from the Bangboo of the En-Nah Gang, Roscaelifer's vigilante squad protecting Lady Sunbringer. As they are acting in the moral grey, they were not hesitating to cause chaos and make the whole tea party inconvenient while conveniently saying "they are all acting in the interests of all Bangboo and Roscaelifer". Velina apologises for the incident while listing other examples of their doing (like the large pile of bananas in front of Aurelia Academy as a way to express their grievances against the new Logic Cores; they were meant to be banana peels, but as robots, Bangboo can't eat bananas and as the consequence of this sloppy plan, they've achieved the opposite effect and the students were quite delighted to receive free bananas instead).

This is when Lindverne joins the conversation and Velina formally introduces her to the Proxy (although she absolutely HATES being addressed as "Lady", unlike the other two Sunbringer manifestations; she also hates being treated like authority). She talks to the Proxy in a chill, laid-back style similar to Billy, as if she inherited the coolness and relatability of the original Lady Sunbringer, and compliments him or her on uncovering clues related to the Bangboo corruption incidents. (The Proxy didn't expect her to be like this at all.) She also admits that she hates how stiff and controlled tea parties are and prefers more casual hangouts. By rights, she tells the Proxy, Eldreda or Dracie (Dracaene) should have been the one attending, but Eldreda has been very busy lately, and Dracaene is helping sort out the Singularity Leakage that appeared at the CCD and made the lives of the staff more difficult (hence why she walked into it). Not long before the tea party, she talked with Velina about inviting the Proxy over. According to her, the Singularity Leakage at the CCD has only gone dormant and could reappear at any moment, so she deployed people there and is going to ask Dracaene about what happened. This is when Lindverne instructed the Proxy to go chat with Claret and get to know her better.

55.comment: S3 Ch2 · Meeting Claret Flint for the First Time
55.content:
# MEETING CLARET FLINT FOR THE FIRST TIME

When Belle (or Wise) goes up to Claret the first time, she seems to be annoyed at something. She is annoyed at the fact that the Proxy has been staring at her for some time, wanting them to say what's been on their mind. Claret then remembers that the Proxies are the people that Dracaene and the others are trying to save from succumbing to Ether corruption. That's when our Proxy introduces themself (either Belle or Wise).

Claret doesn't seem particularly enthusiastic about it, as she got sweet-talked into it by Lady Dracaene ("innocent-faced little liar") while Dracaene was eating through three days' worth of Flint Workshop's Porcelloy output being at it.

Thinking to himself/herself, the Proxy comments to him/herself that Claret is that outspoken and doesn't hold her words back. As such, per Lindverne's instructions, the Phaethon sibling present tries to cozy up to Claret by stroking her ego and complimenting her, which eases the air a little between a certified narcissist and a hacker from the surface who wants answers to what happened to their teacher at Helios Academy. He or she also promises Claret to repay her kindness soon. As expected, this works on Claret's narcissistic mind but gets pretend-annoyed when the Proxy overdelivers by bowing down, thinking it's way too formal.

This is when Claret tells Belle (or Wise) to visit her workshop sometime so she can take a look at their situation with Pyrois, their Etheric Other. She also confirms to the Proxy that she wants to settle her business with Dracaene and won't let her get away with whatever she has done with the Porcelloy.

This is when Velina and Sigrid were waving at the Proxy from a distance. That's when Velina mentions that some of the guests are arriving late thanks to having navigation difficulties in the storm belt, but thankfully, they are now arriving. Sigrid is responsible for welcoming this batch of guests and invites the Proxy to come along with her. The Proxy questions why they have to go with her; Sigrid answers that these guests are Hollow technology scholars, meaning he or she would be able to squeeze useful answers out of them regarding his or her condition. Because of this, they agree and start following Sigrid.

56.comment: S3 Ch2 · Meeting the Esteemed Scholars (and Tying Unexpected Loose Ends)
56.content:
# MEETING ESTEEMED SCHOLARS (AND TYING UNEXPECTED LOOSE ENDS)

When the Proxy arrives behind a building near the airship port of Roscaelifer, Belle/Wise and Sigrid are talking about Sixth Street, where the siblings live and manage their video store, Random Play. The siblings are nagging Sigrid about getting a membership card to rent tapes out cheaper.

This is when the scholars arrive and they are greeting them, letting Belle (or Wise) offer a few useful insights into Roscaeliferian life for those who only arrived a few days later than the Proxies.

The first guest they meet is Salvi, leader of the New Eridu expedition team and a member of the White Star Institute.

Salvi then introduces the rest of the guests: Professor Oakley from the Metis Academy and Ms. Lawton, a colleague of his at the institute. Both of them are scholars who have spent many-many years studying the properties of Hollows.

As the Proxy would settle into a cozy tea talk with the scholars about the cure for his or her illness, Salvi introduces the now grown-up Truvia Mosseint to the Proxy, introduced as the daughter of Mr. Mosseint, the CEO of High Ambitions Corp., tearing decade-old emotional wounds apart, triggering a flashback scene.

In the flashback, we get to initially see a calm moment of the young Proxies playing chess with the young Truvia, climaxing in the quote from Truvia: "Haha, looks like someone's gonna be losing for the rest of their life, huh?". This ties back to the tragedy of Serpico all over again and the permanent bittering of their previously idyllic friendship. Then, the scene switches to a destroyed Helios Academy, with the buildings fallen down, damaged and burning in flames. This was the moment when Truvia said something incredibly cruel to the young Phaethon siblings. When they took offence, she told them they had no right to feel offended after what they had done to both Serpico and the academy. Truvia then hopes to never see the siblings again in her life and runs away. The flashback ends here, cutting back to the present, to the now adult Truvia.

In this moment, Belle (or Wise) is completely lost, not knowing how to react to a long-not-seen friend-turned-enemy, especially seeing that she recognised him or her. Mr. Salvi mentioned that both the Proxy and Truvia are experts in Hollow navigation AND that he knows they used to be classmates at Helios Academy, so the two should be left to talk to each other. Unknowingly and in good faith, he forces the Proxy to solve a decade-long conflict with Truvia between four eyes at the tea party.

(This really makes Belle [or Wise] feel like he or she has choked on a dumpling whole, as they know pretty well Truvia hates their guts.)

Truvia then deflects as she's saying she's got motion sickness during the trip, but then, Sigrid is still trying to matchmake them by offering them a stroll in the nearby park (also in complete good faith, not knowing a thing about the decade-long feud between them). She and the Proxy both accept the proposition and are left alone to talk their problems out.

57.content:
# TRUVIA · A BITTERSWEET REUNION

The Proxy and Truvia arrive to the park at the sight of a tree fully made out of Porcelloy called Porcelloy Veins. Truvia seems surprised by it, as she never expected that there would be such an abundance of it that they would use it for public decoration. Belle (or Wise) then explains it to her that it's also one of the nodes of the Porcelloy veins. She answers back to the Proxy that it's also essential for the computation of Rosetta Data. Truvia then brings up that Belle (or Wise) knows a lot about the place, despite claiming they've only been in Roscaelifer for a few days and asks them about the connection between them and Rosetta Data. The Proxy says they have no idea. ("OUT-OF-NARRATION NOTE: How, though? Do they include electronics inside to harness the elemental properties of the alloy, or does it just magically cast frequencies on its own that line up with GPS signals and thus are coincidentally perfect for geo-tracking? This is a major plot hole.") Truvia seems to be not that convinced, thinking that it touches on one of Roscaelifer's top secrets that people like her working for TOPS and thus, the corporate elite of New Eridu ought not to know. The Proxy tells her that they don't know and will ask around so that they can talk about it next time.

This is when she signals she wants to keep distance, due to their past at Helios Academy and gestures them to move deeper into the sky city to see what's up ahead.

They go down to the fountain of the park where the Proxy asks how she feels in that moment and if she has recovered from the motion sickness. She says she's feeling better. She says her state of health is much better than when they used to be kids. (Otherwise, her father would have never let her come to Roscaelifer.)

The Proxy asks Truvia about her father; she says that he may be old, but he's still very much healthy and in good strength, even though he or she meant to know about their relationship and what she thinks of him. This is when the Proxy, in his or her thoughts, alludes mysteriously to some kind of spiralling that is never spelled out, making Belle (or Wise) wonder whether things have improved between them in terms of their father-daughter relationship.

Truvia immediately notices that, but then, the Proxy deflects, making Truvia suggest they should keep going.

They end up visiting the large public chess board of the park next, which brings up memories of those cherished moments when they used to play chess with each other as children. For a moment, they finally get to reconnect as the friends they used to be, bringing that long-lost warmth back into their relationship. Truvia also asks about what happened to them since the "incident" as they were growing up. Belle (or Wise) then explains the video store to her and how they are running it with their sibling, who hasn't changed at the core of their personality even though they have to carry the responsibility and maturity of adulthood now. He or she also offers their most premium membership card to her, allowing her to rent whatever she wants, as many as she wants, whenever she wants, saying it with glowing eyes like they're finally gaining a friend back they've long thought they lost forever with their actions. Truvia agrees, warming up to the aspect.

In this cozy moment, the two friends were now able to set their bitter differences aside and be the friends they always wanted to be, always kind and supporting of the other.

Then, the Proxy asks the same back, to which Truvia answers she has continued research on Hollow communication, with the help of her father. She also reveals that High Ambitions Corp. was also able to salvage a small portion of the research materials made by the scholars of Helios Academy and her dad is planning to adopt the tech for civilian use and she's helping him at every step. This means they've been trying to research the tech behind the HDD (Hollow Deep Dive System) this whole time and make it commercially viable. The Proxy then asks the question in their head if Truvia is also going in and out of Hollows as often as they (plural) do and what the condition of their ocular implants is. The Proxy also asks another question to him/herself: do they know that Helios never researched the hidden dangers behind these powers? This makes them directly confront Truvia, even at the cost of breaking that idyllic reconnection.

Truvia then answers yes. She says she has no intentions of judging the choices he or she has made anymore, but she doesn't want the study to go waste it; not after getting so close so many times and having so many memories attached to it.

The Proxy says that it's not what they meant; the Academy never fully resolved the issues and their implant has started acting up again, putting their life in danger, as he or she has the real chance of succumbing to Ether corruption.

"Enough!" Truvia says. At this point, Truvia doesn't want to make the wound of the past deeper, not wanting to talk about it anymore. She doesn't want the Proxy to drag her back to that fateful, terrible day, especially since they started reconnecting so well.

Truvia Mosseint: "We were just kids back then, we didn't know any better."

Truvia then starts talking about one of the main concepts of this universe: time being malleable and non-linear.

This is when we cut to another scene.

58.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Second Proxy Joins the Reunion
58.content:
# THE SECOND PROXY JOINS THE REUNION

This is when the other (non-playable) Proxy joins the scene.

Our primary Proxy's sibling was previously heading back to Amber Hall after the post-party shopping. He or she has heard from Sigrid that he or she is talking to an old classmate and decided to check in.

Truvia thinks this remark from the other Phaethon sibling is kinda cold, especially when their brother/sister was way more excited about the reunion. She'd like to chat longer, but she doesn't want to keep up with two chatterboxes at the same time, so she clocks out to her accommodation, while promising a **proper** catch-up next time.

On the way back from shopping, the sibling passed Cuppa Moment just as the tea party was wrapping up and heard from Sigrid that the Proxy had gone for a walk with an old classmate, never guessing it would be Truvia. Before leaving, Truvia says she is glad to have seen both of them again in Roscaelifer and hopes they can sit down and catch up properly next time. She turns down an escort back to the lodging the ESD arranged for the guests, since she has checked the map and would like some time to herself. She is gone before either of them can answer.

59.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Siblings Talk It Out
59.content:
# THE SIBLINGS TALK THE TRUVIA SITUATION OUT

The other Proxy asks what happened because things felt off when they got there. Our primary Proxy tells their brother/sister a quick rundown of everything that happened between him/her and Truvia, making them sympathise with their sibling.

Our primary Proxy apologises to their sibling about not thinking their question about the ocular implants through.

The other Proxy mentions that even if they are trying hard, they can't talk to Truvia about the power within them without addressing the obvious Serpico-shaped elephant in the room and that they need to fight the right way for it.

Still, life isn't all doom and gloom: Norma messages the second Proxy with good news. It's about Toby's recovery going incredibly well: she was able to fully restore Toby's memory data. Also, she wants the Proxies to know something even better and very important, so she wants them to see her at Aurelia Academy ASAP. As such, they are heading back to the academy.

The sibling tells the Proxy not to overthink it, since they meant well. What worries the sibling is the power inside the two of them: nobody knows how much Truvia understands about it, and if anything goes wrong with her implants, it will be a serious problem. Norma's message arrives on the sibling's phone.

60.comment: S3 Ch2 · Norma's Got Good News!
60.content:
# NORMA'S GOT GOOD NEWS!

As soon as the Proxies arrive back to Norma's lab at Aurelia Academy, she immediately starts speaking about the exciting discovery inside Toby's memory banks: a mysterious male figure in a green suit, wearing medallion in his neck. The guy has beat Toby up because he wasn't being cooperative with this shady person. The person tells Toby to get into some kind of machine, since he has been entrusted with a **very** important mission that he should never forget. If the Proxies could find the machine, they could immediately find the mysterious culprit.

Then, on the wall behind the culprit, to his right shoulder, they notice a Bangboo graffiti. It seems like some kind of symbol, belonging to someone or some group; turns out, it was the marker of the En-Nah Gang, the vigilante organisation that swore its alliance to Lady Sunbringer, in order to protect the Mother of All Bangboo.

Norma then wonders how they ended up getting involved with the culprit. Then, our primary Proxy brings up the theory that the culprit might have just happened to **be** on En-Nah Gang turf without being associated with them. The gang really cares about Bangboo rights, and a gang like that cooperating with a human who hurts Bangboo doesn't line up.

This is when the second Proxy brings up they should visit an En-Nah Gang territory to find out. Norma brings up Clink Market on Gear Street (where gang members are swapping bottle caps they've scavenged) as a good first start. As Norma is explaining those bottle caps and Gear Street to them, the second Proxy comes up with the idea to get some bottle caps ready to bribe the Bangboo around them for gathering intelligence. They message Cissia who in a few minutes, she comes into the lab with a bunch of them. She says that she was worried she would struggle to find something good to eat in Roscaelifer and go hungry, so she stuffed lots of food and drinks into her luggage. That makes her rich by Bangboo standards. The looney snake police officer girl even presents them with a funny story around all of it, as it's usual from her.

After this encounter, the Proxies and the zany snake girl get moving to Gear Street.

61.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Wolf of Gear Street
61.content:
# THE WOLF OF GEAR STREET

After a long skip of not doing so, the Proxy finally connects their consciousness to Eous again Avatar-style to get into Clink Market behind the tiny, Bangboo-sized door hiding it and find out more about the En-Nah Gang. There, near the entrance, they find Mr. Knowaboo, a Bangboo who gives out intel for the right price. When the Proxy (in Eous' body) first addresses Knowaboo, he doesn't respond, so as a backup plan, they reach for the bottle cap Cissia gave them, a Limited Edition Janus Quarter summer ice-cold Orange God cap worth a fortune by Bangboo standards. Seeing this, he immediately opens up: the door in the distance is protected by a Bangboo in a suit; that guard is a member of the En-Nah Gang. He also asks the Proxy what kind of business they have with the gang and offers his help to them. As such, the Proxy shows a photo of the place where Toby got knocked out, but even the all-knowing Knowaboo couldn't help with that; however, he says that going through the door might yield some answers.

He says the door is protected with a series of security questions. As such, Knowaboo asks the Proxy to wait a bit so that he can make notes that they can read when they get questioned.

The answers of the security questions are these:

1. The En-Nah Gang has no secret passcode. Any claims that you need to pay to obtain one are scams!
2. Members of the En-Nah Gang verify each other's identities through badges they carry with them. These badges feature special anti-counterfeiting measures, and forging one is no easy feat!
3. The En-Nah Gang's mission is to protect Lady Sunbringer. Everything they do revolves around Lady Sunbringer. In short, if you encounter an En-Nah Gang member, just shout "Long live Lady Sunbringer, En-Nah!" a couple of times!

Accepting this advice, the Proxy is able to waltz through the security systems pretty easily.

Beyond the guard and the door, a little farther in, the Retroflux Zone can be found. There is a lift there, where going down leads to the gang hideout.

While going through the Retroflux Zone (the water circulation system), they keep meeting new Bangboo, all talking about "seeing Lady Sunbringer's revelation".

The Proxy: "What is the connection between the revelation and the culprit? It's still bothering me."

At the hideout, we get to meet Griff Ashton, the boss of the En-Nah Gang. He is of a high class, as he has the marker of a posh accent: the "gah" syllable in the Bangboo language. The Proxy also notices something strange: almost all the Bangboo there are of the Databoo model.

Griff mentions that Bangboo can only officially become En-Nah Gang members with the blessing of Prophetboo, the Great Prophet. He is the oldest member of the gang and the first large Databoo to receive the revelation.

This is where the lie of Eous seeing the revelation comes to light. Since he doesn't seem to act in bad faith, the Great Prophet lets it somewhat slide and leaves Eous' fate to the Great One. Turns out, the Great One was Remielle all along. (Remielle also gets to see the special trump card of the Proxy, the mind link through the HDD, the first time.)

Remielle tells us, the Proxy, that Retroflux Zone is her home, ever since she became a criminal. According to her, she is able to live with them because Prophetboo saw her more than a century ago (yes, Remielle could be your great-grandmother!). In the Bangboo's eyes, she's still a respected Void Hunter and friend of Lady Sunbringer, their "mother"/inventor figure.

The explanation to that is simple: Remielle says that **in the eyes of the En-Nah Gang, the split Sunbringers are all impostors and the revelation the Bangboo keep talking about is a cry for help from the REAL Lady Sunbringer**. The revelation is a vision that occasionally appears to Databoo that process Rosetta Data (the master copies of Carrot Data, aka. navigation data). The Bangboo only believe in what the revelation says to them.

Remielle Dan: "The true Lady Sunbringer, imprisoned in endless darkness."

According to the En-Nah Gang, the real Lady Sunbringer is imprisoned somewhere hidden, and nobody knows where she is hiding. Nobody, not even Remielle, knows whether it's some sort of riddle or a delusion (or a combination of both), or whether they are telling the truth about Dracaene, Lindverne and Eldreda.

After this, Remielle also asks the Proxy why they are here and quickly explains the Toby situation and the mysterious man to her. Hearing this, Remielle offers her help to the Proxy again: stepping in as "Lady Remielle of the En-Nah Gang", she will spread good rep for them so that the Bangboo assist them in locating the crime scene. The Proxy agrees enthusiastically but then quickly reminds themself there is always a catch with Remielle and wants to know it. Remielle says that her condition didn't change: helping her investigate Girtablullu, the Enchainer larva, since the Ethereal and the culprit might be connected. The Proxy asks for details, but she still keeps speaking in riddles. After that, Remielle gently nudges Griff about the place the Proxy is looking for and Griff gathers the nearby Bangboo immediately.

Griff explains to Remielle that a few gang members have found the place the Proxy was looking for: it's at the absolute bottom of Retroflux and it used to be one of the candidates for a new hideout, as one of the four backup options. Recently, the electronics have started malfunctioning, though, and Ether concentration started getting worse there. Remielle asks the Proxy to go with them and they reluctantly agree. Since getting there would be difficult with Eous, Remielle requests Belle (or Wise) to go with them while being disconnected from Eous, but Griff brings up a hidden lift in the red phone booth on Beckford Street that is big enough for humans to use.

Going back to their sibling, the Proxy is talking it out what happened to them, still not being able to fully trust Remielle, as she might be hiding her true intentions. After all, she wants to harness the power of Pyrois in order to manipulate the Singularity Leakage and track down Girtablullu, as all of it is connected. The Proxies agree to then go back to Retroflux with Remielle and Pyrois and find out what's going on.

(The revelation turns out to be true in its own way: the first Sunbringer never left, and she has spent the last century shackled in Porcelloy in the Secret Chamber atop the Airspace Control Tower, as the kindling for the Rosetta Data; see "S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)".)

62.content:
# QUIT HORSIN' AROUND!

As soon as the Proxies are getting to the phone booth near Spotlight Theatre, Beckford Street, they also run into Sigrid alongside the Bangboo Griff has mentioned, since she has found the movement of the Bangboo quite suspicious as a member of the police force. Just as Belle (or Wise) was about to make up a fake excuse to save the exterior of the Bangboo, Sigrid starts talking about a character called Mr. Goboo from the theatre play "Awaiting Goboo" because she thinks the Bangboo is an Actorboo who got stuck in his role. Sigrid then apologises for the inconvenience she has caused and walks away. The Bangboo then incorrectly assesses that Sigrid might be on their side and the Proxy has to explain the truth multiple times to him before taking the lift down.

Strictly speaking, Belle (or Wise) makes this trip alone. Back at Amber Hall, the twins agree Remielle is still holding something back, since her Q&A game forbids lies without obliging her to tell the whole truth. They still don't know why she tried to assassinate Lady Sunbringer, and the one goal she admits to is using the Proxy and Pyrois to steer Singularity Leakages and track down Girtablullu. The sibling offers to fetch Billy and Cissia, but the Proxy declines, since a crowd could compromise the investigation and make the En-Nah Gang nervous. The Proxy trusts Pyrois and Remielle to be enough. The sibling and Fairy provide remote support. The booth turns out to be a short walk from Amber Hall, which explains how easily Remielle comes and goes.

At the booth, the En-Nah Gang guard is so flustered that he denies any phone booth exists while standing in front of it, then insists he is waiting for someone he can't name. Sigrid seizes on that and recites a line from "Awaiting Goboo" about waiting for Mr. Goboo. Since the play has no phone booth, let alone a theatre or an Actorboo, she reasons to herself that this must be a Spotlight Theater actor who stayed in character too long, and she apologises for interrupting his rehearsal. The guard runs with it, reciting his boss's teaching that constant practice builds the courage and conviction worthy of protecting Lady Sunbringer. Sigrid agrees that courage and conviction are how one protects Roscaelifer, and the two of them talk straight past each other. The Proxy keeps quiet, dreading how hard it would be to explain Remielle if Sigrid ever found her.

Down in the Retroflux Zone, Remielle teases the Proxy for covering for an accomplice in front of an Airspace Patrol officer. She sums Sigrid up as rigid and earnest, with an unnervingly sharp intuition that makes her hard to deal with. Griff, meeting the Proxy in person for the first time, gushes over their looks. He has already cleared the barricades around the elevator to the bottom of the Retroflux Zone and sends them off before dark (see "S3 Ch2 · The Sewage Claims Its Child Again").

(Narration note: "Awaiting Goboo" is the Bangboo stage world's version of Beckett's Waiting for Godot.)

63.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Sewage Claims Its Child Again
63.content:
# THE SEWAGE CLAIMS ITS CHILD AGAIN

After taking the lift back into the Retroflux Zone, the Proxy meets Remielle again and explains why they arrived late. Another lift takes them to the crime scene in the very deepest part of the Retroflux Zone.

Ending up there, the Proxy gets lost in their own thoughts and Remielle has to tickle their nose to make them pay attention. Belle (or Wise) seems to be annoyed about it and doesn't want to talk, so Remielle offers a feather to tickle her back; obviously, as an angel Thiren, she doesn't budge. Now that both of them are even, the Proxy starts telling Remielle that continuing to explore the area carries the risk of running into a Singularity Leakage, so she has to behave to avoid one. Then, the Proxy sees her mind drift off as well.

Despite the Proxy's warnings, she still ends up stepping into them, having to fight way more enemies. Belle’s (or Wise's) reasoning is that they'd hold back Remielle because their combat skills haven’t improved a lot. Remielle then compliments the Proxy because only them and **Joyous** were able to enter a Hollow and fight in person. She keeps stroking their ego, telling the Proxy that their combat abilities are better than their friends'. Not a whole lot of people are left, she adds, who still remember what happened to Joyous.

Arriving to the crime scene, Fairy runs a forensics scan on the mech they had to fight there. Retrieving the operation logs, the perpetrator has used the mech to implant potent Ether into Toby. The Proxy also finds trace files of a virus; they think it either be related to controlling the Bangboo from afar and make them commit crimes, or some other reason.

Digging deeper, Belle (or Wise) finds a photo inside the memory module who is likely the culprit.

This is when we find Season 3 Chapter 2's third big plot twist: **The one in the image might be Serpico, which might suggest he survived the Helios Academy incident and is likely the one who used Toby for his shady purposes.**

Seeing this, the Proxy is trying to deny this; "this cannot be him, this must be someone who looks like him", says Belle (or Wise). As such, they ask Fairy to fully recover the corrupted image to make sure everything checks out.

Just before the analysis could get completed, a rapid string of warnings start blaring from the broken mech. Remielle pushes the Proxy away from the mech before it could explode. Belle's (or Wise's) life might have got saved, but the clue to the mystery behind the Bangboo victims got destroyed with the explosion. The loss makes the Proxy very angry, and their eye implant shines bright gold as they start to see unfamiliar visions and hear unfamiliar voices.

Since the Proxy was looking into the eyes of Remielle, we get to see a flashback from an earlier period of her life; it's Remielle's Void Hunter admission ceremony, a celebration for defeating some kind of big enemy. There, she was talking to Beliora (nicknamed Beli), an old friend of hers about mundane things, like her legs being tired from standing and her back itching.

Then, a second memory flashes in, involving the original Lady Sunbringer and talking about an experiment. There happens to be friendly back-and-forth banter between the two about the goal of the experiment, but then, Remielle was not able to memorise it. Beli says to Sunbringer, though, that she shouldn't worry, since she memorised everything for Remielle and there shouldn't be any problems. Remielle then asks what she meant by "shouldn't", as she was supposed to say that everything will DEFINITELY be fine.

Sunbringer is then talking about the Karma Core within Thaumiel being sealed shut and most of their research remaining entirely theoretical and Professor Arche's experimental plan remaining only theoretically feasible. Then, Sunbringer tells the two women they can still back out of the experiment any time, already hinting at something ominous.

Remielle, however, still expresses enthusiasm because this is their one chance at conquering the Hollows once and for all.

Finally, we switch to a third flashback where Remielle and Beli are talking their problems out, especially since Beli got distracted on that day. Then, Remielle invites Beli to dance and forget their worries for a moment.

Then, Belle (or Wise) wakes up and Remielle tells them that she was able to see his/her memories. The Proxy confirms the same for Remielle. They saw quiet, friendly moments and talks with Lady Sunbringer about experiments. Then, Remielle admits that she has killed Beliora with her own hands.

When the Proxy goes back to Amber Hall, Remielle starts talking to that strange robot again from earlier. Remielle asks her of why she's haunting people like restless ghosts, only for the mysterious robot to tell Remielle she's concerned about her mental state. Remielle answers back that it's the worst time to appear and she can just pretend her not existing if she just stays away and tells the robot to scram. She doesn't go away and then, Remielle just asks her if she knew about the strange resonance between her and Phaethon, based on the part of Remielle that's already fused with the Karma Core.

Then, the mysterious robot is talking about Remielle's previous encounter with Eldreda; she is sure that Remielle has figured out what the three "Sunbringers" are. Remielle answers back that she has a good, educated guess.

After this, the robot asks Remielle about her plan, to which she plans a short summer vacation in Roscaelifer. The robot is telling her that she's wasting her time like this, but Remielle says they don't need to be in a hurry. She knows that the strange robot has foreseen a storm, and when it will arrive, better than she ever will, so she wants to enjoy its calm before its power comes. After all, she wants to take a good final look at Roscaelifer, Lady Sunbringer's magnum opus alongside the Bangboo and her final "gift" Sunbringer left for this world.

64.comment: S3 Ch2 · A Worried Brother (Or Sister)
64.content:
# A WORRIED BROTHER (OR SISTER)

When Belle (or Wise) arrives back to their bedroom in Amber Hall, their sibling welcomes them with relief. What happened in the Retroflux Zone severed the connection between the Proxy siblings, and the other was seriously considering going down there with Billy and Cissia before Remielle intervened and used his or her phone. Obviously, the makes the primary Proxy question how she got their password, making her seem even more suspicious. They also explain to their sibling what exactly happened down there. Nothing like sharing memories with the person the ocular implant has synced up with has ever happened before, they say, although Remielle mentioned that something similar happened back in the Outer Ring, when the Proxy turned into an Ethereal and she had to pull Thaumiel out of them. The Proxy's theory is that they might be in resonance with each other, some sort of frequency they share. There has to be something else besides the implants and the Void Hunter weapon.
