To keep looking for answers, the second Proxy suggests to their sibling that they should go visit Lady Dracaene the night after the next day, as she is the one overseeing their medication. The first Proxy finds the date strange and asks their sibling why; they explain that Dracaene will be hosting a welcome banquet for the guests at the CCD reception hall and the Phaethon siblings have invitations, too. This means the CCD's Singularity Leakage issue is most likely resolved and Dracaene is back from the detour. Also, there's a simultaneous banquet happening in Vyrium hosted by Lady Lindverne and the ESD for guests who haven't been able to clear security checks to Booastrum yet, as Velina and Norma were already heading to the island for preparations.

Then, the Proxy we follow asks to their sibling if Serpico was the one behind the Bangboo murders, but their sibling, too, couldn't believe it was him, especially as he is suspected to have long been dead. This is when the other Proxy leaves and this lets the Phaethon we follow keep digging into the log data from Retroflux in order to find more clues about the culprit (who looks suspiciously similar to Serpico).

A few hours later, the second Phaethon notices that their sibling's room is still lit. Going in, they find their sibling sleeping peacefully on the table, so they cover them with a blanket and take a turn in the analysis of the logs.

Fairy collects what they've been able to find so far and gathers them into neat bullet points:

1.) The culprit's victims share no common traits and their identities are of limited use for further deduction.

2.) When the perpetrator put potent Ether into these Bangboo, he also set a specific activation time and location.

After this, Second Assistant (the second Proxy) asks Fairy to dig into Airspace Patrol's recent records, starting from when Singularity Leakages began appearing more frequently. Just as Fairy is about to bust the internal systems of the APD open, the second Proxy asks Fairy to stop and stick to public records, since they don't want to get arrested. It's already too late, though: Fairy is a speedy AI and has already gathered everything it needed from the internal records.

Fairy is presenting the gathered data as a complete schematic with all Singularity Leakage times and locations marked in it. Some examples include the Energy Hub in Scamall Hollow and the Retroflux Zone, and the CCD is marked, too. Looking at the map, the leakages are all scattered around Booastrum. Then, Second Assistant reminds him/herself there's still a window when these leakages can be reactivated. As such, he or she asks Fairy to mark the locations of the reactivated Singularity Leakages, too.

Since the locations are rapidly changing, it is no wonder why it took so long for Lady Dracaene to deal with the leakage problem. Multiple leakages are happening in close proximity, both in time and location. If multiple Singularity Leakages interact with each other and start overlapping, the affected area expands in real space.

When Second Assistant asks Fairy to reorganise the data, they come to a shocking revelation; the leakages came closest to overlapping when they formed an almost perfect line from the edge of Scamall Hollow to the main urban district of Booastrum. This shows the true intent of the culprit with creating Singularity Leakages was to move something from the Hollow into Booastrum.

This is when the primary Proxy wakes up and puts the last piece of the puzzle into place: it might be Girtablullu they are trying to move up, helping it to become an Enchainer and expand Scamall Hollow.

To get more hands-on evidence, the second Phaethon is suggesting they should follow the trails and do on-site investigation with Billy and Cissia, starting with the Energy Hub and then following the Singularity Leakages one by one until they track down either the culprit or Girtablullu. Fairy and the second Proxy are staying in Amber Hall providing support, as always. Having agreed on the plan, the Proxies fall asleep again until morning comes.

65.comment: S3 Ch2 · Who Framed Belle and Wise?
65.content:
# WHO FRAMED BELLE AND WISE?

Going through the entire Singularity Leakage trail from the Energy Hub in Scamall Hollow, the Proxy and their two friends, Billy and Cissia, find themselves at its end in Lady Dracaene's office in the CCD.

66.comment: S3 Ch2 · A Proxy in a Sith's Clothing
66.content:
# A PROXY IN A SITH'S CLOTHING

When it seems to the Proxy that all hope is lost, with Carole Arna's truth out of reach and the world bound to succumb to the rule of Etheric matter, Remielle comes up to them and offers an olive branch. She also tells the Proxy that they, too, are considered a criminal now, an outlaw just like Remielle.

At this point, Belle (or Wise) is unable to talk to Remielle; it is a gut-wrenching day for our protagonist. Remielle says it's fine and understandable, but they should get somewhere warmer and dryer because she doesn't want them to catch a cold.

Remielle says that from now on, they can't go home to Amber Hall because it would be like walking into your own death sentence, so they have to flee to Remielle's place in the Retroflux Zone, which leaves the other Proxy having to testify the innocence of their sibling.

At Remielle's place, she takes care of the Proxy blamed for directly doing the attempted assassination, showing her doting and motherly side.

Remielle then immediately sees how these events have completely broken the spirit of the Proxy, making them act obedient in front of Remielle, which is strange from a usually cheerful and assertive Belle and from a Wise who is normally chill and collected.

Going further into the pep talk, Remielle admits she never liked rainy days because the wetness makes her wings heavy and soaked, not being able to dry them on her own. She would resort to towel-cleaning them because a hair dryer is too harsh for them, while air-drying takes forever and makes her wings smell bad.

She also remembers getting into Beli's bed and drying her wings in her sheets. No matter how many times Beliora got angry for this, she'd always do the cleaning in the end and dry the damp spots Remie can't reach, the loving, considerate friend she had been until her death. Aaaahhh, the good-old days~

After this, she opens up about the New Eridu records of what became of her and Beli. Remielle and Beliora were both sent into an operation called the "Day of Silence", where an accident put Remielle into a deep, 100-year-long coma, while Beliora died and became an Ethereal, an Enchainer.

She's also bringing up the Enchainers: they are the Ethereals that possess the Karma Core within them. Karma Cores can only be obtained by slaying an Enchainer, and since they cannot be formed naturally, only the Creator can make them. They hold the power to form and rewrite the laws of Hollows, and they are used to make Enchainers for the Great Hollows.

Remielle, with her team, was able to kill one of those Enchainers after a long and arduous battle, but they were not able to destroy the Karma Core itself.

Arche and Lady Sunbringer wanted to get rid of the dangerous parts of the cores while using their enormous power within to benefit humankind, Thirenkind and Constructkind alike. They've found a way to seal Karma Cores inside Porcelloy, and from that discovery, they forged the Void Hunter weapons **Tailless** and the **Qingming Sword**, as well as Remielle's own **Thaumiel**. Thus, the power of these weapons comes from the Creator Themself, which explains the side effects (Tailless driving Miyabi insane and corrupting her judgement, the Qingming Sword inducing amnesia, dementia and loss of the five senses in Ye Shunguang, Remielle inching closer and closer to turning into an Enchainer Ethereal by using the powers of Thaumiel). At the time, people were naive (including Remielle herself) that they could master that power, that they could finally conquer the Hollows once and for all, so everyone thought the two's plan is solid and they have all thought it through. They couldn't have been more wrong.

Remielle then talks about how she can stop time using Thaumiel through the example of her feathers that can pin people in place. Since she is fused partially with the Karma Core of Thaumiel, she can replicate the effect on a smaller scale without using the weapon, too. (That little bit of power isn't enough to take on the Dracaene impostor, though.)

This is when Remielle realises she was talking way too much in their little Q&A game and lets the Proxy ask again. The Proxy, in turn, tells Remielle they didn't even intend to ask this time around. So instead, Remielle helps the Proxy getting started.

With this help, the Proxy opens up about their Helios Academy days again and when they were talking to Truvia about the past in Roscaelifer. They mention that on that day, Truvia felt off, like she was talking about someone else's life as hers (which ties into her behaviour in Season 3 Chapter 4). Since then, the Proxy had the feeling of being watched.

67.comment: S3 Ch2 · A Horse Misled Into the Wrong Direction
67.content:
# A HORSE MISLED INTO THE WRONG DIRECTION

Still believing the lies of Girtablullu posing as Dracaene, Sigrid is looking for the Proxy at their Retroflux Zone hideout to arrest them for attempted murder, in the name of Airspace Patrol.

When Remielle was about to come up with a plan to hide, the Proxy gives themself up and gets arrested. At this point, Remielle sees no point in hiding and also gives herself up to the police. Sigrid says they only want to ask a few questions to the Proxy at first and that they should come with her. As for Remielle, she says that if Sigrid ever decides to make a move on her, she guarantees her death. Then, she asks whether Sigrid really wants to die like this, as a puppet controlled by that "Dracaene" thing without learning the truth. She tells Sigrid about her knowledge of the impostor Sunbringers: **Dracaene at the CCD was Girtablullu in disguise.**

Seeing the somewhat lukewarm response of Sigrid, Remielle thinks that she has already been suspecting that the "Dracaene" at the CCD was not the real one. She tells the full story to Sigrid in an attempt to clear the Proxy's name; either Girtablullu or Bashmu entered the CCD through a Singularity Leakage and, through Lady Dracaene's Karma Core, became partially fused with her.

Remielle then presents the more refined version of her "impostor Sunbringers" theory: the original Lady Sunbringer has likely divided her Karma Core into three parts and entrusted them with the three forms that spun off from her. That would also explain why Girtablullu and Bashmu appeared at roughly the same time. Then, there is also the possibility of a third Enchainer larva out there that was simply not discovered yet.

Remielle then starts reasoning why it is NOT Bashmu who took place of Dracaene: Bashmu is a very large Ethereal and it couldn't have gone unnoticed, so the Dracaene impostor was either Girtablullu or a hypothetical third Enchainer larva. It succeeded at possessing Lady Dracaene, but only partially, as if it was a full success, there wouldn't have been a reason to keep impersonating her. Dracaene's and Girtablullu's consciousness coexist in the same body, competing for control over the body and the power of the Karma Core. Judging by the current state of things, it seems that Girtablullu is winning the fight.

Sigrid denounces everything she has just heard as mere speculation and she believes in Dracaene's innocence until they provide evidence to their claims. Remielle tells the Proxy she believes in them, based on the rules of their Q&A game: "you are allowed not to tell the whole truth, but you aren't allowed to lie, either" and tells Sigrid they shouldn't go just yet because she has an idea about how to get Girtablullu out of Dracaene.

68.comment: S3 Ch2 · A Plan to Save Dracaene
68.content:
# A PLAN TO SAVE DRACAENE

Back in Remielle's room, the Proxy and Remielle sit down with Sigrid to talk about the plan to save Dracaene from getting consumed whole from the inside out by Girtablullu.

Since the enemy has already taken control of the CCD, they cannot communicate over the radio, as Girtablullu is able to listen in on their conversations. Even Remielle doesn't know how they could bring the Ethereal down in a single strike, as nobody knows how far-gone the process of Girtablullu fusing with Dracaene's Karma Core is.

Speaking so highly about Roscaelifer's order and stability while laying out the plan surprises Sigrid, as the internal records about her made her appear quite stern and cold.

This is when the Proxy puts a crucial puzzle piece into its place: they could go to the CCD banquet as guests, and just as the impostor appears there as Dracaene, lure it out of the CCD and into a Singularity Leakage (or a string of leakages). There, they could separate Girtablullu from Dracaene and deal with the Ethereal without anyone at the banquet finding it out. As long as they have stable Hollow observation data to run the calculations, they should be fine.

Then, they realise they can't go back into Amber Hall for their HDD terminal to have some data available, nor ask their sibling or Fairy for it, as they are now considered a wanted fugitive. Before Belle (or Wise) could start panicking, Sigrid mentions that Scamall Hollow has a derelict area called Roswick where computer equipment containing gear similar to those processing Rosetta Data at the CCD can be found; this is a place they can get Hollow observation data from comfortably. However, due to the size of the equipment, it was left abandoned and never got retrieved.

They also need a Databoo-type Bangboo to do the data processing locally; that's when the Bangboo of the En-Nah Gang come in, as most of them belong to the Databoo model of Bangboo. Remielle then says that it might not work out because as it was previously found out, these Bangboo consider ALL three of the Sunbringers impostors, NOT just Dracaene, but she's trying the idea out on at least Prophetboo, the oldest and wisest of them all.

This leaves the team with one final question: how are they supposed to enter Scamall Hollow without tipping off the impostor? Sigrid tells them that she's going to find a way by next day and pretend that the conversation never happened. She also threatens Remielle with arrest, shall she turn out to be a liar.

Before she leaves Remielle's room, she decides to turn back and asks Remielle something important; she asks her why she wanted to assassinate Lady Eldreda, while she wants to save Dracaene. Remielle tells Sigrid that none of the three are the Sunbringer she is looking for, as they are the gifts of the original Sunbringer, left behind for the world to cherish and build upon. She doesn't want to see the three "gifts" be destroyed by monsters from unknown places. Then finally, Sigrid hums in agreement and leaves. The Proxy and Remielle go back to Prophetboo and lay out the situation in front of him. He wrestles with it for a while, but eventually agrees with them to cooperate.

Finally, after a long day, the Proxy goes to sleep before the big mission. He/She first voices his/her worries about Remielle turning into an Ethereal from the power of Thaumiel to her. She reassures the Proxy that she's a tough nut to crack and that the inevitable transformation only happens decades down the line. She also has calming medicine on hand that soothes the corruption symptoms of the weapon, and with that, the Proxy, for real, goes to sleep.

69.comment: S3 Ch2 · Sneaking Into Roswick (Mr. Roar Rides Again)
69.content:
# SNEAKING INTO ROSWICK (MR. ROAR RIDES AGAIN)

The Proxy spends their first night as a wanted criminal on the sofa in Remielle's room, down in the En-Nah Gang's hideout in the Retroflux Zone. They are too worn out to think about getting back to Amber Hall and fairly sure their sibling and friends are worried sick. Before bed, Remielle teases her "dear fellow wanted criminal" about sleeping badly, and the Proxy turns the question back on her own health.

This time, she answers it. Every use of Thaumiel strengthens the Creator's Corruption in her, and she can feel herself sliding slowly and irreversibly toward becoming an Enchainer. She insists it won't happen anytime soon, though, and that she has no plans to snap and attack her partner mid-mission. She needs the power, so she won't hold back. For the bad flare-ups, she carries a specially made calming medicine from her "companion", and her method is to take it behind the closed door of this little room and wait the symptoms out. That is what happened a week earlier. Back-to-back fighting pushed her to the edge until the Corruption started showing on her skin, and since she would rather die than let anyone see her looking monstrous, she vanished until she had it under control again. She apologises for running. She offers the Proxy her bed if they can't sleep, then takes the offer back, because after the rain and a day of sweating, the bed probably smells.

An En-Nah Gang Guardboo standing watch by the sofa has its own story about the day. It saw Sigrid walk straight up to the phone booth that hides the elevator down to the hideout (the booth near Spotlight Theatre on Beckford Street), muttering that this was where they last crossed paths and there might be clues. She poked around for ages and seemed to miss the hidden switch completely, then stumbled on her way out, crashed through the floor of the booth and dropped straight down the elevator shaft. The Guardboo is convinced she had worked out the entrance from the start and simply skipped the switch, which proves how sharp and scary "the legendary Sigrid" is. The Proxy is fairly sure she slipped.

Sigrid is back early the next morning, as promised. She has secured a Carrot (Hollow navigation data) for the Roswick area and will escort them there herself. When Remielle asks whether she plans to march them in as newly captured fugitives, Sigrid's long pause before saying no makes it obvious she considered it. She has brought a crate of "costumes and props" that will let them walk openly into Scamall Hollow at her side. Remielle and the Proxy assume she means Airspace Patrol uniforms and praise the idea. Sigrid mumbles that yes, that is the plan, and tells them to hurry up and change.

The crate holds two **Mr. Roar mascot suits**. A short walk through Booastrum later, passers-by are pointing at the Deputy Director of the Airspace Patrol with two Mr. Roars in tow, and Remielle points out that nothing in Roscaelifer could look more suspicious. Sigrid explains that she got back too late the night before to prepare anything, and that one of her squad found a Mr. Roar suit near Beckford Street on routine patrol, so she brought it along. It is the suit Remielle abandoned two days earlier (see "S3 Ch2 · Remielle's and Velina's Swift Visit"). Sigrid concludes that Remielle must be fond of Mr. Roar, too, and then admits that the second suit is her own. She sets one rule for the disguise: in character, every sentence ends with "rawrr". The Proxy christens the pair the **Roar-Roar Twins**. When Remielle sighs that she never expected to wear the thing twice, the Proxy reminds her she looked like she was having fun the first time.

At the port outpost near Booastrum, an Airspace Patrol soldier wants to know why there are two of them. Sigrid tells him with a straight face that Mr. Roar has a twin, since a single Mr. Roar could never keep up with Roscaelifer's pancake demand. The twins back her up with their shift schedule: the Proxy works Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, and Remielle covers Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. Asked why she is bringing Mr. Roars into a Hollow, Sigrid says it is for pancakes. While the two suits panic in whispers, the soldier works it out for himself: the pancake ingredients must have been lost in the Hollow and the Mr. Roars are going in to find them, because Roscaelifer needs pancakes as much as the Airspace Patrol needs Lady Sigrid and Lady Lindverne. After another long pause, Sigrid confirms it. The episode files this under her reputation as a "Legendary Misunderstanding Magnet": she keeps a perfectly straight face and says very little, and the people around her talk themselves into whatever explanation makes sense to them. The soldier opens the route, and the three of them walk into Scamall Hollow without raising a single alarm.

Nobody else from the hideout comes along. Prophetboo stays outside the Hollow to relay the data work (see "S3 Ch2 · Meridian Hall (Memories of the Forgotten)").

70.content:
# ROSWICK (SUNBRINGER'S BACKDOOR)

**Roswick** is a town that Scamall Hollow swallowed whole, and no Airspace Patrol unit is scheduled to patrol it that day, so the moment they arrive, the Proxy pulls off the Mr. Roar headpiece before they suffocate in it. Remielle gloats that the costume is far too tight and stuffy, which means getting stuck in it the other day was never her fault.

Sigrid keeps staring at her and finally says that Remielle seems much livelier than the Remielle described in the records of the first-generation Void Hunters. Remielle guesses the records make them all sound stern and proper, and explains that they had to look the part people expected of Void Hunters. In truth, the head of the Hoshimi family got lost at the drop of a hat, and Joyous spent every other day nursing a hangover. Even Sunbringer was a bit socially awkward, and none of that made it into the official records. When the Proxy asks what the real Remielle is like, she tells them the real one is standing right in front of them, which is about the answer the Proxy expected.

Past a tunnel, the town comes into view, twisted out of shape by the Hollow. Remielle has been here before, more than a hundred years ago, in the days when there was only one Sunbringer. The enormous building in the distance is **Meridian Hall**, a research facility that Sunbringer oversaw personally, and its main purpose was to work with Joyous and the others on verifying whether the Rosetta Data computational model was viable. Remielle has no idea how the place ended up inside the Hollow, and she remembers it looking far less warped. The equipment inside should still work, since much of it was made of Porcelloy and resists Ether. To get through the distorted space, they will rely on a "backdoor" that Sunbringer left behind.

The Proxy takes them along Roswick's tracks the usual way, with Pyrois grinding the rails, and Sigrid has a hard time with her first ride. Ethereals gather as soon as they land, and Sigrid waves off Remielle's offer of help as barely a warm-up. (This fight doubles as the story's tutorial for Sigrid's spear kit: the fourth hit of her Basic Attack, *Frost-Tipped Spear*, carries her into the *Aerial Patrol Spear* state, and holding the attack there unleashes *Converging Spear*.)

A glowing object lies in front of Meridian Hall, right where Remielle left it a century ago. Sigrid notices it looks like certain devices inside the CCD, and Remielle says that is because both are Sunbringer's creations. It is one half of the key to Sunbringer's backdoor, and Remielle explains how it works on the way to the sensor slot. Roswick's other buildings were homes and facilities for the researchers, with nothing important inside them, while Meridian Hall stores the prototype used to verify Rosetta Data. Sunbringer always believed those instruments might be useful again someday, so she built an emergency restoration system for the entire hall: once activated, it rapidly returns the space inside and around the building to the "default state" recorded when the device was configured, so people can come and go. She gave every Void Hunter a copy of the two-part key in case anything went wrong. Remielle found carrying it a nuisance and hid both pieces nearby, the way people hide a spare key under a doormat or in a flowerpot. All she remembers of the second piece is that she put it somewhere rather high up. When the Proxy asks whether she simply tossed it somewhere, she warns Detective Belle (or Wise) that someone that sharp could end up as a static background asset with every RGB value set to 255.

Hunting for the second piece, they climb toward the high ground. The Proxy hacks a maintenance robot to open the way, and later charges a drone's battery to clear another path, which surprises Sigrid; the Proxy nearly mentions the things they have handled "on the island" and decides not to. Near a Dimensional Astrolabe, Remielle remembers a beautiful spot up ahead with a view over all of Meridian Hall.

Along the way, the Hollow plays back **Echoes of the Past**, voices with no one behind them. First comes Sunbringer, informing everyone of a "major situation". Then, Joyous asks whether the experiment was a success, and Remielle says he has most likely been dead for a very long time. Last comes Beliora, talking about the beginning of a miracle and a celebration, and Remielle confirms the voice is Beli. She says she misses who she used to be. When she picks up the second piece of the key, she tells it that it has waited here long enough and she will take it to fulfil its purpose. On the way back, she says goodbye to her old friends. When the echoes start up again, she grumbles that they know how to ruin the mood, and when the Proxy asks if she is okay, she says yes.

The second piece floats into the slot beside the first, and Meridian Hall is fully restored. The key and its sensor slot resemble a magic cube in constant rotation, and so does the warped hall itself. Putting a scrambled cube back together by its hidden patterns is close to what Rosetta Data does, which may be what Hollow navigation comes down to.

71.comment: S3 Ch2 · Meridian Hall (Memories of the Forgotten)
71.content:
# MERIDIAN HALL (MEMORIES OF THE FORGOTTEN)

Inside Meridian Hall, the space is still shifting, and Remielle puts it down to a delay in a device that is more than a century old. The hidden space has drawn in a nest of Ethereals, and the three of them clear three waves while Remielle informs the squatters that anyone not paying rent has to move out.

At the end of the hall stands what they came for: **the prototype used to verify Rosetta Data**. Remielle steps aside and tells the Proxy that what comes next is something only they can do. The machine looks intact, and its modules are close to modern ones. Once the Proxy boots it up, it runs suspiciously smoothly and feels a lot like their own HDD.

The data run works through **Prophetboo**, who waits outside the Hollow. The Proxy connects to him as a relay node that disguises their Rosetta Data request as ordinary traffic. To keep their exposure low, they pull only the minimum data from the CCD and process everything else locally on the prototype. There was only time to install the essential modules on Prophetboo, and most of the bandwidth is reserved for the Rosetta Data transfer, so the voice link crackles when **Griff** comes on the line to report that he is assisting Prophetboo. With the link stable and the traffic disguise in place, the Proxy starts the designated path prediction calculations while Sigrid and Remielle stand guard. Watching them work, Sigrid remarks that a Hollow specialist gives off a completely different aura, and that seeing it with her own eyes, she understands that Rosetta Data was born here.

Remielle sees something else. In her eyes, the Proxy at the terminal overlaps with Sunbringer, who once sat in the same spot, and the memory plays out in full ("The Unreached Destination"). Sunbringer reports that the link bandwidth is stable and the verification unit synchronised, and once she has checked that the Professor (Arche) can hear her, she announces, in the tone of someone reporting a disaster, that she must inform everyone of a major situation: the theoretical verification of Rosetta Data is complete, and it is a resounding success. Remielle nearly has a heart attack. The **Swordmaster**, head of the Hoshimi family in that era, explains proudly that Miss Sunbringer has been practising the "composure training" he recommended, and Remielle demands to know how many more people his family's strange tradition is going to torment. **Joyous**, the project's core technology provider, wakes up from a nap and asks whether the experiment worked. When Remielle says it would have gone even better if he had stayed asleep, he protests that his nap only showed full confidence in his colleagues, and calls the success the first step toward taking back the world. **Beliora** tells them all to be honest and show a little joy, because even if Rosetta Data is only a beginning, it is the beginning of a miracle. She insists that Professor Arche is not allowed to skip the celebration. Joyous suggests a party like the one Mayflower treated them to last time (the same name as New Eridu's present-day Mayor; the story leaves the link unexplained). Remielle is afraid he will drink until morning again, and Beliora reminds him that the Professor would throw him out just like last time. Sunbringer settles it with a ball that serves only soft drinks.

Back in the present, Remielle says that in those days, they thought taking back the world was only a matter of time, and that with their companions beside them, they could go anywhere. None of them ever reached the promised destination.

When the calculations finish, Remielle lingers. The place reminds her of some old friends, she says. Insisting that she is perfectly fine, she hurries them out so they won't miss the banquet that night. The Proxy uploads the complete path data to Prophetboo, and the three of them change back into the Mr. Roar suits and return to the hideout.

**Related records.** Remielle's own file adds that she was also present when Sunbringer prototyped the first Bangboo, and that the rabbit ears were her proposal (see "Agent BG · Remielle Dan — Void Hunter Era & Century in Stasis"). The Databoo's vision of Sunbringer trapped in endless darkness, which is why the En-Nah Gang calls all three ruling Sunbringers impostors, gets no answer here (see "S3 Ch2 · The Wolf of Gear Street"); Chapters 3 and 4 explain it.

72.comment: S3 Ch2 · Entrusted Trust (Setting the Banquet Trap)
72.content:
# ENTRUSTED TRUST (SETTING THE BANQUET TRAP)

Back at the hideout, the Proxy shuts themselves in Remielle's room and spends the rest of the day building and calibrating small devices for triggering Singularity Leakages, finishing just before the welcome banquet. At some point during the calibration, Remielle and Sigrid quietly slip out together and come back just as quietly a while later. The Proxy is curious, but there is no time to ask. (That talk is where the two of them worked out the plan behind the arrest; see "S3 Ch2 · After the Storm (The Morning After)".)

**The devices.** They are cobbled together under extreme time pressure from scrap found in the Retroflux Zone, and the design borrows from two things the Proxy has seen: whatever corrupted the fallen Bangboo, and the viral program inside the corrupted mech deep in the Retroflux Zone. Each device imitates the structure of a Bangboo Logic Core as closely as possible and carries potent Ether taken from a Singularity Leakage in the Retroflux Zone, and a timer makes that Ether pour out at a set moment and open a Singularity Leakage. The Ether inside each one is limited and the build is crude, so every leakage is tiny. The trick is to place them so their areas overlap just enough to form a passage that can send Girtablullu back into Scamall Hollow. The last device has to sit inside the banquet venue and be triggered by hand with Pyrois' newly awakened power.

**The plan.** Sigrid places the devices at the spots the Proxy marked. When the impostor appears, the Proxy activates them and opens a small leakage at the venue. Remielle uses Thaumiel to freeze the impostor along with everyone at the venue and drags it through the leakage into the Hollow before it can react. There, they subdue it and rescue Dracaene.

Sigrid agrees to get them into the venue unnoticed and then names her condition. If their conclusions turn out to be wrong and the Proxy made the whole thing up, Remielle finishes the sentence for her: the banquet becomes the place where Sigrid arrests both the fugitive who attempted to assassinate Eldreda and the fugitive who attempted to assassinate Dracaene. The Proxy promises to accept that. Sigrid asks that none of them betray the trust they have placed in each other, and tells them that the door to the balcony outside the banquet hall will be locked so they can wait out there. When the music starts, the banquet begins and the guests share the first dance, and that is their signal to get directly above the hall and prepare to act.

Before they leave, Remielle admits something is bothering her. She can't understand how Roscaelifer spiralled into such a mess with Sunbringer in charge, since the Sunbringer she knew was brilliant and far too calculating to watch something like this from the sidelines. She suspects something has happened to Roscaelifer and Sunbringer alike that is still hidden from view. Then, she sets the thought aside, tells the Proxy not to get too nervous and promises to have their back.

At the venue, Sigrid goes in to set up while the Proxy taps into the surveillance cameras above the hall to confirm the device positions. On camera, a soldier stops Sigrid to ask what is in her box. She tells him it was specially prepared for Lady Dracaene, and he decides it must be dessert for a heart-to-heart and leaves happy, which makes Remielle laugh at how used she has become to the strange things that happen around Sigrid. The welcome banquet opens with a greeting to the honoured guests who have travelled all the way from the surface of New Eridu.

While they wait, Remielle admits that a ball of all places brings back memories. Long ago, she loved to dance, and since none of the other Void Hunters cared for it, she always ended up dragging someone onto the floor with her, because spinning to the music felt freeing. The Proxy has already glimpsed this in her memories. When it is time to move, the Proxy heads for the side fire escape. Remielle, wondering why anyone would go to that much trouble, picks them up and flies.

73.comment: S3 Ch2 · One Last Dance (The Long Goodbye)
73.content:
# ONE LAST DANCE (THE LONG GOODBYE)

Directly above the banquet hall, the two of them wait for the music below to end, since that is when Girtablullu is expected to make its entrance as Dracaene. The Proxy tells Remielle to keep her head down, and she replies that on a night like this, everyone below is looking at their dance partner. The Proxy, calm a moment ago, admits the nerves: whatever they call it, what they are about to do could pass for an assassination. Remielle laughs that to the crowd below they must look like a pair of unforgivable criminals and says she has seen far grander spectacles. The music has a while to go, so she asks the Proxy to dance with her to settle those nerves. They are already partners in crime, she points out, so it is too late to worry about propriety. The Proxy has never danced before and warns her not to complain about stepped-on toes.

**The dance (cinematic).** As they dance, Remielle confesses that she has been keeping something from them and that they will be angry once they know, since their partner turns out to be a liar. Below, soldiers announce Lady Dracaene's arrival and hold everyone in place for her speech. Remielle apologises and tells the Proxy that when the dance ends, it is time to say goodbye. Belle (or Wise) almost made her forget that she no longer belongs to this era, and that she was always meant to fly into the abyss alone. The Proxy still has a place to go back to, so she will handle the rest on her own.

She freezes the hall with her feathers, the Proxy included, and goes for the false Dracaene. Girtablullu snarls that if she is that eager to die, so be it, and forces its own Enchainer transformation. Remielle tells it to bring it on as she drags it through the leakage into Scamall Hollow. The freeze fails to hold Belle (or Wise). Screaming her name and swearing they won't let her shoulder this burden alone, the Proxy breaks free and follows her through.

On the other side, out of breath, the Proxy promises to pluck her like a chicken if she ever freezes them with those feathers again. She asks why they came, and they remind her that she is the one who called them her partner in crime, and partners don't ditch each other. She starts to apologise, and the Proxy tells her to save it until this is over.

Her reasoning comes out later, in the hiding place after the escape (see "S3 Ch2 · Accomplice Act (The Culprit Takes a Bow)"): the Proxy still has somewhere to return to, while the era she knew and the people she loved are long gone, so she couldn't bring herself to drag them in. The archive caption for the scene is "Every goodbye is a little death."

74.comment: S3 Ch2 · Into the Abyss With You (Girtablullu's Cocoon)
74.content:
# INTO THE ABYSS WITH YOU (GIRTABLULLU'S COCOON)

In Scamall Hollow, a huge Ether glow dominates the area: **Girtablullu's cocoon**. Its plan ruined, the larva is pulling in every bit of Ether nearby to make up its energy deficit and force its fusion with the Karma Core, which would let it devour Dracaene completely. Remielle can't say how much longer Dracaene can hold out inside it.

New Ether growths have sprouted all around, and Remielle compares them to a blood transfusion: they gather Ether from the air and feed it into the swelling cocoon, so cutting them off stops its growth. The Proxy asks whether any "main arteries" run among those blood vessels, and Remielle, pleased, says she found two. If they sever both, the energy supply across the whole area fails, and then, the cocoon itself can be destroyed. Now that Player 2 has joined the game, she says, they can clear the stage at double speed.

The run plays out with Pyrois on the ground and Remielle in the air. The space is unstable, so the Proxy rides the tracks while Remielle waits for them at the end of the line. At intervals, the cocoon detonates, and the rule is to reach the nearest cover before every blast, which comes faster and harder the closer they get. A railcar carries the Proxy into the next area, and Pyrois drives its blade into the first artery, which makes the cocoon's glow dip. Remielle scouts a safer route through a building, where a blast tears open a wall next to a giant fan. Back on the tracks, a railcar comes flying straight at the Proxy, and Remielle catches it and uses it as a shield. When Pyrois stabs the second artery, the cocoon lets out a shockwave and dims again. The two of them close the remaining distance in the gaps between explosions. Matching Remielle's rhythm, they punch through the shell together.

The shell breaks, and Girtablullu crawls out of it announcing that its evolution is complete. It calls them puny humans and orders them to become the sacrifice for its rebirth (see "S3 Ch2 · Aerial Deathmatch (Girtablullu, Stagnant Aberrant)").

75.comment: S3 Ch2 · Aerial Deathmatch (Girtablullu, Stagnant Aberrant)
75.content:
# AERIAL DEATHMATCH (GIRTABLULLU, STAGNANT ABERRANT)

What comes out of the cocoon is **Girtablullu (Stagnant Aberrant)**, a half-finished Enchainer. It revels in the power of the Karma Core and says that if it had tasted this power sooner, it would never have wasted its time pretending to be human. Remielle remarks that she had no idea Ethereals could be so talkative and suggests those be its last words. In battle, it shields itself with a **Corruptive Barrier** that breaks fastest under Defensive Assists. (The game adds Velina to the trial squad beside Pyrois and Remielle for this fight, although the scene itself only has the Proxy and Remielle in the Hollow.)

When the barrier breaks, the thing calls on the Karma Core as a child of the Creator and devours half of its own shell to keep fighting, still trying to fuse with the core completely. Remielle wonders aloud whether this is how a beast born from the Hollow thinks, and the Proxy, sickened by the sight, says they should put it out of its misery.

Beaten down, it flees. Remielle tells the Proxy to take a breather, because it is time for her to get serious. The Proxy asks her to bring it down alive so they can pull Dracaene out of its core. What follows is an aerial deathmatch, with Remielle fighting in the open sky for the first time in over a century; she says it has been a long time, but this is her domain. She trades barrages with the larva and dodges its charged lasers. Each time it vanishes to strike at her back, she counters. She complains that it never faces her head-on and tells it she leaves no openings. When it brings down pillars to block her path, she blasts straight through them. Once its core is exposed, she calls checkmate and tells the monster she hopes it enjoys this dance of death.

76.comment: S3 Ch2 · The Fall of Girtablullu (Dracaene Saved, the Core Lost)
76.content:
# THE FALL OF GIRTABLULLU (DRACAENE SAVED, THE CORE LOST)

With Girtablullu brought down, they find Dracaene inside its core. Remielle pulls her out, alive but fading fast, and the Proxy stabilises her Ether Activity on the spot.

Then, the bigger Enchainer larva arrives. **Bashmu** devours what is left of Girtablullu and leaves as quickly as it came. Unable to tell why, the Proxy turns to check on Remielle, who says she is fine and tells them to forget about chasing "that big one". Saving Dracaene is what matters, she says, and they still have to see this little act through to the end. Lindverne's voice cuts in, confirming the suspect's location and putting all units on Combat Readiness Level One (see "S3 Ch2 · Accomplice Act (The Culprit Takes a Bow)").

**What they didn't know yet.** The next day, Remielle tells the Proxy that she misjudged the moment (see "S3 Ch2 · After the Curtain Falls (Serpico Lives, End of Chapter 2)"). She believed the Karma Core was still inside Dracaene, so she paid Bashmu little attention when it appeared. In fact, the core had stayed inside Girtablullu, and Bashmu swallowed it along with the body. That makes Bashmu the one in line to become the Enchainer now, and by Remielle's reading a far more intelligent one than Girtablullu ever was. Dracaene most likely held only a third of the original Sunbringer's Karma Core, and the other two parts are still inside Eldreda and Lindverne.

Dracaene survives, but she will probably stay unconscious for a long while, since losing a Karma Core is no small matter. Flint Workshop keeps her condition under control for the time being, and Remielle is to help stabilise her with her own ability once they reach Vyrium.

77.comment: S3 Ch2 · Accomplice Act (The Culprit Takes a Bow)
77.content:
# ACCOMPLICE ACT (THE CULPRIT TAKES A BOW)

Lindverne and Sigrid arrive with Airspace Patrol soldiers and a group of foreign guests from the banquet. Lindverne names Remielle an S-rank wanted criminal and warns her that resisting would be pointless. The Proxy is confused on every count, starting with why Lindverne is here when she was supposed to be in Vyrium. When they move to explain, Sigrid cuts them off and addresses them as an unfamiliar face whose identity she doesn't know. If they have nothing to do with this, she tells them, they should stay quiet and stop interfering with official duties. The Proxy reads it as a signal to stay out of it, without knowing why.

Lindverne orders Remielle to hand over Dracaene. Remielle plays the villain to the hilt: she was growing tired of "this little one" anyway, and since Dracaene is still breathing, whether she survives is up to them now. She adds that she expected Dracaene's disappearance to throw them into chaos and finds it dull that they caught up so quickly.

The guests react. **Daniel** marvels that the legendary former Void Hunter Remielle Dan is still alive and can't understand why she would try to kill Lady Sunbringer. **Alma** shudders to think what would have happened if Lady Lindverne had not rushed back from Vyrium in time. **Owen**, a TOPS member, notes that Lindverne went out of her way to bring the guests here to witness the arrest, and says that the truth behind another assault concerns him far more. Lindverne answers that she believes both answers lie with the same person, and asks Remielle two questions: did she abduct Dracaene at the welcome banquet and leave her gravely injured, and did she infiltrate the Computing Center and attempt to murder Truvia, High Ambitions Corp.'s lead researcher? Remielle admits to both without hesitation.

The Proxy nearly blurts out that someone else hurt Truvia, then understands. Nobody would believe that Lady Dracaene was nearly devoured and assimilated by Girtablullu without seeing it, so someone has to answer for all of it. Remielle has volunteered. At the worst possible moment, her body gives out: the Enchainer transformation surges past her limit. When Sigrid warns her not to resist, she gasps that she won't, she will simply vanish before their eyes.

**Accomplice Act (cinematic).** The Proxy steps in, done being a spectator, and asks whether her performance has room for one more. Remielle asks if they want to share the stage with someone like her, and the Proxy tells her they will finish this act together. As Owen demands to know what they think they are doing, the Proxy announces that they are rescuing their partner in crime. With a parting "until we meet again", they make their exit with her in the guise of Pyrois while Owen shouts for the soldiers to catch them. That puts a warrant out for Pyrois, which nobody had planned for.

**Partnering in crime.** In a hidden corner of Booastrum, Remielle, breathing hard, begs the Proxy not to look at her, and the Proxy promises not to. Asked why she kept the plan with Sigrid and Lindverne a secret, she says the two of them are different: the Proxy has somewhere to return to and she has nowhere, since the era she knew and the people she loved are long gone. The Proxy loses patience. She called them her partner in crime and held them together on that rainy night, and now, she tries to leave them behind; she is over a hundred years old and acting like a cranky kid. Someone does have to answer for Dracaene and Truvia, they tell her, but nobody has to carry all of it alone. Partners in crime run together and get wanted together. They ask her what kind of friend takes all the heat by herself. Remielle notes that they are getting more silver-tongued by the day. When the Proxy snaps that they are angry and she should be able to tell, she apologises properly to her dear partner in crime.

She says she will go back to her refuge and rest. The signs of the transformation seem stable for now, and she leaves the rest to Lindverne and Sigrid. She turns down an escort and reads the Proxy's mind out loud: they think they can't let her out of their sight again, or she will do something outrageous on her own. She promises she won't go anywhere this time and will come and see them once she has recovered a little. Before the Proxy can answer, there is the sound of wings beating behind them, and she is gone.

78.comment: S3 Ch2 · After the Storm (The Morning After)
78.content:
# AFTER THE STORM (THE MORNING AFTER)

Back at Amber Hall, the Proxy tells their sibling and the others everything, then passes out from exhaustion and wakes up the next morning with their wanted status lifted. Breakfast turns into an ambush of kindness. Cissia pushes bacon and the sibling offers an egg. Billy's contribution is a choice of ketchup, mayo or motor oil. When the Proxy asks why everyone is being so friendly, Cissia says they have turned to skin and bones in a single day, and Billy declares that breakfast is a sacred Amber Hall tradition. Velina and Norma stopped by the night before, just as worried as everyone else. The sibling guesses that the Proxy is still worried about Truvia, who is in intensive care.

The doorbell brings Sigrid and Lindverne. Cissia stammers out "Lady Sunbringer!", and Lindverne asks to be called plain Lindverne, since all the "Lady" business makes her feel old. Then, she admires the breakfast spread. Sigrid brings good news: Truvia has been stabilised, still unconscious but out of critical condition. Lindverne formally thanks the Proxy on behalf of Roscaelifer for mornings as peaceful as this one. The Proxy says they only did what they had to and owes everyone an apology for not thinking about what would come after, and when Sigrid begins to apologise for the secrecy, the Proxy tells her they know she was only worried about them.

Remielle is being taken to Vyrium as, in Lindverne's words, a friend who needs their protection. Her Enchainer transformation can be treated with Porcelloy there, and in return, she will use her unique ability to help stabilise Dracaene, whose condition isn't good, though Flint Workshop is keeping it under control for now. Remielle also left a message: she is already waiting at "the usual spot". As the Proxy heads straight upstairs, Cissia wonders aloud why they are going upstairs to meet Remielle. Lindverne tells her with a smile that curiosity isn't always a virtue.

**What the others say before the Proxy goes up.**

- **The sibling** has been suspiciously attentive all morning, offering extra food, including limited-edition Roscaelifer pudding, and even a massage. When the Proxy calls it out, the sibling admits that Billy and Cissia were panicking while they were stuck at Amber Hall without contact. The sibling knew the Proxy would turn things around and make it home, though, because they are both Phaethon and they have faith in family. They get choked up with relief and earn a head pat for it. They also want to talk to Truvia together once she wakes up, and there is a decent chance she pulls through.
- **Lindverne** explains the plan. Sigrid and Remielle worked most of it out in a secret talk while the Proxy was busy with the devices after Meridian Hall. Only after Remielle had dragged Girtablullu into the Hollow and Sigrid had taken command of the situation could Sigrid reach Lindverne and pass on Remielle's suggestion, and Lindverne agreed to it. After the attack on Truvia and what happened to Dracaene, there had to be an explanation. Leaving the culprit open for long would hand an opening to the guests who didn't come with good intentions, since too many people are watching Roscaelifer for a chance to profit, and the mastermind behind it all would fan the flames. Naming Remielle as the culprit was a performance for the foreign guests to steady the situation, and they never meant to do anything to her. Remielle's collapse and the warrant for Pyrois were accidents, because nobody expected the Proxy to charge in. Since Remielle helped them, Lindverne is willing to turn a blind eye to her conflict with Eldreda, though she thinks the two of them still have things to discuss.
- **Sigrid** apologises formally and braces for anger, and the Proxy tells her she had her reasons. She admits she has been second-guessing herself ever since she found the Proxy hiding in the Retroflux Zone, because with Lindverne away, she had neither the confidence to handle a crisis like this alone nor the courage to fully trust them. The Proxy's vow to save Dracaene and Remielle's determination reminded her of Lindverne and steeled her resolve. Speaking for herself as Sigrid de L'Azur and leaving her title as the Airspace Patrol Department's Deputy Administrative Director out of it, she invites them to spend a night together as friends, with Lindverne making it four: an all-night marathon of the complete *Ridu's Agent 006* film series, which is about a hundred years old. A private chat revealed that Remielle loves it as much as she does, and Lindverne is the one who recommended it to Sigrid in the first place. The Proxy can practically taste the retro nostalgia and wisely keeps that to themselves.
- **Billy and Cissia** argue over who saved whom at Amber Hall. Cissia claims she kept Billy and the sibling safe, and Billy claims his killer aura scared off a soldier who wanted to confiscate her egg pudding. They settle on fifty-fifty before Cissia admits that the soldiers only stood outside Amber Hall keeping everyone in, which the Proxy suspects was Sigrid's doing. Billy hated feeling helpless and swears he is sticking by the Manager's side next time, and Cissia immediately wants in, too.

79.comment: S3 Ch2 · After the Curtain Falls (Serpico Lives, End of Chapter 2)
79.content:
# AFTER THE CURTAIN FALLS (SERPICO LIVES)

At the usual spot upstairs, Remielle greets the Proxy with a "rawrr" and a cheerful good morning. She has recovered enough to tease them again, offering to act a little more distressed so they get the chance to take care of her, and the two of them waste a minute on the horrifying idea of Mr. Roar disguised as Remielle, perhaps with a pair of fake wings. She has come to say goodbye, though only for the time being: she will recover in Vyrium and help stabilise Dracaene while she is there.

**Dracaene and the lost core.** Dracaene will probably stay unconscious for a long while, since having a Karma Core taken from you is no small matter. Remielle admits her mistake at the banquet (see "S3 Ch2 · The Fall of Girtablullu (Dracaene Saved, the Core Lost)"): she thought the core was still inside Dracaene and paid Bashmu no mind, when it had in fact stayed in Girtablullu and went down Bashmu's throat. Bashmu is now in line to become the Enchainer, and it seems far smarter than Girtablullu. Remielle suspects the "culprit" may have planned it that way from the beginning, because Girtablullu could never have managed alone, so who lured it to Booastrum with the Singularity Leakages? The real culprit is still hiding somewhere in Roscaelifer. She isn't too worried for the moment, since Dracaene likely held only a third of the Karma Core and the other two parts are still inside Eldreda and Lindverne.

**The Void Hunter weapon theory.** The Proxy asks the obvious question: if Karma Cores are sealed inside Void Hunter weapons, why is Lady Sunbringer's split into three and kept in three bodies? Remielle answers with the truth behind the so-called attempted assassination. She came to Roscaelifer looking for Sunbringer, the one she once knew, and found Eldreda, who looked so much like her friend and wasn't her. After she reclaimed Thaumiel, the remnant inside it resonated with the Karma Core fragment in her own body, and she began to sense the Karma Cores inside the Sunbringers. As far as she could tell, Sunbringer never fused with a core to become an Enchainer. The core was divided into three parts and stored in the three Sunbringers, the way cores are sealed inside Void Hunter weapons, so perhaps, she says, that is what the Sunbringers are: living Void Hunter weapons. She calls it a working theory with plenty of gaps. Her real question is where the Sunbringer she knew has gone. She can't believe her friend would die so easily, yet one day, Sunbringer simply vanished from everyone's memories and became the three. Until she has her answer, she expects to stay in Roscaelifer for a long time.

**The lie.** When the Proxy runs downstairs to bring her breakfast, a figure Remielle knows (shown only as "???", and later described as "the mysterious dice") is suddenly standing behind her. She scolds it for creeping up on people like a ghost, complaining that it and "that emotionless girl" always turn up when someone is having a pleasant moment. She agreed to join their little covenant, she says, without ever agreeing to be stalked (her file says she joined the Covenant of Dayat; see "Agent BG · Remielle Dan (One of the First Void Hunters)"). The figure asks whether she believes the Sunbringers are Void Hunter weapons. Of course, she doesn't, she admits, and calls it a small lie, hardly her first. The Proxy will uncover the truth about the Sunbringers sooner or later whatever she tells them, and now isn't the time, for the Proxy's sake, for the three Sunbringers and for Roscaelifer. Asked whether the three know what they are, she says perhaps, though she can't be certain, and adds that the figure knows the truth and so does she. Only one question matters to either of them: where are the Sunbringer she once knew and the Sunbringer the figure has been searching for? (Chapter 3 brings the truth out: the three are Enchainers the original Sunbringer made from her own core; see "S3 Ch3 · The Storm Has Yet to Settle (Sunbringer's Secret)".)

**The Undead's Appearance.** Somewhere in Booastrum, a man with **Serpico Mosseint's** face stands over Truvia while she lies gravely wounded and unconscious. He calls her pitiful. Recalling that the monster was called Girtablullu, he admires its frightening will to survive and how much smarter it became after touching the Karma Core, since it came embarrassingly close to pulling the whole thing off. He tells her not to worry, because their "old classmate" handled everything as usual and always did enjoy doing the unexpected. She, on the other hand, has never been good at adapting on the fly, which is why she keeps losing to them, again and again. Then, he suggests she simply admit that she is worthless, only to laugh it off as a joke, since she would never accept an ending like this. Before going off to attend to something, he says he looks forward to her performance in the next act. The archive caption for the scene says that the ghosts of the past never go far.

At the end of Chapter 2, the story presents him as Serpico, the adoptive brother whose death at Helios Academy Belle and Wise have blamed themselves for ever since, alive and fully informed about everything that happened. He is already brewing a new scheme. Chapter 3 reveals who is behind the face: Youkai, piloting an artificial body built in Serpico's adult likeness (see "S3 Ch3 · Kusarikku, the Replacement Sunbringer (Serpico Is Youkai)" and "NPC BG · Serpico Mosseint (the deceased child & the adult impostor)"). His words to Truvia also foreshadow her own turn in Chapter 4 (see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)").

80.comment: S3 Ch3 · Their Secret Histories (A New Invitation)
80.content:
## SEASON 3 CHAPTER 3 · THEIR SECRET HISTORIES

*"Miracles never appear alone. They're always accompanied by soaring birds and the bright dawn."*

# A NEW INVITATION

A few days after the banquet, Amber Hall holds what Cissia calls a Random Play family meeting (number who-even-knows-anymore) over a plate of fresh pancakes, since in Roscaelifer, every important conversation seems to happen over food. The news came by phone. Cissia picked up a call from Carinus of the Administrative Affairs Department, whom she only remembered as "that blond guy" from Aurelia Academy. After nearly hanging up on him, she passed him over to the sibling.

Carinus called with an invitation on behalf of the AAD. Since Dracaene was moved to Vyrium for treatment, most of the Flint Workshop staff stationed at the CCD have gone back there with her, and the CCD can now offer Belle (or Wise) little beyond basic recuperative care. The AAD therefore invites them all to Vyrium, Flint Workshop's home island, to finish the treatment there, with the details to be arranged with Claret. Billy has wanted to see Vyrium for ages (it normally takes a special permit) and Cissia approves of anything with free food and lodging, so the two of them accepted for everyone before the sibling could get a word in. Carinus also mentioned that Lady Lindverne has already arranged the paperwork: she is flying to Vyrium that afternoon and has offered to take them along.

The Proxy agrees, with worries of their own. They stopped Girtablullu from evolving, but Bashmu still has Lady Dracaene's Karma Core. Remielle's power can only keep Dracaene stable for a while. Bashmu is missing, and so is whoever has been manipulating the Bangboo and opening the Singularity Leakages. The one piece of good news is that Truvia is out of immediate danger, and it still doesn't feel like the right time to visit her.

The plan is settled over breakfast. Belle (or Wise), whichever sibling is {{user}}'s Proxy, goes with Billy and Lindverne that afternoon. The sibling stays at Amber Hall for a day to give Fairy a round of maintenance and upgrades as a reward for her help during the Singularity Leakage investigation, and will take one of the daily airships the next afternoon. Billy packs island-grade maintenance oil, emergency repair screws, survival gear and a stack of Cunning Hares business cards, since Boss Nicole is out of contact somewhere and he intends to grow her network while she is away.

An hour later, a stranger arrives at Amber Hall's front door at the worst possible moment (see "S3 Ch3 · Phoenix Comes Through the Door (Amber Hall)"). By the time that is sorted out, Cissia has decided to stay behind, too, and the arrangement leaves the two siblings on different islands when Booastrum goes silent (see "S3 Ch3 · Booastrum Falls and a Meteor in the Sea (End of Chapter 3)").

81.comment: S3 Ch3 · Phoenix Comes Through the Door (Amber Hall)
81.content:
# PHOENIX COMES THROUGH THE DOOR

A dishevelled blonde girl is making her way across Booastrum toward Amber Hall with a delivery box over her head, following the navigation voice assistant on a cracked phone. A short montage shows the route she took. After stumbling into a Bangboo, she fell into a ticket booth, then grabbed onto a passing flying bus only to fall into the water, and she finally landed in a pile of delivery boxes, which is where the one on her head came from. When the assistant announces that she has arrived, she holds the phone's photo of Amber Hall up against the building to make sure. With the box off her head, she sidesteps a toy bus somebody left on the path and congratulates herself on not going down at the finish line.

At that exact moment, Cissia, who thinks Lady Sunbringer has arrived, flings the door open at full speed shouting for her, and the door knocks the visitor off her feet and out cold. Billy declares her dead, and Cissia decides she is a killer.

Upstairs, both Proxies look her over with Billy and Cissia. She has no serious external injuries, and her breathing and heart rate are normal. Cissia panics about medical bills she couldn't pay even with two extra zeroes on her salary and considers turning herself in, because the Demon Lord says confessing earns a lighter sentence. Then, she finds an island access pass on the girl. Fairy runs the name through Roscaelifer's customs platform and confirms it: the holder is **Phoenix Reffaella**, registered as a medical assistant at High Ambitions Corp.

That sets off a fresh wave of panic, since High Ambitions is Truvia's family company, and Cissia is sure the heiress's medical team will arrive any minute and blame them for whatever happened to her. Billy proposes the official story that the door was an accident and partly the girl's fault for standing there. The Proxy notices something that doesn't add up: if she is a High Ambitions medical assistant assigned to Truvia, why was she standing outside Amber Hall?

Lindverne arrives in casual clothes. She is keeping a low profile, since these days, the sight of the Airspace Patrol's Administrative Director anywhere makes people assume another emergency, and this trip to Vyrium is technically personal leave. Her horns give her away regardless, and the Proxy jokes that for a moment, they thought a fourth Sunbringer had shown up. She teases Billy and Cissia for coming down from upstairs as if they were hiding something and mentions a report from Sigrid about a disappearance, and the two of them take that as their cue to confess in a rush, complete with Cissia's old sob story from her first day at the video store about a lazy good-for-nothing from the Outer Ring who was betrayed by a door.

The disappearance has nothing to do with them. During a routine inventory check, **about thirty Airspace Patrol uniforms** went missing from a warehouse, and Lindverne has sent Cadyn and others to investigate. As for the girl upstairs, High Ambitions hasn't reported anyone missing. Even with Remielle taking the blame for the attacks, High Ambitions lodged a forceful protest, and after several rounds of negotiation, Roscaelifer agreed to let them send additional medical personnel to the island. Phoenix is probably one of them, and her ID is genuine.

Cissia decides to skip Vyrium and stay with the unconscious girl until she wakes up, mostly to talk her out of reporting them, and the sibling stays to help. Before the airship leaves, Billy offers to carry Lindverne's heavy case, and she tells them what is in it, since it concerns the Proxy, too: a small amount of **Porcelloy recovered from Girtablullu's remains** on the day the Proxy and Remielle rescued Dracie. Porcelloy has no business inside an Ethereal, and she wants Claret to analyse it and lead them to whoever is behind Girtablullu and Bashmu, the one who hurt Dracie. For a second, the cheerful Sunbringer looks frightening, and then, she shakes it off and herds everyone to the airship before it gets dark.

What the Proxies don't know yet is that the High Ambitions badge is a cover. Phoenix belongs to Krampus, the same Phoenix that Zhao sent to Roscaelifer alongside Promeia at the end of Season 2 (see "S2 Epilogue B · Krampus Travels to Roscaelifer"), and she is far more dangerous than a girl who loses fights with doors would suggest.

(IMPORTANT NOTE: According to an experimental report in her Agent Record, **Phoenix is unable to die**. As her vitals decline, her body draws on concentrated Ether reserves and pushes her into a state the report calls "transcendence". See "Agent BG · Phoenix Reffaella (Krampus)".)

82.comment: S3 Ch3 · The Homeland of Porcelloy (Vyrium and the Flint Blood)
82.content:
# THE HOMELAND OF PORCELLOY · VYRIUM AND THE FLINT BLOOD

Vyrium is the one division of Roscaelifer that doesn't float. Porcelloy production needs Porcelume as its raw material, which would make logistics a nightmare in the sky, and the workshop needs a stable, efficient cooling system, which the ocean behind it provides. Remielle meets the airship at the port in a new outfit and under a new name, "Ramiel". Most of Vyrium's people are Flint Workshop craftsmen who know little about Remielle Dan's wanted status, Lindverne has arranged a temporary identity for "Ramiel" that should hold until their cooperation ends, and Remielle offers to pass herself off as the famous Void Hunter's descendant if anyone asks. Claret's treatment is working wonders: as long as she leaves Thaumiel alone, Remielle barely feels anything wrong, although Lindverne reminds her that while she is keeping Dracie stable, the Karma Core's pull on her could worsen at any moment.

Claret and Roxy are at Blazelight Hall dealing with a "situation", so Remielle appoints herself tour guide. Along the way, the Proxy learns who Roxy is. Officially Claret's chief assistant, she is a Flint by upbringing and never by blood, and she has been inseparable from Claret ever since they were childhood companions (Remielle's own description is "a sweet little matcha cake"). The Flint Workshop factory is enormous, and its heart, the Porcelloy production line, lies in a vast complex underground. Visitors need an access pass signed by Claret herself, and Claret confiscated Lindverne's months ago after she swung a prototype Porcelloy weapon around inside and wrecked some equipment. Billy asks whether the Workshop is hiring, swearing he has never once thought of flipping Porcelloy for extra Dennies. Lindverne tells him outsiders can't learn the techniques at all and leaves the explanation to Claret.

**Blazelight Hall** is the Flint family's guest villa, where Claret rests and receives visitors. It is secluded and quiet, so Claret and Roxy have moved in to treat Dracaene and Remielle there in secret, since both conditions have to stay hidden. Dracaene still hasn't woken up, and Lindverne asks Billy to save his questions for indoors, because even Vyrium has too many eyes and ears.

In the reception room, they find Claret on the floor with her thumb in Roxy's mouth, explaining in a panic that Roxy suddenly got dizzy and she was only helping. Roxy proposes three ways to handle a "catastrophic social incident". One is a diversion (such as announcing that the two of them are plotting to make Claret the AAD's Administrative Director in Eldreda's place), and another is a fifty-page report that convinces the witnesses it was a hallucination. The last, a "permanent solution", turns out to be begging them to keep quiet. Lindverne offers to stay neutral if Claret forgives half her debt, and Claret says she would rather livestream the whole thing to Booastrum.

The explanation is the chapter's first secret. **Roxy's heart was replaced long ago with one made of Porcelloy**, and since she isn't a Flint, Claret has to give her regular doses of Flint blood to keep the Porcelloy active. Porcelloy itself depends on the **Flint bloodline**. It is high-purity Porcelume alloyed with various rare metals depending on its use, and most metals won't bond with Porcelume well enough to make a stable alloy. Only Flint blood can catalyse a stable bond, which is what makes "Flint Porcelloy", and it is why the craft is inherited and can't be taught. Being the only source of something everyone wants made the family a target, so Claret's ancestors settled in Roscaelifer under the protection of the Sunbringer of that era, who also played a part in the earliest breakthroughs in Porcelloy forging. The latest breakthrough came a few years ago, and Porcelloy now needs only about a tenth of the blood it used to, so making it barely strains the family at all. Claret reminds the Proxy how much Porcelloy they owe for, and Roxy warns that Claret is about to tell them there's no rush to pay her back, like last time.

Claret then opens Lindverne's case and is puzzled by how much Porcelloy is in it, since Porcelloy suppresses Ether activity and Ethereals should want nothing to do with it. She rushes off to her lab. Roxy leads the others through a hidden door into the treatment room, a private study handed down through generations of the family. The equipment Dracaene once commissioned for the Proxy's treatment is now stabilising Dracaene herself, and so is an unfinished project Eldreda commissioned without explaining its purpose, for which the Workshop keeps delivering samples to her; Lindverne has heard nothing about the AAD needing that much Porcelloy. Dracaene's Ether levels could cross the critical threshold at any moment, and only Remielle's help keeps them in a safe range.

The Proxy suggests that since Dracaene is an Intelligent Construct, they could replace the parts worst damaged by the Corruption or even build her a new body, using Lindverne and Eldreda as references. Lindverne says it wouldn't work. The three Sunbringers were created as vessels to carry the Karma Core, which is also their source of power, so the only way to fully restore Dracie is to track down Bashmu and take hers back. When the Proxy asks whether a core that corruptive wouldn't put Dracaene in even more danger, Lindverne stumbles, and Remielle covers for her by saying Sunbringers can't be judged by ordinary standards. (Lindverne also asks Billy whether his design is modelled on Starlight Knight, and the Proxy decides they must have misheard.)

Claret's analysis changes the whole case. Pieced back together, the remains are **mechanical devices that served as central control units for restraining Ethereal behaviour**. They worked as a linked set driven into the creature's spine like wedges, and their residue and fractures show they were inside Girtablullu long before it touched Dracaene, possibly since its birth. Flint Workshop experimented with that technology decades ago and abandoned it. Claret's conclusion is that Girtablullu may not be a natural Ethereal at all, and that someone made it as a tool. The Proxy puts the sequence together: Bangboo were used to open a Singularity Leakage as a path for Girtablullu into Booastrum, so that it could ambush Dracaene and steal her core, and Bashmu fits somewhere in the same plan.

Worse, Claret swears on her family's honour that this Porcelloy comes from a batch reported stolen (Lindverne remembers Velina travelling all the way to the Waifei Peninsula to retrieve it). The batch disappeared at the **Shrouded Reef**, a small island near Vyrium where the Workshop kept a transfer station for product awaiting shipment to New Eridu under Roscaelifer's research partnership with the city, plus a small research base. The reef lies at the edge of the **Minerva storm belt**, whose reach has shifted more often since the fall of the old capital. About a year ago, a devastating storm hit. Everyone was evacuated in time, but afterwards, nearly half the stored Porcelloy was gone. A large salvage operation recovered only a little, and everyone assumed the sea took the rest. The Proxy remembers Dracaene's question from Chapter 1 about whether the culprit was an outsider or an insider, and the group reaches the same answer: an outsider got in with help from someone inside Roscaelifer with high-level clearance. Claret compares it to discovering the cockroach was living in the house all along.

They agree to tell Eldreda and hunt the mole with the AAD's help, but in case the mole is listening to their communications, **Roxy will deliver the news to Eldreda in person**, along with the Porcelloy samples she was already due to bring to Booastrum that day (see "S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)"). Claret will look into the old transfer station, promising to send a professional investigation team of her most trusted allies, and Roxy supplies the "team" with reading material that includes a *Practical Infiltration Guide*. Lindverne will go through the old accident reports, and the Proxy and Billy are sent to rest at the Ultramarine Inn nearby.

**Remielle's advice.** Since merging with the Karma Core, Remielle's senses have sharpened, and she heard everything. Alone with Lindverne, she warns her that the Proxy's question about Intelligent Constructs will come back, and that the Proxy may yet learn that Flint Workshop never examined Dracaene at all and only provided technical support on Lindverne's orders. Lindverne is nothing like the Sunbringer Remielle knew, who was much better at lying. Remielle also tells her something important: the Proxy can enter a strange resonance with Thaumiel, or with the Karma Core inside it. It has happened twice between them, and both times, they glimpsed each other's memories. On a whim, she wants to see whether this last ember of Helios can burn through the shackles of fate and finish what her generation could not. Lindverne admits she doesn't remember what the first Sunbringer went through with them. Remielle suggests that Lindverne tell the Proxy the Sunbringers' secret, and calls it fate that a lie born from Helios should end when it meets Helios's last legacy. Lindverne decides that she, Dracie and Eldreda have to face it together. Dracie would support her, but she has never understood Eldreda, whose eyes always seem fixed on something farther away. She resolves to have an honest talk with her as Lindverne, leaving the title out of it.

**The killer appears.** Outside the inn, the Proxy spots a young man in exactly the clothes the culprit wore in the footage of the Bangboo attacks, and he has **Serpico's face**, grown up the way Serpico would have looked today. The Proxy tells Billy about the childhood friend from Helios Academy who died years ago and would never have done anything so cruel. The man slips away across a bridge and down to the docks and leaves by motorboat. With no time to call anyone, the Proxy and Billy rent a fishing and sightseeing boat and follow him (see "S3 Ch3 · Shrouded Reef Mystery (Into the Transfer Station)").

83.comment: S3 Ch3 · Shrouded Reef Mystery (Into the Transfer Station)
83.content:
# SHROUDED REEF MYSTERY · INTO THE TRANSFER STATION

After nearly an hour on the water, the Proxy and Billy come ashore where the man's boat landed. They find fresh footprints and a book lying in the sand, Roxy's *Practical Infiltration Guide*, whose first page says an infiltration needs a flawless disguise and reliable equipment, along with the ability to adapt on the fly. Its owner is just ahead. **Claret**, in her idea of a flawless disguise and carrying her "flawless tool", is about to show an iron gate the lock-picking skills of the Flint family head when she discovers that the old mechanical lock has been swapped for an electronic one and that she has lost the guide.

She assumes Roxy sent them after her and only then learns that they followed the culprit here, which is how the Proxy finds out that this island is the **Shrouded Reef**. The almost brand-new lock means someone has been using the abandoned station, and the Proxy points out that the culprit turning up here right after they linked the stolen Porcelloy to it is far too convenient to be a coincidence. Claret agrees to a full search on one condition: the island is still Flint property, so they follow her lead. Billy then calls on the professional investigation team hiding in the shadows to show themselves, and Claret admits through gritted teeth that there is no team. Unable to pull anyone off the production line, she came alone, and after losing Roxy's materials, she is absolutely not about to cry. Following Roxy's guide, they get the lock open.

Inside, two heavily armed guards are complaining that they should have pulled out last week and that nobody will tell them whether some "secret operation" succeeded. They mention that "the young master" has just gone in, and one of them says the young master makes his skin crawl. Neither Billy nor Pyrois is built for stealth, so Claret takes point and handles the guards herself. The ID on the first one carries the **TOPS** logo: a biometric access card issued to TOPS mercenaries secretly stationed at the transfer station, whose permissions vanish the moment the holder's vital signs do. Claret knows TOPS has never been a unified front and suspects one of its factions of acting in the shadows, since ever since Eldreda announced wider cooperation between the Five Central Departments and the factions of New Eridu, plenty of eyes have been fixed on the profits Roscaelifer could bring.

Guard chatter fills in more. A "bigshot" is back and unhappy, "those punks" in the cells nearly escaped again, duty at the research institute is worse because of what the guards there have to stare at all day, and kidnapped Bangboo are being worked as forced labour. (If the Proxy stops to help, a timid Bangboo explains that they were snatched and made to fix pipes and clean machines, and the group frees them through a side door and sends them off through the vents.)

In the surveillance room, the console password is still the one Flint Workshop set, which tells Claret all she needs to know about the occupiers. The feeds show how much money TOPS has poured into the place: the old staff dormitory and archives now have heavy airtight doors, and the clearing below the surveillance room is packed with enough mechs to equip a small Airspace Patrol base (Claret is mostly relieved that Lindverne isn't there to ask for some).
