Then, they find the young man with Serpico's face. A guard is complaining that the prisoners curse at them all day and have dug a hole through a wall, and wants them separated and punished. The "young master" refuses with a pleasant smile: honoured guests deserve kindness, especially "the quiet young lady", a precious research subject who agreed to cooperate on the condition that her friends stay unharmed, and he means to keep his word. The guard mentions that they were all dosed with muscle relaxants that afternoon, and the young master strolls off to have a friendly chat with them and vanishes from every camera.

The cells hold people Billy and the Proxy know (see "S3 Ch3 · The Cunning Hares in the Cells (Anby's Blood)"). Claret cuts the cell door open in a shower of sparks, and the alarms go off. They fight their way out through the hole the prisoners dug, with Billy carrying the unconscious Anby. On the way, they pass a thick-walled room that Anby says once held a huge Ethereal; after its protective glass cracked, the captors moved it underground beneath the nearby research institute, where they have been taking her for experiments. The room is littered with **Porcelloy remains**, control devices built to be installed in the spines of certain special Ethereals, and Claret has every fragment collected for analysis.

At the exit, a TOPS combat mech called **Conqueror** blocks the way, and when it is damaged, it drops its power limiters and comes back as **Ares**. Claret realises the thing is built from Porcelloy, and a great deal of it. That is the last straw. She cuts her own finger and runs her blood over her weapon until it becomes a blood axe. Stealing her Porcelloy to make a lousy mech and turn it against her is unforgivable, she declares as she destroys the mech. Then, they all get off the island as fast as they can.

84.comment: S3 Ch3 · The Cunning Hares in the Cells (Anby's Blood)
84.content:
# THE CUNNING HARES IN THE CELLS · ANBY'S BLOOD

The voice in the cells belongs to **Nicole Demara**, threatening her captors with the name of the Cunning Hares. The detention zone holds the whole field team, with **Anby Demara** and **Nekomata** (Nekomiya Mana) locked up alongside Nicole. Billy is overjoyed, and Nicole's first reaction is to call him an idiot for getting captured, too. Anby has a fever and has been unconscious for a while. She is the "research subject": the captors take her away every few days, and she cooperates so that they won't hurt Nicole and Nekomata, who would otherwise be fish food.

Nicole tells the story like a company president who blames herself. During the Hollow Champion competition, with debt collectors on their heels, a huge job fell into their laps. The client smuggled them aboard a cargo ship to sneak into "Minerva Quarter" and photograph a rival's R&D base, and gave them a ridiculously heavy camera to do it with. The island they landed on was crawling with Bangboo and had a huge factory clanging day and night, which Billy recognises at once as Vyrium. Claret recognises the Hares, too, as the stowaways who caused a mess at the port and buried her staff in incident reports; officially, they were sent back to New Eridu the same day. As soon as their ship left port, another ship stopped it, and the new captors were after Anby from the start. Their first question was about the camera, and when Nicole said they had dumped it in the canal on the client's orders, the captors looked relieved and attacked. The Proxy and Claret draw the obvious conclusion: the client and the captors were working together to smuggle the camera into Roscaelifer, with the stowaways as a diversion, and a plan like that only works with a mole inside Roscaelifer.

The jailbreak also settles an old mystery. Nicole spots Billy's gaudy new Starlight Knight outfit and demands to know what she supposedly approved. It turns out to be six months of salary paid in advance for his body mods, and the "approval" was a bad phone line: Nicole had told him to take the five Dennies under her pillow and that he would get approval in his dreams. She bans him from receiving a single Denny for ten years and orders the outfit sold on the Inter-Knot when they get home. Until then, she tells him, it had better be good for protecting Anby. Nekomata thanks Billy, since Nicole has finally stopped being mad at the rest of them for walking into the trap.

Back in Vyrium, Claret has them examined (see "S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)"). Nicole and Nekomata have scrapes and mild malnutrition, and the muscle relaxant wears off within hours. **Anby has no visible injuries but is clearly anaemic, because her captors drew a lot of blood from her during the experiments**, and she has a mild lung infection. She stays sedated and resting at Blazelight Hall while the others get rooms in Vyrium. Lindverne will want to question them about the Shrouded Reef, and Claret promises that the stowaway business won't come up.

The chapter never says why the captors wanted Anby's blood. The Proxy has just learned that Porcelloy is forged with Flint blood as the catalyst and that the restraint devices in these Ethereals are made of Porcelloy, and TOPS's research base kept files on "test subject survival conditions" that were wiped before anyone could read them (see "S3 Ch3 · The Truth Buried Beneath the Ground (The Island Facility)"). Anby herself has no explanation, and the genetic origin of the Silver Squad replicas she was cloned alongside has never been revealed (see "Agent BG · Anby Demara / Soldier 0 (Cunning Hares)"). **Treat any link between Anby's blood and Porcelloy as an open question in play, never as an established fact.**

85.comment: S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)
85.content:
# MESSENGER IN THE MIST · ROXY ALONE ON BOOASTRUM

Roxy carries the Porcelloy samples and the news about Girtablullu to Booastrum alone, as agreed (see "S3 Ch3 · The Homeland of Porcelloy (Vyrium and the Flint Blood)"). On the way, she reflects that after the last delivery, Claret swore never to send Eldreda any more Porcelloy, since she never gets anything back for it, and here they are again. Eldreda doesn't always come to these deliveries in person and sometimes has them leave the Porcelloy in the conference room safe. Today, though, Roxy carries more than Porcelloy, and if Eldreda doesn't show, she will take it to the Airspace Control Tower herself.

The Computing Center is in chaos. The Airspace Patrol has called a surprise drill against a Singularity Leakage, announced on a hastily printed notice, and the staff have been pulled away from their workbenches and confined to the first floor. With the communicators down, the one Bangboo receptionist on duty is drowning in requests. Deputy Director Cora went to speak to whoever is running the drill and hasn't come back. Roxy fills the wait by being Roxy. She helps a maintenance Bangboo who assumes she is too frail to lift anything (she moves the junk with one hand) and explains deadlines to an optimistic junior. A curious young man has heard legends about "a blood-drinking monster" forging her an eternally beating heart, and she tells him that being alive is enough without overthinking it. The human receptionist hands her homemade cookies for Claret as thanks for the day Claret caught a Bangboo who fell from an upper floor. Roxy at first takes it as a bid for Porcelloy and apologises, then thinks wryly about how "kind and generous" Claret is (in Roxy's memory, Claret is swearing that if she gives those three weird-eyed swindlers one more gram of Porcelloy, she will write her own name backwards).

Eldreda's usual booking, conference room 2 on the second floor, isn't in the reservation system. Upstairs, staff complain that the Airspace Patrol has never treated them like this and that neither Lady Lindverne nor Deputy Director Sigrid has explained the drill. On top of that, every soldier sent today is a new face who knows nothing about procedure. Roxy tells them to keep their distance. The conference room has a mechanical lock, which she opens without damaging anything, and inside, she finds Cora and several CCD staff held prisoner by "Airspace Patrol soldiers". They are impostors in the stolen uniforms (see "S3 Ch3 · Phoenix Comes Through the Door (Amber Hall)"), and Roxy takes them apart.

Cora explains that they barged in an hour or two earlier to announce the drill and locked up anyone who asked questions. Eldreda hasn't been at the CCD today. Roxy sends Cora and the others out through a hidden passage to call the real Airspace Patrol, asking Cora to tell Claret she will be back late tonight. Then, she heads for the **Airspace Control Tower** by the inner elevator so as not to alert the impostors outside. She runs into another squad in the stairwell, which tells her the CCD is not their only target. The tower itself is unusually quiet.

Near the top floor, Roxy overhears **Carinus**, Eldreda's right hand at the AAD, talking with someone she can't see (shown only as "???"). Carinus reminds his companion that their "little oversight" last time nearly got Lady Dracaene killed and set the whole plan back to where it stands now, and the other voice promises that this time, the preparations are thorough. Carinus answers that even a tiny rat can bring the whole plan down. A moment later, Roxy is caught. An unknown force pulls her into an Ether singularity, and as her things clatter to the floor, Carinus remarks that they almost let her disturb Lady Eldreda. Then, her phone starts to buzz.

Back at Blazelight Hall, Claret finally gets through to Roxy's number, and Carinus answers. He tells her smoothly that Roxy is discussing official matters with Lady Eldreda, whose visitors must leave their devices outside, so he only picked up because the phone kept ringing. He promises to have Roxy call back after the meeting, and Claret, relieved, wishes him good night.

Lindverne arrives with the night's operation plan. The Airspace Patrol unit stationed in Vyrium will seal the waters around the Shrouded Reef. One group, guided by Billy, will clear the transfer station and recover the Porcelloy and supplies left there, while Lindverne leads the rest into the research base, guided by Claret, to seal it and destroy the giant Ethereal that may be hiding there. Claret's analysis of the transfer station fragments says they were control devices like the ones in Girtablullu, built for something even bigger, so Bashmu seems likely. Taking Bashmu down would mean recovering Dracie's Karma Core. Lindverne asks the Proxy to come with her, since the research base may hold a Singularity Leakage. Remielle stays in Vyrium to guard against an ambush, and because she is still drawing on Thaumiel to keep Dracie stable, which takes its toll even without combat.

(Carinus' side of the story is in "NPC BG · Carinus (AAD, Roscaelifer)" and "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)". Eldreda's whereabouts are explained in "S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)".)

key: The Truth Buried Beneath the Ground
86.comment: S3 Ch3 · The Truth Buried Beneath the Ground (The Island Facility)
86.content:
# THE TRUTH BURIED BENEATH THE GROUND · THE ISLAND FACILITY

**A Bygone Era.** While the others prepare, Remielle talks in Vyrium with "the mysterious dice", the unseen companion who caught her lying to the Proxy at the end of Chapter 2 (see "S3 Ch2 · After the Curtain Falls (Serpico Lives, End of Chapter 2)"). Lindverne, she says, is nothing like the Sunbringer she knew and is closer to her opposite, and the dice reminds her that Lindverne is a different person. Remielle knows, and points out that the identity passed down to Lindverne anyway, and to all three of them. Watching Dracaene and talking with Lindverne, she has started to wonder whether things would have gone differently for her generation if the Sunbringer she knew had been more like them. The dice says they can never know. She has another question that may be answered soon: when the lie called "Sunbringer", hidden from the world since her time, finally comes out, how will Roscaelifer react, and how will New Eridu?

**The research base.** The Airspace Patrol surrounds the Shrouded Reef on schedule, and the group heads for the Flint research base built into the cliff behind the transfer station, which TOPS has turned into its own. Just as they approach the lobby, a fresh **Singularity Leakage** opens and swallows the entire building. The Proxy notes from the Ether readings that it formed recently, the same way the one around Girtablullu did. Fritz of the Airspace Patrol reports that floors one through four show signs of activity within the past few days but no personnel, while Ether activity from the fifth floor up is abnormally high. Every entrance to the underground levels was sealed before they arrived. Demolition charges could bring the whole destabilised structure down. Fritz hastens to add that he would never underestimate Lady Claret or Flint Porcelloy, and Lindverne warns him that he is only making Claret angrier. Claret knows the way: the **System Control Room** at the centre of the fifth floor controls every gate in the facility and has a backup elevator straight down to the underground levels.

On the fifth floor, they spot the man with Serpico's face standing calmly inside the control room, making no attempt to run. Lindverne wants to smash straight through the wall, and the others remind her that the structure is unstable and a Sunbringer's swing could bring the building down, so Claret makes her promise to step in only if there is no other choice. The Proxy hacks a robot and rams a shelf out of the way while Claret clears out the Ethereals that have moved in. After that, a TOPS computer gives up its files. One folder holds an **"Experiment Report: Controlling Ethereal Behavior with Porcelloy Restraints"** with device blueprints, and Claret claims she could have cut their material use by forty percent and is outraged at how much Porcelloy they wasted. A memo gives up the gate password. A third folder, "Research on Test Subject Survival Conditions", has been wiped completely, which suggests its contents were classified even higher than the Porcelloy work.

Near the control room, they find fresh battle marks, left by someone well trained, and a crescent-shaped weapon fragment. By the time they reach the room, the man is gone. The elevator log shows a descent to the underground levels about twenty minutes earlier, which looks like a dead end or a trap, and Lindverne decides they are going down anyway, since Bashmu may be there. The Proxy recognises the fragment as part of **Promeia's** weapon and explains that she is a Judge of the Krampus Compliance Authority, TOPS's internal watchdog, which horrifies Claret. Lindverne reasons that Promeia must have come to check whether another TOPS branch had overstepped its authority and been attacked after finding something she was never meant to find. Then, she says out loud what the Proxy is too embarrassed to suggest: the enemy of their enemy is a friend, and a Krampus Judge must know more about TOPS's plans in Roscaelifer than any of them.

Underground, they find Promeia fighting off a pack of Ethereals. Lindverne asks Claret whether one glass window matters to the structure, then smashes it and drops down to finish the fight on a count of three. Promeia thanks her and calls it the clean, precise power of a Sunbringer. Lindverne picks up Promeia's cape and marvels at how light and soft it is. She wants one of her own, and she drapes it back over Promeia so she won't catch a cold. Promeia makes no secret of being a Judge of Krampus and asks to cooperate, since what lies in the room ahead is more than she can handle alone. Lindverne agrees to a **temporary alliance with Krampus**, lasting as long as they share the same goal and the same enemy, and then asks for a link to buy the cape. Claret is appalled at allying with "a TOPS lackey". Promeia has never heard of Bashmu.

The tunnel to the deepest room, the **Underground Test Site**, is guarded more tightly than anything else in the base, and the Ether concentration rises with every step. The room at the end looks empty. It is a trap (see "S3 Ch3 · Kusarikku, the Replacement Sunbringer (Serpico Is Youkai)").

key: Enchainer of the Hive Lord Hollow
87.comment: S3 Ch3 · Kusarikku, the Replacement Sunbringer (Serpico Is Youkai)
87.content:
# KUSARIKKU, THE REPLACEMENT SUNBRINGER · SERPICO IS YOUKAI

The man with Serpico's face welcomes them to the Underground Test Site and greets Belle (or Wise) as his dear old classmate, then needles the Proxy for keeping such a big secret from their friends, since their credibility as a human would vanish if it came out. The Proxy refuses to accept him, because the Serpico they knew would never treat other people's lives as worthless. He answers that people change, especially after coming back from the dead. When Claret accuses him of hurting the Bangboo and stealing Dracaene's Karma Core, he admits to making use of Roscaelifer's Bangboo with the blessing of one of the city's "big shots", and calls Dracaene's case a slight complication, since her death was supposed to be swift and more peaceful. He also explains the bait: he left the Porcelloy remains at the transfer station for them to find and risked being seen in Vyrium so they would follow him here.

Then, he asks Claret to guess what the room is for. The Porcelloy devices on its walls are built to confine Ethereals, far more of them than Bashmu would need, which means they are meant for something much stronger. He confirms it: the room was built for **a true Enchainer**. To humans, it is an ordinary room and to an ordinary Ethereal a big cage. An Enchainer carrying a Karma Core finds it miserable, and with a resonance field tuned to the right frequency, it can barely stand. He presents the star of his show, **Lady Lindverne Sunbringer**, and asks whether she would prefer her other name: **Enchainer of the Hive Lord Hollow**.

Lindverne starts coughing and weakening. The Proxy suddenly resonates with the Karma Core inside her and sees something the others can't. The man calls the Proxy special and says it all ends here before unveiling "my replacement for Sunbringer": **Kusarikku** drops from the ceiling with orders to bring him the Karma Core. Lindverne warns him never to underestimate Sunbringer, and the fight is on, with Lindverne, Claret, Promeia and the Proxy against it. (Like Girtablullu the scorpion-man and Bashmu the horned serpent, Kusarikku takes its name from Mesopotamian myth, where Kusarikku is the bull-man. In battle, its grabs have to be broken with a well-timed Counter Assist.) The Proxy's thoughts race mid-fight: the Sunbringers were supposed to be Intelligent Constructs, so if they are Enchainers, was Sunbringer something the Hollows created? The man taunts Lindverne that it is a hard secret to admit and that the first Sunbringer was the same, and Claret shouts that she doesn't care what Lindverne is, she is still Lindverne.

Kusarikku pins Lindverne and knocks her greatsword away. Promeia and Claret pull her free and counterattack. When a fissure throws them off balance, Kusarikku slams them into a wall. As it closes in on Lindverne, the Proxy snatches up her greatsword and blocks the blow, swearing it won't steal another Karma Core. The two of them hold the sword together and resonate again until the greatsword reshapes itself into a saw. With it, Lindverne casually splits Kusarikku in half. **Lindverne keeps her Karma Core.**

The man applauds and calls it a half-baked amateur taking on a professional, and he doesn't run. He tells the Proxy they are no longer the top student they used to be: while everyone's attention was fixed on this room, he finished what he was after, and Booastrum has gone through earth-shattering changes. Then, he says it is getting late and he has to catch the last train back to Booastrum, so it is time to end the "old classmates" charade. When the Proxy names him, he confirms it. **The thing wearing Serpico Mosseint's grown-up face is Youkai**, the AI that rode Lockspring into the Creator's messenger and slipped free of the wreckage. After tormenting Aria and Lady Vesper in New Eridu, it threw in with Mosseint. The adult Serpico was a counterfeit body that Youkai has been piloting all along, and the real Serpico died at Helios Academy, as the siblings always believed. Youkai made the visit to Truvia's bedside at the end of Chapter 2. He hopes the Proxy will still be entertaining next time, and the body drops to the floor, empty. Claret later finds that he destroyed every storage unit inside it while uploading his data, so it tells them nothing.

Looking back, the Proxy calls the counterfeit body, wearing the face of someone long gone, an omen of the storm that was gathering.

88.comment: S3 Ch3 · The Storm Has Yet to Settle (Sunbringer's Secret)
88.content:
# THE STORM HAS YET TO SETTLE · SUNBRINGER'S SECRET

The next morning, nobody in Vyrium can reach Booastrum. Claret can't get through to Roxy, Sigrid or Velina, and the Proxy can't reach anyone at Amber Hall. Even Fairy has gone offline. Youkai was telling the truth: while the Shrouded Reef had their attention, something far worse happened on Booastrum, and failing to take Lindverne's Karma Core hasn't slowed whatever he started there. Lindverne brings worse news. Vyrium's airport has received an official notice that **all travel routes are shut down**, issued by the **Administrative Affairs Department as an emergency executive order**, with no word on Eldreda or anything else on Booastrum. The Airspace Patrol teams still searching the Shrouded Reef are unlikely to find more. When Lindverne starts to talk about "the Enchainer thing", Claret sends her off to question the TOPS stragglers her people caught trying to flee.

With Lindverne gone, Claret makes the Proxy promise that some secrets never leave the room, and turns to Promeia. Promeia is honest about her position. An Enchainer, whatever form it takes, is still an Ethereal at its core, and Ethereals call for vigilance. Most people in New Eridu meet Ethereals with hatred or fear, so the information has to stay out of the public eye, although from Krampus's perspective, she can't promise to keep the secret forever. She has already handed over every communication device she carried. Claret accepts that the alliance is Lindverne's to end and keeps Promeia at Blazelight Hall as a guest under watch, with food and necessities on Flint Workshop.

Then, Claret asks the Proxy to find Lindverne and talk to her alone. Claret has known Lindverne all her life. She and Roxy rode on Lindverne's shoulders as children, and Lindverne was the adult Claret wanted to become, then the friend she goofed around and watched old movies with. Now, she is the Sunbringer who chases ridiculous new ideas and never pays her debts, yet it is impossible to stay angry at her. To Claret, Lindverne is just Lindverne. She is also the Flint family's benefactor and the hero who has always protected Roscaelifer, and none of that will change. Her support is a given, which is exactly why it feels like too little. She noticed that the Proxy and Lindverne felt something in each other when the Proxy helped Lindverne break free in that cage, and she is certain the Proxy is special to all three Sunbringers. When Lindverne is upset, she sits somewhere open in the wind, sometimes for a whole day, so the docks are the place to look. The Proxy tells Claret she should say all of this to Lindverne herself one day, and Promeia agrees, to Claret's loud annoyance.

**The real Sunbringer.** Lindverne is at the docks. She apologises for frightening them, and the Proxy admits it did. Everyone looks up to the Lady Sunbringer who dissolved the Hive Lord Hollow and still protects Roscaelifer, and nobody wants to believe that she was a creation of the Hollow from the start: **the Enchainer of the Hive Lord Hollow**. The first Sunbringer knew the trouble the truth would cause, for Helios Academy and Eridu as much as for herself, so she deceived everyone with the lie that she was an Intelligent Construct. The three sisters inherited that lie and still carry it. Eldreda, Dracie and Lindverne were created through the power Sunbringer had as an Enchainer, **Genesis Reconstruction**: she divided her Karma Core into three parts and used them to create the three Sunbringers. That is why the core does them no harm, since it was theirs from the beginning and is the source of their power. Remielle had worked most of this out while treating Dracie.

It is the first time Lindverne has told anyone, and she expected it to feel like the end of the world and finds that she feels lighter. She never carried it alone, since she had Dracie and Eldreda, but the first Sunbringer may well have felt alone. In her era, each of the other Great Hollows had its own Enchainer, every one of them an emissary of the Creator, and Sunbringer was an outlier to humans and Enchainers alike. Lindverne asks whether the Proxy can trust that neither the first Sunbringer nor the three of them ever acted on the Creator's will. The Proxy says of course, since Rosetta Data and Roscaelifer would not exist otherwise. Anyone who knows Roscaelifer will stand with them as Claret does, the Proxy adds, because what matters is the people they have come to know and trust, and everything Sunbringer has done for the world won't disappear because of what she is.

Remielle interrupts, amused at how cozy they are getting. She worked out the secret long ago, and she apologises to the Proxy for her Void Hunter weapon story at the end of Chapter 2, since she lied to keep her old friend's secret a little longer. The Proxy accepts on the condition that they get two questions per round in their next Q&A game. Remielle protests that the Proxy could lie to her, too, for instance by telling her she has put on weight, and Lindverne observes that the Airspace Patrol's only two S-Rank criminals are now standing in one place. Then, Remielle points at something in the sky (see "S3 Ch3 · Booastrum Falls and a Meteor in the Sea (End of Chapter 3)").

For the full story of the original Sunbringer, which Chapter 4 fills in, see "S2 · Lady Sunbringer & Roscaelifer".

89.comment: S3 Ch3 · Booastrum Falls and a Meteor in the Sea (End of Chapter 3)
89.content:
# BOOASTRUM FALLS AND A METEOR IN THE SEA

The thing in the sky looks like a meteor in broad daylight, and it seems to come from the direction of Booastrum. Remielle wonders whether this counts as illegal dumping from a great height. Then, it plunges toward them into the sea and washes up on the beach across the shore. The silhouette is a person. Lindverne doubts anyone that frail could survive such a fall (Sigrid might, she says), and the Proxy recognises the girl from the photo on her island pass: **Phoenix Reffaella**, the High Ambitions medical assistant who was lying unconscious in Amber Hall when the Proxy left for Vyrium.

The chapter closes on the Proxy's narration that none of them knew yet how the girl who fell from the sky would change their future. Chapter 4 picks up on the beach (see "S3 Ch4 · Journey to the Sky (A Meteor Washes Ashore)").

**Where things stand at the end of Chapter 3:**

- Booastrum is cut off. Every line of communication is dead, Fairy included, and the AAD has shut down all travel routes by emergency executive order. Nobody in Vyrium knows what has happened there or where Eldreda is.
- The sibling and Cissia were still on Booastrum, since they had planned to follow on the next afternoon's airship, and Phoenix was there, too, until she fell out of the sky.
- About thirty stolen Airspace Patrol uniforms are being worn by impostors who seized the CCD under cover of a "surprise drill".
- Roxy is missing after being pulled into an Ether singularity in the Airspace Control Tower, and Carinus has told Claret she is in a meeting with Eldreda.
- The Sunbringers are Enchainers, and Lindverne has told the Proxy, Claret, Promeia and Remielle. Lindverne still has her Karma Core fragment, Dracaene's is inside Bashmu, wherever Bashmu is, and nobody knows Eldreda's situation.
- Youkai, who wore Serpico's face all along, is back on Booastrum.
- The Cunning Hares are safe in Vyrium, with Anby recovering at Blazelight Hall from blood loss and a lung infection.
- Promeia is a temporary ally and a guest under watch at Blazelight Hall.
- Dracaene is still unconscious in the hidden treatment room, held steady by Flint Workshop's equipment and Remielle's Thaumiel.

90.comment: S3 Ch4 · Journey to the Sky (A Meteor Washes Ashore)
90.content:
## SEASON 3 CHAPTER 4 · JOURNEY TO THE SKY

*"Within a sleepwalker's dream... another dreamer awakens."*

# A METEOR WASHES ASHORE

The chapter opens on the beach at Vyrium, where the girl who fell from the sky lies unconscious beside a strange case that came down with her. When the Proxy wonders whether falling out of the sky is some modern way to travel, Lindverne admits that even she and Sigrid only drop down from Booastrum like that when they are in a hurry, and they still have to watch out for airships and buses on the way. The Proxy's point is that this girl simply fell. Lindverne has already looked her over: no obvious injuries and steady breathing, which is exactly what makes no sense, since nobody survives a fall from that height without a scratch. The Proxy notes she isn't even a winged Thiren who could have glided down. Remielle is the one who notices the rest. The girl did have injuries when they found her, and every one of them has already vanished.

Remielle has Belle (or Wise) recount everything about her since the day before and reasons it out. The girl's only proof of identity was an island pass that could be forged, and turning up outside Amber Hall might have been a wrong turn. Jumping off a locked-down Booastrum to reach Vyrium, though, means she was after someone who was in Amber Hall then and is in Vyrium now. Billy and Eous don't have ties to Roscaelifer and the Sunbringers anywhere near as deep as the Proxy's, which leaves the Proxy, her "dear partner in crime". The Proxy has never met the girl and can't imagine why she would come looking for them, or how she knew they were in Roscaelifer. Remielle doubts she is an enemy, since nobody working with the occupiers would go to such lengths to get out, and she probably knows more about what is happening on Booastrum than anyone. The Proxy's worry goes straight to their sibling and Cissia, who should have been with her. They decide to take her to Blazelight Hall, whose medical equipment might wake her sooner, and nobody pries the case open in case they damage whatever is inside. Lindverne carries the girl, who is lighter than she looks, and the case turns out lighter than it looks, too.

At Blazelight Hall, Claret and Promeia are in the middle of an argument. Claret can't understand TOPS founding a whole organisation just to police its own side. Promeia says it exists to stop the unchecked abuse of power and resources, and that without Krampus, New Eridu and Roscaelifer would be in an even worse position. Claret takes that as a claim that Roscaelifer has to dance to TOPS's tune. Claret expected Lindverne to spend longer talking with the Proxy, and when Lindverne explains that the girl in her arms seems to have fallen from Booastrum, Promeia isn't surprised in the slightest: knowing **Phoenix**, that sounds possible. She asks why Belle (or Wise) looks so shocked, and whether Phoenix hasn't told them who she is.

The "unconscious" Phoenix answers that herself. She sits up to announce that Miss Phoenix's real identity is a **Krampus Judge** and nearly scares Lindverne half to death. She woke up while Lady Sunbringer was carrying her and decided that if she waited, she would get a better chance to spring back to life and frighten them all. When the room doesn't play along, she offers to keep playing dead a little longer and promises to scare every single one of them next time. Promeia, whom Phoenix calls "Mia", asks whether she wants the Boss to find out she has been fooling around on the job.

It is the first proper look anyone gets at her, and it sets the tone for the chapter: a woman who treats her own death as her best running joke (see "Agent BG · Phoenix Reffaella (Krampus)"). Her first serious question is for Promeia, and it is about Eldreda (see "S3 Ch4 · Let's Assassinate Eldreda Again! (Phoenix's Accusation)").

91.comment: S3 Ch4 · Let's Assassinate Eldreda Again! (Phoenix's Accusation)
91.content:
# LET'S ASSASSINATE ELDREDA AGAIN!

Phoenix asks Promeia whether she thinks she could beat Eldreda. Promeia, who knows exactly where this is going, allows that she might have a chance if she gave it everything she has. Phoenix disagrees: the gap between humans and Enchainers can't be closed by effort alone, and it takes a Void Hunter to defeat a Void Hunter and an Enchainer to defeat an Enchainer. So she turns to **Remielle** and, addressing her by her old rank as **Lieutenant Colonel Dan**, cheerfully invites her to join another attempt to assassinate Lady Eldreda. Claret can't pretend she didn't hear that, and Remielle is delighted to be invited to kill one Sunbringer in front of another. Lindverne has had enough and starts to warn them off, whoever they are, if Eldreda was their target from the start. Phoenix corrects her: Lady Eldreda has been the one targeting them, or rather all of Roscaelifer, the whole time.

To show good faith, Phoenix decides Krampus will put its cards on the table first and tells Mia to share everything they found; if the Boss has a problem with it, Phoenix will handle her. Promeia lays it out:

- The operation against Roscaelifer was proposed by **Mosseint**, head of High Ambitions Corp., and its stated objective is to seize complete control of the Rosetta Data. The Proxy immediately wonders whether Truvia knew from the start.
- During an internal review, Krampus found records of High Ambitions operating in the waters near the Minerva Storm Belt about a year earlier, and Phoenix and Promeia followed them to the research facility on the Shrouded Reef. What they found there is that Mosseint's true targets from the very beginning were **the Karma Cores inside the three Sunbringers**. More precisely, he wants a complete Karma Core so he can continue the research Helios Academy failed to finish.
- High Ambitions caught on halfway through and fought back hard, and Promeia judged that the situation had gone far beyond what the two of them could handle. The only person in Roscaelifer they trusted to help was Belle (or Wise), who happened to be in the city for treatment. Phoenix had heard all about the Proxy from Zhao ("Xiao'Zhao") and the others, since the Proxy has helped Krampus out plenty of times before.

Lindverne asks why they didn't come to her or to the Airspace Patrol, and Phoenix tells her flatly that they couldn't rule her out as the mole. Even with all of TOPS's resources, High Ambitions could never overpower Roscaelifer from the outside, with three Sunbringers protecting it in the Minerva Storm Belt; somebody high up must have looked away or helped. When they set out for Booastrum, the only Sunbringer they could rule out was Dracaene, who had already been attacked, and now that Lindverne has been kept outside Booastrum, Phoenix can clear her, too. That leaves **Lady Eldreda of the Administrative Affairs Department**, who has been far too quiet and did nothing after Dracaene was attacked, apart from ordering a lockdown on Booastrum.

Claret explodes at the "little Krampus brat": even if Roscaelifer has a mole, it could never be Eldreda, anyone but her. Phoenix notices that Claret denied only that Eldreda could be the mole and asks whether the mole is Claret herself, and Claret threatens to seal her mouth shut with Porcelloy. When Phoenix asks why she is so certain about Eldreda, Claret lets something slip. Dracaene has stayed stable partly thanks to Thaumiel's power and partly thanks to research Eldreda commissioned from Flint Workshop long ago, and if Eldreda were the mole, why would she have had them start preparing so early? Everyone stares, and Claret protests that she promised Eldreda to keep it secret. The Proxy reminds her that they all believe Eldreda is innocent, even if Phoenix's reasoning still has some merit after everything that has happened, and that Claret has already let it slip. Lindverne asks her one more time what Eldreda commissioned. Claret says she only knows what they were told to do, since Eldreda never gave her reasons. When the Proxy puts a name to it, a Karma Core substitute, Claret spells it out: Eldreda wants a way for the Sunbringers to survive even after losing their Karma Cores, and the **artificial Karma Core** is the solution the Workshop is testing now.

The Proxy works through what that means: Eldreda must have known for a while that the Sunbringers could lose their cores, and she prepared for what would come after without trying to stop it. Phoenix asks, no offence meant, whether Eldreda has a split personality. If she doesn't, it is stranger still. She saw it coming and prepared for it, yet she did nothing when Dracaene was attacked, even though she had the power and authority to step in, unless the goal all along was to make the Sunbringers lose their cores. Remielle offers "Miss Phoenix of Krampus" another possibility: perhaps Eldreda simply can't stop it from happening. Phoenix admits she hadn't considered that, and the Proxy agrees that Remielle has a point. Nobody has seen Eldreda in a while, and the enemy may have gone after her, too, except that the lockdown order went out in her name.

Lindverne asks Phoenix whether she knows anything else about what is happening on Booastrum, and Phoenix's case answers the question (see "S3 Ch4 · Return Ticket to the Horizon (Mechs Made by Genesis Reconstruction)"). The accusation against Eldreda hangs over the whole journey back to Booastrum until the real mole turns up (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)").

92.comment: S3 Ch4 · Return Ticket to the Horizon (Mechs Made by Genesis Reconstruction)
92.content:
# RETURN TICKET TO THE HORIZON · MECHS MADE BY GENESIS RECONSTRUCTION

**The case.** Asked what else she knows about Booastrum, Phoenix remembers why she came and looks around for her case, about this big, which should have fallen with her. Claret hands it over, and Phoenix can't remember the password. When it finally opens, the Proxy realises it looked familiar for a reason: the strongbox was theirs to begin with. Inside is **Fairy**, upgraded and stronger than before, who greets her master and says it is good to see them again. The Proxy introduces her to the room as their AI assistant and one of their most reliable partners, and Fairy appreciates the praise.

Fairy reports what happened. Early that morning, the Administrative Affairs Department issued an order in Lady Eldreda Sunbringer's name closing every shipping route across Booastrum, and at the same moment a large contingent of armed TOPS personnel arrived and seized key facilities across the island. Fairy has nothing on Sigrid's whereabouts. Phoenix fills in the rest. The sibling's first move was to try to reach Sigrid, without success, and just as they were about to go out, an elite TOPS squad surrounded Amber Hall and **took the sibling and Cissia away by force**. Phoenix overheard orders to take them alive and unhurt, and Fairy confirms the raiders used no violence beyond knocking out Cissia, who resisted and got minor injuries, before taking her away with the "second assistant". The sibling asked Phoenix to get Fairy to the Proxy, which mattered more than fighting, and Phoenix agreed without understanding why. She claims she carried the case from Amber Hall to Gear Street with High Ambitions on her tail and then took the plunge. Fairy corrects her: nobody was chasing her, she tripped while running and fell from Booastrum to Vyrium. Phoenix calls that close enough, since she fell out of the sky either way.

The pieces still don't fit. TOPS holds Booastrum and Eldreda never showed up, yet a real lockdown order would have to be announced by Eldreda in person before it could be enforced, so someone with that kind of authority seems to be acting in her name. Claret is the one who says the name, Carinus, and can't see how it would be possible. Lindverne refuses to believe that Eldreda or Carinus would ever betray them or Roscaelifer. She doesn't know what is going through Eldreda's head, so she will find her and get her answers directly, and as for High Ambitions, or rather TOPS, she will make every last one of them pay.

**Quietude Isle.** Booastrum is sealed, but Fairy finds a gap: about thirty minutes earlier, a shipment from **Quietude Isle** airport arrived at the harbour outpost on Booastrum and was signed for. Quietude Isle is an old supply port and depot that was still busy when Claret was a child and fell out of use after "some things happened". It only started being rebuilt a few months ago, after the AAD proposed it at the Five Central Departments meeting on wider cooperation with New Eridu (Carinus argued they would need a new airport for the growing flow of people and supplies). Fairy's link to the island's surveillance shows High Ambitions has taken it over completely. Claret wants to simply take it back, since it belongs to Roscaelifer. Promeia warns that a head-on assault could make High Ambitions fight to the bitter end and drag everyone down with it, and in the worst case, every person and Bangboo stranded on Booastrum could be taken hostage. Lindverne agrees with Promeia: High Ambitions holds far too many hostages, and acting recklessly would only put people in greater danger. The plan is to slip onto Quietude Isle unnoticed and board a supply airship into Booastrum.

Claret wonders how they are supposed to sneak in at all and jokes about turning up with crates of Porcelloy as a gift and pretending to surrender, only to find everyone staring at her. Remielle thinks a nice gift might work, if not Porcelloy then something High Ambitions would still value, and Claret works out what they mean: tie her up and hand her over as a present. The Proxy points out that it would at least be more believable than some random TOPS mercenary capturing THE Lindverne Sunbringer, and Claret can't believe they are seriously considering it. Phoenix volunteers herself. Krampus has surely been marked hostile by now, so the story writes itself. A gravely wounded Krampus Judge recovering at Amber Hall was discovered during another High Ambitions raid and chased down after a desperate escape on which even her wings couldn't save her. Now, she has been squeezed for intel on Quietude Isle and gift-wrapped for High Ambitions as proof of loyalty. The Proxy can't help noticing that she gets more excited the longer she describes it. Lindverne finds it more believable than her own capture, and the Proxy raises the snag: High Ambitions has seen all their faces by now, so how will they get Phoenix up there? Claret has already figured out a way and reminds the Proxy of the High Ambitions mechs they found at the Shrouded Reef transfer station. The Proxy wants to go and recover them. Lindverne says there is no need: tell her what is needed and she will take care of the rest. The Proxy doubts anyone can make that happen on the spot, and Claret answers that maybe nobody else could, but Lindverne is a Sunbringer, so they should leave it to her.

**Goodbyes.** Lindverne lays out the plan. The team will be small, with Phoenix as the hostage and Lindverne as her escort. Belle (or Wise) insists on coming, too, for their sibling and Cissia and for any Singularity Leakages on the way, and Lindverne meant to bring the Proxy along anyway. Remielle stays in Vyrium to keep Dracaene stable and to back them up, and Claret takes charge of Vyrium's defences, her responsibility anyway, with Promeia's help ("just don't slow me down"). Lindverne thanks them all for lending Roscaelifer their help even though their goals may not perfectly align, and warns that once they reach Booastrum, they will probably lose contact with everyone outside. Before leaving, the Proxy makes the rounds. Remielle reports that Dracaene is stable for now, though she won't stay that way if Remielle and Thaumiel are away too long. She teases the Proxy for not begging her to come along ("my dearest partner in crime, please don't make me face this adventure alone"), and promises to fly to Booastrum if anything goes wrong while she helps keep Vyrium safe. Nicole reports that Roscaelifer's medical care is the real deal and the Bangboo medics expect Anby to wake soon. Swearing to dig up dirt on TOPS, she asks the Proxy to give whoever hurt Anby a few extra punches in the face. Billy adds a few for Nekomata and himself, and points out that even with Anby's medical bill waived, they still owe for a broken door. Nekomata has sat up with Anby all night. Nicole, who has been awake all night, too, sends Billy to help with the mech and goes to take over from Nekomata herself.

**A mech from thin air.** At the landing pad, Claret is glad of an extra pair of hands, and Billy offers to do the heavy lifting, assuming they are building an entire mech from scratch, which there is no time for. Lindverne uses what she calls Sunbringer's Authority (her fragment of **Genesis Reconstruction**) to recreate the mech from everyone's descriptions, and it goes badly in an entertaining way. Phoenix's description (purple, gold and black, two pairs of wings, like a big purple moth flapping around) produces exactly that, and Claret can't believe TOPS would build something that bizarre. The real thing is a humanoid mech made of Porcelloy, completely mechanical and nothing like a mechanised Ethereal. Billy says it looked a lot like Black Hole, the villain from *Starlight Knight*, and Lindverne, who has of course seen Starlight Knight, produces something so close that they are surely about to get sued. Several more rounds of corrections follow (thrusters on the legs, less black, two pointy things on the back of its head, the way it jumps like a big old toad, an exoskeleton that wastes Porcelloy) until Phoenix calls the latest draft almost obscene to look at and Claret takes over the description herself. The mech comes out right. Lindverne adds a few tweaks of her own and swears it outperforms the original by a mile, and admits she doesn't do this often and Dracaene or Eldreda would be much better at it. Claret sighs that it isn't fair: real design means overtime day after day and losing your hair by the handful. Lindverne consoles her that even Sunbringers can't match her workshop's production lines for output and efficiency. Then, Claret asks them, as an afterthought she tries to take back, to look out for Roxy, who is smarter than she is and must have found somewhere safe to hide, and the Proxy promises to bring Roxy home. Nicole tells Claret the Cunning Hares are ready to help however they can.

After the airship leaves, Claret calls Promeia out of hiding, since she knew Promeia was there, and so did Lindverne and "that girl you work with". Promeia admits she came to make sure there were no complications, and the complication is Phoenix. Any Krampus Judge would have done as the hostage, Promeia included, and it would probably have been safer for everyone if she had gone and Phoenix had stayed in Vyrium. She meant to say so at the time, but Phoenix discreetly signalled her to keep quiet. Knowing Phoenix, she isn't done having fun yet. Claret asks whether Promeia thinks Lindverne missed any of this. Lindverne isn't the Airspace Patrol's Administrative Director for nothing, Claret tells her: she acts carefree, yet nobody is more cautious when Roscaelifer is in real danger. Whether Phoenix cooperates or stirs up more trouble matters less than having a strong enough fail-safe to keep a wild card like her in check. Promeia guesses who that fail-safe is, Lindverne, and Claret confirms it: Lindverne herself is Roscaelifer's most reliable fail-safe, and with her around, nobody gets out of line. Promeia hopes so. The infiltration itself is the next entry (see "S3 Ch4 · Airport Assault (Quietude Isle)").

93.content:
# AIRPORT ASSAULT · QUIETUDE ISLE

At Quietude Isle, a guard wants to know which squad they are from and why anyone needs two mechs for one half-conscious woman. Lindverne, as the escort, introduces them as a special mobile task force assigned to escort Krampus Judge Phoenix, who must be interrogated immediately. The guard thinks he has heard the name, and while he checks the records, Phoenix plays the defeated captive with enormous drama: to think that she, Krampus's number one Judge and greatest secret weapon, would meet her match in two such formidable foes, after a battle evenly matched to the bitter end. The guard remembers his buddy describing Krampus's secret weapon as a big guy over three metres tall and covered in flames, which she doesn't resemble, then finds that the higher-ups did warn them some Krampus people might show up. Phoenix steers the conversation further off track by explaining that she stumbled on High Ambitions' books while investigating and found all the ways the company shortchanges its employees and stretches their hours, the guards' shifts most of all. The guard agrees they have been pulling that for ages. Lindverne cuts her off by declaring the mission highly classified and threatening to take the guard in, too, if he keeps asking. He leads them off to wait for a cargo airship, the only kind still running, and starts stalling. The Proxy suspects it, and Lindverne realises they were seen through a while ago. The guard drops the act. Their acting is terrible, even worse than his, and orders have just come down to shoot anyone suspected of being a Krampus Judge on sight. Phoenix complains that this wasn't part of the plan.

**The fight.** The guards try to warn Booastrum, and Fairy breaks into Quietude Isle's communications. The fight across the skyport is mech work, swapping between melee and ranged modes and firing a stronger laser after a dash or heavy special. Explosives and heavy objects get shot or punched out of the way. Phoenix asks whether Lindverne is the "no witnesses means perfect stealth" type, too, in which case the two of them might get along, and decides Lindverne must be a master of stealth, which explains how she captured Phoenix in the first place. Lindverne calls her a drama queen and wants Claret to build one of these mechs for everyone in the Airspace Patrol. Belle (or Wise) gets stuck in theirs when the hatch jams, because Lindverne forgot to leave room for a Bangboo and made the cockpit single-occupancy (sorry, Belle, sorry, Eous). The Proxy tells her she will have plenty of chances to redeem herself.

With their cover blown, Phoenix wonders whether they still need a hostage, and supposes Roscaelifer's great leader is about to kill one, or, more accurately, stab an ally in the back. Lindverne tells her to prove she is an ally. Phoenix vows in grand style to get the two of them to Booastrum even if it costs her life. When Lindverne tells her to forget it and focus on staying in one piece, Phoenix wishes she had been told sooner, since she would have coughed up a little less blood. Fairy has hijacked Quietude Isle's channel and swapped the outgoing alert for a question about how many meat dishes are in tonight's staff meal (none), and by her impeccably reliable calculations, the enemy will notice in about fifteen minutes. They need to reach the **Central Station** in that time and board a short-range airship to Booastrum, and Lindverne calls fifteen minutes more than enough.

The skyport is stacked with supplies, a sign High Ambitions planned this for a long time. Asked who they are, Lindverne introduces them as gym equipment salespeople, then corrects herself: the troopers are the gym equipment. When a big target turns up, Phoenix announces it isn't her specialty and leaves it to the other two, and when the Proxy asks whether she isn't supposed to be a Krampus Judge, she answers that you always save the best for last. A damaged transport platform gives way under the mech's weight. Phoenix says she has taken so many falls lately that she is getting used to it, and the Proxy finds themselves out of the mech without knowing how and goes looking for Eous. Lindverne has Eous with her, decides the fall was a blessing in disguise since the Proxy is free of the cockpit at last, and offers Phoenix a turn in the mech, which is pretty fun to pilot. Phoenix saves that for a day with more time. Fairy plots a route along the logistics tracks. Phoenix introduces herself to a trooper as the Phoenix of Krampus, sent by her Boss for their lives, and when he says he has never heard of her, tells him he has now. The Proxy wonders why hardly anyone in High Ambitions seems to know who she is; Phoenix explains that she is Krampus's secret weapon and anyone who has seen her is dead, then says she is kidding.

At the Central Station, the last troopers boast that they have the numbers even against a Sunbringer and wonder why the reinforcements they called for ages ago never arrived, and Phoenix pities them for being abandoned already. They field a mech exactly like the one Lindverne built. Lindverne offers them the chance to lay down their weapons and leave Roscaelifer alive, and a trooper promises that High Ambitions will rule Roscaelifer soon. Once the last of them falls, someone is waiting for the group (see "S3 Ch4 · A Commissioner Sent Alone (Severian)").

94.comment: S3 Ch4 · A Commissioner Sent Alone (Severian)
94.content:
# A COMMISSIONER SENT ALONE

The man waiting at Quietude Isle's Central Station is **Severian Lowell**, Senior Commissioner of New Eridu Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division. He is Seth's older brother and Cissia's boss (the "Demon Lord", in Cissia's words, whom she has never once seen smile). He looks around and remarks that Booastrum doesn't seem to match their intel. When Lindverne explains that this is a nearby airport and that High Ambitions holds Booastrum, he concludes that he has boarded the wrong airship again, and that the situation in Booastrum matches their intel exactly.

Phoenix recognises his badge as the surface city's. He introduces himself to Lindverne politely and adds Krampus Judge Miss Phoenix like a free bonus thrown in at the end, which offends her, since they are old friends; he promises to be more courteous the next time he puts her on trial. Their history is, in his word, complicated. He can't discuss the details, but he has been gathering evidence to put her on trial as soon as possible and see justice duly served. When she argues that the two of them are practically in the same line of work, he reminds her that Public Security does not practise extrajudicial punishment, and she answers that this is exactly why she said they are in the same line of work. Lindverne lets it drop and asks whether, unlike certain people, he has a legitimate reason and proper authorisation to be in Roscaelifer at a time like this. He does: New Eridu's City Administration and Roscaelifer's Five Central Departments asked Public Security to join the rescue. Lindverne hopes the request came from Eldreda. It came from **Velina Airgid**, Administrative Director of the External Strategy Department.

**The phone call.** His orders trace back to a call that officially never happened. Velina had been placed under house arrest after the lockdown order, and she called **Mayor Mayflower** anyway. She had no news of Eldreda, and while the Airspace Patrol was struggling to retake Booastrum, High Ambitions was far too well prepared. When the Mayor asked whether she wanted the City Administration to step in, Velina said she had no desire to act beyond her authority and be questioned by Lady Lindverne later. What she proposed was how his intervention should be reported. High Ambitions threatened an unprecedented catastrophe for New Eridu's future, so the Mayor was forced to overstep his jurisdiction, and Roscaelifer won't let that jeopardise its cooperation with the City Administration. Since Roscaelifer is under lockdown, no outgoing call was ever made. He told her she grows more persuasive by the day, and that officially, the City Administration takes no sides: the balance is hard-won, and he respects Roscaelifer as he respects TOPS and the Defense Force. Velina credited him with that balance, since it exists because he preserved each side's right to choose its own path, and he called himself an old man who has long outlived his usefulness. Then, she gave him his justification: if the Rosetta Data slips out of the Celestial Nexus's control, every Hollow becomes an unknowable death zone again, so whatever High Ambitions wants threatens far more than Roscaelifer. The Mayor noted that the ESD shouldn't even know that much, which shows how far the Sunbringers trust her. He called Roscaelifer, the utopia Sunbringer dreamed of, a precious exception in this day and age. Everyone fighting to protect that legacy, he said, reminds him of the **Three Pacts**, the three corporations at TOPS's round table (see "S1 · TOPS (The Outstanding Paragons Alliance)"): once they were all in the right, and now, each believes its own path is the only right one. He promised New Eridu would not simply stand by, and Velina promised to thank him in person once it is over.

**The orders.** About thirty minutes earlier, the electronic monitoring device Cissia wears had sent an emergency alert of abnormal vital signs, which told Severian that a crisis was under way in Roscaelifer. The Mayor gave him the job. Severian suggested Victoria Housekeeping would be better suited if force was needed, and the Mayor declined, wanting as few people involved as possible. Of Mosseint, he said, having crossed paths with him a few times, that the man has courage to go with his talent and conviction but walks with his head down, rarely looking up or asking where his road leads. He takes consequences into account once he knows what they are. So someone else must be pulling Mosseint's strings, and the Mayor authorised Severian to **execute whoever hides behind Mosseint and dares to come after the Rosetta Data on the spot, no report required**. Severian summed up his mission in three parts: help Roscaelifer out of its crisis and make sure his subordinate Cissia survives, then bring the mastermind behind High Ambitions to justice. Lindverne thanks him for his assistance. (By the end of the chapter, it turns out Mosseint is already dead, killed by Truvia and Youkai; see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)".)

Back at the Central Station, Phoenix marvels that she has lived to see the day the two of them fight side by side. Severian sums up that the enemy is holding Cissia and the Proxy's sibling hostage, and the Proxy admits nobody knows where they were taken.

He takes his job very seriously and won't hesitate to use the force he thinks is necessary to uphold true order, and his combat style matches: he dodges incoming attacks almost before they happen and turns each one into a counterattack (see "Agent BG · Severian Lowell (Public Security)"). With him on board, the group heads for Booastrum itself (see "S3 Ch4 · The Flag Never Falls (Back Into Booastrum)").

95.comment: S3 Ch4 · The Flag Never Falls (Back Into Booastrum)
95.content:
# THE FLAG NEVER FALLS · BACK INTO BOOASTRUM

Before they can leave Quietude Isle, a ticking sound leads them to one of the defeated troopers. The Proxy fears a bomb, and it turns out to be a communicator. The voice on it is **Youkai**, wishing his "dearest friends" good morning and asking whether they dreamed about him. The Proxy recognises that annoyingly punchable voice at once, and Youkai is touched that they know him so well already. He knew about their rampage across the skyport all along. It is a shame they brought Fairy, he says, since **Jinni**, "our best at blending in", might have slipped them back into Booastrum under his nose. Jinni is the most discreet of the four "keys", the AI quadruplets that include Fairy and Youkai himself (see "S2 Interlude · Youkai (The Fourth Key)"). He left them the hidden route on purpose and thanks them for clearing out a pack of useless High Ambitions idiots, and as a reward he offers them about a third of a Karma Core. Since that may sound stingy after how far they have come, he throws in an invitation. Belle (or Wise) is to be the star of his little show; Truvia and the sibling are already there, and a true Helios reunion wouldn't be complete without the Proxy. The sibling should be fine for now, and how long that lasts is up to the Proxy. Everyone will be waiting at the **Airspace Control Tower**.

When Lindverne demands to know what he did to Eldreda, he turns on her: the third Sunbringer, poor thing, he almost feels sorry for her. The evidence is right in front of her face and she still won't believe it. Is she a Sunbringer at all, or the type whose brain is all muscle? The High Ambitions invasion, the Booastrum lockdown, everything he is doing right now, all of it was Eldreda's call. When she refuses to believe it, he calls her as hopeless a fool as Eldreda. Lindverne insists she is fine and wants to head straight for the control tower and Eldreda. Phoenix stops her: not quite. The plan they agreed was to take back Booastrum first and find Eldreda after that, and Phoenix asks whether she has got that wrong. Lindverne agrees, and Phoenix is pleased she remembered it right. Fairy apologises for not disguising the communications channel well enough to buy them time and calls it a failure as their assistant. The Proxy tells her she has already been a huge help, and that the call at least warns them Youkai has plenty more traps waiting in Booastrum.

Severian reads the provocation as deliberate: it wants their attention fixed on the control tower, or more precisely on Lady Eldreda. The Proxy agrees there must be something Youkai doesn't want them to notice, and Phoenix gets it: it's like hiding Xiao'Zhao behind Banyue Shifu, where nobody would even know she's there. The Proxy wonders what could matter more to Youkai than Lady Eldreda, and Severian suggests the Rosetta Data. To an AI like Youkai, the Proxy agrees, the Rosetta Data has to be worth far more than a Karma Core, so why would he work with High Ambitions to seize the Sunbringers' fragments? It doesn't make sense. Lindverne decides that Eldreda must know what this is all about, and Severian says time is short and they should leave for Booastrum at once. (Between this call and the landing, the chapter cuts away to Youkai and Truvia; see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)".)

**The counterattack.** Booastrum is a battlefield, with the Airspace Patrol fighting High Ambitions mercenaries in the streets. Since this is an emergency, Severian asks Lindverne's permission to use necessary force in Booastrum, and she tells him she is no stickler for rules and he should do whatever he thinks necessary; anyone who resists, he announces, will be subdued immediately. A patrol soldier greets Lindverne with relief, and Lindverne rallies everyone: now is their chance to strike back, and Roscaelifer soars eternal. She will force her way through to the central elevator and retake the control tower, and she tells her people to claim their victory for Roscaelifer and for themselves. When the mercenaries try to hold the line, Lindverne asks since when the place was theirs to defend. A mercenary asks who these people are, and Phoenix gives Severian's name as her own: she is Severian from Public Security, and anyone who wants revenge should feel free to come and find him. The city starts to turn. **Cadyn** reports that apart from parts of Gear Street and Emerald Central Park, the armed personnel across Booastrum are under control, with squads two and three on their way to finish the job. There is no exact count of casualties yet, but the injured, people and Bangboo alike, are in the medical teams' care. Lindverne orders them to stay vigilant in the reclaimed areas and step up patrols, since the enemy could still be lurking in the shadows.

There is still no word from **Sigrid**. After the lockdown order went out, she suspected something was wrong and led a team into the Airspace Control Tower to confirm Eldreda's safety, and contact was lost after that. Lindverne can't understand how all this happened with both Eldreda and Sigrid in the tower. The Central Elevator to the tower has failed for unknown reasons and urgent repairs will take time, but Fairy's surveillance confirms that the **Sky Bridge** on the CCD's third floor still connects to the tower, so they will cut through the CCD. Cadyn asks to come along, since the CCD is still full of hostiles and nobody knows what is inside the tower. Lindverne sends him back to the residents, who need the patrol more than she does, and promises to handle the tower personally. Phoenix says she is starting to see why Lindverne is the one running the Airspace Patrol, and the Proxy calls the speech cool, worthy of the patrol's director. Lindverne protests that it's no big deal and she was only assigning work as usual, and Phoenix decides she can see why Lindverne and Claret get along so well. Severian clears his throat and saves the small talk for later, and Lindverne gets them moving. They have rested long enough, so they will cut through the CCD and breach the control tower, then find Eldreda and take back "our Roscaelifer".

**The CCD.** Inside, Lindverne finds the place still full of High Ambitions troops and, wondering how there can still be so many of them, orders them to drop their weapons and surrender. A mercenary answers that the word "surrender" doesn't exist in their dictionary, and Phoenix tells him he must have bought a knockoff. They clear the building floor by floor, with Phoenix wondering whether Lindverne is even more of a brute than she is and offering to put in a good word for her at Krampus, where the benefits are pretty sweet. **Cora** can hardly believe it is Lindverne. With Lady Dracaene still not recovered and nobody knowing where Lady Eldreda is, she can't bear to think what would have happened if they had lost Lindverne, too. Lindverne apologises for not coming sooner and tells her it is over. The CCD is in far better shape than she expected, and she praises Cora for it. Cora credits Miss Roxy, and the Proxy is surprised to hear Roxy was there. Cora explains that Roxy arrived the night before needing to see Eldreda in person about something very important. Finding the CCD crawling with impostors in Airspace Patrol uniforms (in league with the occupiers), she gave them a proper beating, and shortly before the lockdown order came, she left for the control tower with a strange case to find Lady Eldreda (see "S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)"). Lindverne realises the missing uniforms were the impostors' doing, too, and the Proxy concludes that Roxy must still be inside the tower. Lindverne tells Cora to rest with the CCD staff and then evacuate, keeping well away from the CCD and the control tower, because things there are about to get very intense.

Outside the tower, on the bridge where they first ran into Girtablullu, the Proxy admits the place brings back unpleasant memories. Phoenix decides the tower looks like bad news and Roscaelifer's working conditions must be rough. The Proxy says it was never like this before: whatever happened, the tower has to be crawling with Singularity Leakages, and who knows what traps Youkai has set up for them. Severian tells everyone they must stay vigilant. Lindverne wonders whether Eldreda is still in there and decides she can explain herself when they find her. The climb itself is the next entry (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Sigrid and Roxy)").

96.comment: S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Sigrid and Roxy)
96.content:
# THE STAIRWAY OF SEEKING · SIGRID AND ROXY

Inside the **Airspace Control Tower**, Singularity Leakages have warped the space, and Ethereals are attacking High Ambitions' own people as readily as anyone else. Severian reads it as stalling: in the mastermind's eyes, the mercenaries are no longer enough to stop them, so the tower is being filled with leakages to buy time, even though the enemy already held it before they arrived. The question is what for. Severian wonders whether it has to do with Lady Eldreda, since they still know nothing about her condition and there may be some connection to the stalling they have yet to uncover. Lindverne says she thinks she knows what the enemy is after: it is time to share a secret only the Sunbringers know.

**The source of the Rosetta Data.** The CCD has never been what continuously decodes the Rosetta Data. Its work is more like filtering spring water from the mountains and bottling it, which doesn't make Dracaene's and Cora's work unimportant; the more important part happens before the filtering. The source of the Rosetta Data is at the very top of this tower, and the one protecting it at its source is **Eldreda**. Up there is a **secret chamber**, and none of the three sisters knows what is inside it. All they share is a hazy memory of a promise made long ago to someone: to protect that chamber no matter what and never let anyone enter or discover its secret. That includes the Sunbringers themselves, who must never set foot inside. Phoenix sums it up: all these years, they have been guarding something without knowing what it is. Lindverne does know that the true source of the Rosetta Data has been hidden in that chamber from the very beginning. If Youkai is still stalling after coming this far, he must have found out about the chamber and be trying to get in, and the Proxy realises Eldreda may be trapped at the top, protecting it. Lindverne hopes so. Either way, the goal is clear: reach the top and make sure the Rosetta Data is safe.

**The climb.** Phoenix has spent the chapter falling from great heights and is appalled to be climbing one. She pleads with the broken elevator and asks for a backup one; there isn't one, Lindverne explains, because if the elevator breaks, you take the stairs, and the tower isn't that tall, only a few minutes at full sprint. Phoenix tells her she will have to carry her to the top if she collapses halfway. The Proxy promises breaks along the way, since the tower is full of leakages and it is safer to take it slowly, and Phoenix adopts Belle (or Wise) as her sibling "from another mister and another mother". The way up keeps running through overlapping dimensions and Singularity Leakages that only the Proxy can open and cross ("good thing we have a legendary Proxy leading the way", says Lindverne). The Proxy hacks door terminals, sending Eous up to reach the ones that are out of reach, and hunts down hardware failures to restore power to a stalled elevator. When Lindverne finds a door locked and tells everyone to stand back so she can take care of it, the Proxy stops her, since forcing it open in such unstable space could set off a chain reaction, and goes looking for another way.

One lock holds something it shouldn't: fragments of high-clearance AAD files. Hiding classified files inside a door lock is a new one on Lindverne, and it doesn't add up, since Eldreda takes data security far too seriously. Fairy has already restored them. They concern the AAD's recent proposal to widen cooperation with New Eridu, which listed **TOPS, the HIA and the White Star Institute** among the invited parties. After Eldreda approved it, its drafter was given full authority to oversee its execution: **Carinus**, Deputy Administrative Director of the AAD. Nobody has seen him since the lockdown, and when Claret called Roxy the night before, he was the one who picked up. His position gives him free access across Roscaelifer, and still Lindverne can't bring herself to doubt his loyalty without solid evidence. Carinus has served Roscaelifer longer than any of the three sisters: he is an **Intelligent Construct personally created by the first Sunbringer**, dedicated to managing and developing the city, and he has worked at her side since Roscaelifer was founded. The Proxy suggests being an Intelligent Construct may have left him vulnerable, since back in New Eridu Youkai hacked Intelligent Constructs and turned them against them again and again. Lindverne asks whether that scheming AI could be controlling Carinus. Severian points out that a hijacked Carinus could have done far more with his authority than issue a single lockdown order. His office isn't far above them.

When an elevator finally comes into view, Pyrois asks the Proxy whether they noticed it, too, and the Proxy puts the thought into words: so many stretches of this route could only be passed through a Singularity Leakage that nobody but the Proxy could reach the top, as if the whole route had been designed to single them out. When Lindverne asks whether something is wrong, the Proxy keeps it to themselves. (Truvia later confirms it: she laid the route as a string of riddles for a fellow child of Helios; see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)".) The elevator only reaches the middle levels, where a power failure has to be fixed first.

**Sigrid and Roxy.** Partway up, they find **Sigrid** and **Roxy**. Sigrid apologises for letting Booastrum fall, and Lindverne tells her it wasn't her fault and that without her and the patrol, things would have been far worse, then gives her a new mission: escort Roxy out of the tower and see that she reaches Vyrium for treatment. Roxy, pale and anaemic, insists on speaking first: **Carinus has betrayed Roscaelifer**. She tells her story. She was carrying the Porcelloy Claret had entrusted to her to a meeting with Lady Eldreda, a regular part of Claret's schedule, and the reception at the Computing Center said there was no appointment on record. The intel about the Porcelloy was too important to wait, so she went straight to the control tower. The moment she walked in, she caught Carinus in a secret meeting. When she tried to get close enough to see who was with him, he spotted her, and a Singularity Leakage opened out of nowhere and swallowed her. She has been trapped since. The Proxy guesses that a leakage appearing out of thin air could mean Truvia, and Roxy confirms that the person with Carinus was **Truvia** of High Ambitions. The Proxy objects that Truvia was still unconscious from her injuries. Sigrid confirms it all the same: Truvia ambushed her the same way inside the tower and **can control Singularity Leakages at will**, which is how she kept them both trapped for so long. Her injury from Girtablullu, which Sigrid saw happen, was a smokescreen that let her slip out of sight without raising suspicion (Phoenix makes a note to try that next time she wants to sneak off and have some fun). Roxy has no idea what Carinus could be after.

Sigrid asks who the two strangers are. Phoenix introduces herself as a hostage kidnapped by Lindverne and the Proxy, while Severian is Public Security here to assist Roscaelifer. Lindverne sums them up as reinforcements. Roxy thanks them, and Severian says he is only doing his job. Phoenix, just following orders herself, insists she isn't with him, which Roxy says is obvious. Roxy claims she is only a little anaemic, and Lindverne, who promised Claret to bring her back to Vyrium in one piece, carries her to the central elevator. Meanwhile, the Proxy wonders whether Truvia could have sided with someone like Youkai or whether Youkai is using her, and decides to ask Truvia in person. Once the elevator is back online, Sigrid waits to see the others safely off toward the top. The elevator only goes down as far as the third floor, so she will blast a hole through its floor and jump straight to the base of the tower with Roxy in her arms. The Proxy finds that a little excessive, even for emergency measures, and Lindverne gives Sigrid her permission. Roxy assures the Proxy it's fine, since she has grown used to this by now, and had milady been giving the orders, the approach would have been far more imaginative. Deciding Roscaelifer's working conditions are rough, Phoenix asks Roxy whether she has ever thought about jumping ship to Krampus and earns a sharp "Hey" from Lindverne. Then, she withdraws the offer herself: on benefits, Krampus could never top Roscaelifer, so Roxy shouldn't even bother coming over. Sigrid bids them farewell for now, since she and Roxy will wait outside for good news. The Proxy worries about the sibling, and Severian points out that for the enemy, the hostages are a means to an end, so there is nothing to worry about.

Higher up, Carinus is waiting, and so is the truth about the lockdown (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)").

key: toll exacted by the Rosetta Data
97.comment: S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)
97.content:
# THE STAIRWAY OF SEEKING · CARINUS' CONFESSION

(The climb up the tower, the AAD files and the meeting with Sigrid and Roxy come first; see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Sigrid and Roxy)".)

**Carinus.** Higher up, they find **Carinus**, wrecked and apologising for letting Lady Lindverne see him in such a disgraceful state. Fairy reports that about 37% of his components are damaged to varying degrees, so he has temporarily lost the ability to function and needs immediate comprehensive maintenance. She also finds traces of multiple intrusions by Youkai. Lindverne tells him not to speak and promises to have him fixed. She will find Eldreda and get the whole truth from her, she says, and once every High Ambitions intruder is in an Airspace Patrol cell, she will restore him and Roscaelifer to the way they were. Carinus tells her she still refuses to believe the truth. **He was the one who promised to share the Rosetta Data and let TOPS into Booastrum, acting alone and on his own authority.** Lindverne asks whether his Logic Core is malfunctioning. He understands why she would want it to be a misunderstanding, but there is only one truth: he betrayed all of Roscaelifer, her and Lady Eldreda included, and he exploited Eldreda's plan to expand cooperation with New Eridu. When Severian asks why High Ambitions, Carinus asks who he is, and Lindverne tells him to answer: High Ambitions offered the most effective maintenance solution, one that could cut the toll exacted by the Rosetta Data to a minimum. The Proxy repeats the phrase, and Lindverne asks Carinus how much he knows about the Rosetta Data. He tells her she doesn't need to know any more; it is no longer her concern. He was outplayed, he says, and nobody walks away from the storm they have unleashed unscathed; there will be no victor.

A flashback shows the meeting. Carinus expected to meet Mr. Mosseint, unless High Ambitions was so sure of victory that it thought he couldn't bring its scheme crashing down in the blink of an eye. **Youkai**, wearing Serpico's face, assured him that Mr. Mosseint would be there any moment, just caught in a little traffic, since Booastrum was in total chaos, and offered to start negotiating with **Truvia**, "our High Ambitions Corp. heiress", who could speak on Mosseint's behalf with the same weight.
