Carinus laid out what he understood: High Ambitions' technology could free Roscaelifer from the price of sustaining the Rosetta Data, and it also gave them the perfect opening to seize the Data for themselves, since they had come for the Karma Cores from the start. Youkai laughed that Carinus had dragged them all the way there to tell them something they already knew, and asked what made him think he could stop any of it. Carinus returned the question: what made them think they could take the Karma Cores so easily when they didn't even know where Lady Eldreda was? Taking it for a bid to cut a deal, Youkai admitted their earlier offer had been a tad low and asked what he wanted. Carinus' terms were to return Lady Dracaene's Karma Core and honour the original agreement to help maintain the Rosetta Data; whether he would still share control of the Rosetta Data with them, as Lady Eldreda had proposed, would depend on their conduct. Youkai sarcastically offered to add another condition, that they turn over a new leaf by surrendering to the Airspace Patrol and becoming model citizens, and Carinus told him he would accept, if they were willing. Truvia asked whether he wasn't afraid they would burn the bridges and take him down with them, and he answered that times have changed, Miss Truvia, and modern bridges are surprisingly resilient. Youkai said he knew what Carinus was after, but the decision was above their pay grade, so they would have to invite the man in charge. He called on Mr. Mosseint, or rather "the late Mr. Mosseint". Mosseint's body crashed onto the table out of thin air, his face frozen in terror and confusion: Truvia and Youkai had killed him, and showing Carinus the corpse was their answer to his terms (see "NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)"). Then, Truvia agreed that times have changed: the leverage they hold only matters if the other side agrees it has value, so Carinus should show them his hand and how many cards he has left to play.

When Lindverne asks what he has done, Carinus admits he gave everything to draw them to the only place he could still control, a round table in a conference room, and handled it the way he had for the past hundred years. The result speaks for itself. When Lindverne asks where Eldreda is, he says she already knows the answer. His last words are for Eldreda: he failed her, and given another chance, he would still try to stop her from meeting an end that should never have been hers. Then, he falls silent. Fairy reports he has gone into temporary dormancy. Lindverne points out that the first Sunbringer crafted his Logic Core herself, so Youkai couldn't destroy it that easily, and wonders what else there is to him.

Severian judges that Carinus' account is at least partly credible, since if he had been High Ambitions' accomplice from the start, Sigrid and Roxy would not be alive; he may have protected them, or at least didn't want them dead. Phoenix observes that Krampus, Public Security, Roscaelifer and everything that happened at Helios Academy all lead back to Truvia and that obnoxious-sounding AI. The Proxy still can't believe Truvia would be Youkai's accomplice, but agrees it must connect to Helios Academy, since Youkai took Serpico's form for a reason, and Lady Eldreda was connected to Helios Academy, too. Everyone has questions for Eldreda now, and Phoenix starts thinking about her verdict for Truvia. They ride the logistics tracks up through the last High Ambitions loyalists, who know what awaits them if they fail. Near the top, the Proxy warns everyone never to underestimate Truvia's power, which none of them has seen first-hand, and Lindverne answers that the enemy are the ones who should be worried: it is time to settle the score once and for all.

At the last stretch before the top, Lindverne thanks everyone for getting her this far, admitting she has been saying that a lot today. She starts on something about what comes next until the Proxy cuts in with a cheerful "let's move and groove". Phoenix asks Lindverne why she looks so surprised and calls it: she was about to say it is too dangerous from here and she will face the boss alone, wasn't she? The Proxy says there is no way she would think that, and besides, the sibling and Cissia are still up there waiting, so the Proxy isn't about to bail now. Severian has no intention of giving up halfway either. Phoenix claims she was only joking and wonders why everyone is so serious: there is a huge boss at the top of the tower, and a walking EXP jackpot that big has to be shared with the whole party. Severian finds her priorities unusual. When Phoenix asks whether she is the only one who thinks that way, the Proxy wonders who would even be thinking about EXP at a time like this. Lindverne agrees with the Proxy that it is time for one last push, and they go up together, the Proxy calling ahead to the sibling and to Truvia (see "S3 Ch4 · Sorry, I Just Can't Seem to Die (Phoenix Impaled)").

98.comment: S3 Ch4 · Sorry, I Just Can't Seem to Die (Phoenix Impaled)
98.content:
# SORRY, I JUST CAN'T SEEM TO DIE

At the top of the Airspace Control Tower, they finally find the sibling and Cissia, alive (Cissia unconscious, the sibling with a few scratches). **Truvia** is waiting with them. The Proxy can only ask her why, and Truvia greets them: so they meet again.

**The Boss's letter.** Here, the chapter cuts back to Krampus headquarters, before the Roscaelifer assignment began. A voice the game labels only "???", the **Boss of Krampus**, tells Promeia to send Phoenix out, destination the Celestial Nexus, Roscaelifer. Promeia asks why Phoenix, and the Boss asks whether Phoenix's hobbies make her too much trouble to work with. Promeia has no problem with the clowning; whatever role Phoenix keeps playing, Promeia can accept it and might do the same in her place, always wanting to be anyone except herself. Her objection is that the targets' crimes don't warrant sending Phoenix. Someone Promeia refers to only as "he" once said that Phoenix should be kept out of operations unless absolutely necessary, since her power, the only thing that could be counted as a benefit of the **Sacrifice Project**, is dangerous and far too conspicuous. The Boss tells Promeia she has changed, if only slightly. Drawing attention is exactly what they need now. Promeia needn't concern herself with the **Three Pacts**, the three corporations at TOPS's round table (see "S1 · TOPS (The Outstanding Paragons Alliance)"): they gave up trying to capture Phoenix long ago, and as long as she lives, she gives them reason to cling to their delusions about the project. Besides, she is not easily killed. This time, Phoenix won't be passing judgment. She is a messenger: an era on the verge of its burial is crying out in a final lament, and as the curtain rises on a new age, she will deliver Krampus's letter to the stage and announce to the world that Krampus is about to make its entrance. The letter reads:

> If the world reaches its end, where shall we stand? Cast aside weakness and show no mercy. Blazing brimstone shall rain upon you. Thus proclaims the karmic fire that sears the skull. Woe. Woe to you who dwell upon the earth.

**The impaling.** As the scene cuts back to the tower over a black screen, Truvia picks up the letter's last words with a short laugh: "Woe to you." When the picture returns, she has run Phoenix through, and the Proxy demands to know what she has done. Phoenix goes down and stays down, and when Truvia later calls herself "someone who just killed your friend right in front of you", she means it. The conversation that follows is the heart of the chapter (see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)").

Phoenix doesn't stay dead. In the middle of the fight that comes after, Truvia brings Pyrois down on one knee and taunts the Proxy: is that all they've got? Then, Phoenix rises out of the flames, and Truvia, staring, asks how she can possibly still be alive. Phoenix apologises for being kind of hard to kill and announces that she has reached her verdict: Truvia is sentenced to burn in hellfire. She just can't stay dead, she says, nothing special, though now, she'll have to get serious. She understands why the Boss sent her: the Boss knew a freak like Truvia would be waiting. She calls Truvia a "purple eggplant" and tells her the Boss has a letter for her. Complaining that the Boss sure likes her poetry (fire this, calamity that), she translates it all into one sentence: today is the day Truvia dies. Mid-fight, she finds Truvia an interesting one and says she loves an opponent who doesn't go down easily. Truvia calls her a monster, and Phoenix tells her the feeling is mutual (see "S3 Ch4 · Pyrois Against the Blasphemer (Showdown with Truvia)").

This is the first time anyone in Roscaelifer sees the "unable to die" line of Phoenix's Agent Record in action. A wound that would kill anyone else only drains her stored Ether, and the reserves flare up and drag her back until she is on her feet again, looking delighted about it. The clumsy medical assistant from Amber Hall is gone, and in her place stands the Krampus Judge whose verdict, when the Boss sends her, is always the same one.

(Narration note: keep her tone bright and mocking while she's bleeding, and let the menace come through in what she says while her voice stays cheerful. The Boss of Krampus is a woman; see "NPC BG · The Boss of Krampus (Krampus Compliance Authority)".)

99.comment: S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)
99.content:
# TRUVIA · THE SPARE WHO WANTED TO BE THE SUN

**Interlude: Truvia and Youkai.** Between Youkai's call and the return to Booastrum, the chapter cuts to the two of them. Youkai, still wearing Serpico's face, announces that her big brother is back and asks whether she missed him, and **Truvia**, awake and in her own body, tells him to get lost. He protests that he just did her a huge favour, since her precious Phaethon got their invitation to the reunion, and she won't say it a third time. He coos that his sweet little sister is finally hitting her rebellious phase, and she threatens to find him a new body to wear and tells him not to say disgusting things to her with Serpico's face. Then, she asks how things are going on Mosseint's end. Youkai mocks her for calling her own father by his name, and she asks whether he believes what he is saying: her "creator"? Youkai concedes the point and calls the old geezer completely past his usefulness: "control the Rosetta Data, command Roscaelifer" was garbage he made up on the spot, and he never expected Mosseint to fall for something so stupid unless the man was going senile (for what became of Mosseint, see "NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)"). Truvia suggests Mosseint was like her, another willing pawn who chose to let Youkai use him, and Youkai insists Mosseint was the only one being used; between the two of them, it has always been a mutual arrangement. He thinks she is still a little too human for her own good: she always knew it was all fake and keeps clinging to boring ideals of fairness and justice when she had so many chances to simply kill them. When he offers to blow up the Proxy's airship on the way to Booastrum, she warns him that if he interferes, he will never get another word out of her about Carole Arna. Phaethon has to lose on a level playing field, because they will never accept a loss unless the conditions are fair. Youkai's advice, as an AI, is that the data shows obsessing over fairness is how people get outplayed and die like clowns, and that could be the two of them. She tells him he doesn't understand anything because he isn't human. He answers that he understands humans better than anyone, as trash who love lying to themselves, and asks whether that sounds right to her, "you thing still playing dress-up as a person". She tells him one last time to get lost, and he leaves her the stage and wishes her the ending she is looking for.

**At the sickbed.** The chapter then shows Truvia lying in a medical capsule, barely awake, with the man in Serpico's body leaning over her. She calls him "Brother" and talks as if they were still children at Helios: she had a long dream in which Serpico never moved, no matter what she said or did, as if he were dead, and she is relieved it was only a dream. Youkai plays Serpico's part. Only a dream, he agrees, and sooner or later, you always wake up; Belle and Wise just told him they are coming by soon to see her, with gifts. She sighs that yesterday, they lost to the twins in Miss Carole's test again, seventy-three losses in a row, and he tells her they'll get them next time. He asks whether she remembers why Icarus fell. She guesses arrogance, and he gives another answer: Icarus left his father and his companions behind and flew too far on his own, and as long as they stick together, they will never end up like him and will become the ones who "seize the sun". Truvia muses that the sun is only one ordinary star among the others, and in Icarus's time, nobody even knew what a star was. They are the same, she says, never told why they have to seize the sun and flying toward it anyway, though it may be too high to ever touch. When he asks whether she is all right, she wonders whether Icarus had a reason of his own, one nobody back then could call wrong or stop him for. What if she could fly higher than every star, even higher than the sun itself, and shine with a light nobody could replace and a heat beyond compare? Could she become the perfect, flawless sun? "Hmm, maybe," he says. Alone afterwards, Youkai drops the act. Such a brilliant child, poor little thing: she worked out long ago that Helios was nothing but a pair of wings made of wax and chose to look the other way, and she always knew the one who would fly toward the sun could never have been her. (The chapter doesn't say when this sickbed scene took place.)

**The confrontation.** At the top of the Airspace Control Tower, after she has run Phoenix through (see "S3 Ch4 · Sorry, I Just Can't Seem to Die (Phoenix Impaled)"), Truvia talks with Belle (or Wise), who is trying in vain to open a way out. She tells them not to waste their time, then compliments them: as a fellow child of Helios, the Proxy solved every riddle she set on the way up and found their way to her, just as she believed they would, since the children of Helios were born to unravel the riddles called Hollows. The Proxy had held on to the hope that this was all a misunderstanding; when Girtablullu impaled her, they thought they had lost a friend for good, so was all of it an act? She tells them it wasn't pretending, exactly: the creature disguised as Dracaene was supposed to be completely under her control, and she never expected it to have a will of its own and turn on her. After that, she simply played along. Shouldn't the Proxy be glad she survived? Perhaps they are disappointed, since a dead Truvia could have stayed exactly as they remembered her, theirs to reshape until only the good side remained, the way they have done with Miss Carole and Serpico?

She explains nothing about why she was waiting. The Proxy has forgotten too much, and she would rather let them die drowning in doubt and bitterness, as Serpico did and as she did. She does tell them about Mosseint. The Helios children were all children with nowhere else to go, while "Pa", she begins, and corrects herself to Mosseint, could have afforded any education he wanted, so why send his only children there? Because to him, they were never his children. They were bargaining chips for Helios Academy's technology, and to a rich man, two dead children meant little next to the promise of Artificial Enchainer technology, a concept he didn't even understand at the time; cutting-edge was enough.

The core beats of the conversation run like this:

Truvia: "When it comes to controlling Singularity Leakages... you've let your power rust for years. You can't possibly beat me after all the practice I've put in."

Truvia: "As long as I'm here... not even a Sunbringer will escape so easily."

Belle (or Wise): "Miss Carole... she was part of the Artificial Enchainer project too?"

Truvia: "Our eyes were central to one of Helios Academy's most important projects: ocular implants that would allow us to wield the power of Karma Cores and become Artificial Enchainers."

Truvia: "Clearly, you were the only one... the only one who walked away with the greatest prize, and yet... you pretend you know nothing about it?"

Truvia: "Sometimes, I honestly can't tell if you've actually lost your memory... or if you're just pretending."

Truvia: "What's wrong? You don't want to see your teacher's lifelong wish come true?"

Belle (or Wise): "Wait, is that why you came here? To take the Karma Cores from the Sunbringers?"

Belle (or Wise): "Miss Carole never told me any of this..."

What it adds up to rewrites Helios Academy. The smart eye implants given to the four top students of Carole Arna's class were the core of a project to turn children into **Artificial Enchainers** who could wield the power of a Karma Core, carrying the idea behind Project Sunseeker into a new generation, and Miss Carole was part of it (see "World BG · Project Sunseeker"). Truvia brushes off the three Sunbringers as people the Proxy barely knows, so what if they die, and asks whether the Proxy is still as arrogant as they were as a child, believing only they can make Miss Carole's wish come true. When the Proxy says Miss Carole would never have wanted this, Truvia agrees, and asks why Carole should get what she wanted.

The rest of what she says, in summary:

- Almost all her happy memories come from Helios, with Belle, Wise, Serpico and Miss Carole. Only Serpico could ever challenge the Proxy for first place, while she was always behind and hardly anyone bothered to compare her with the rest. She didn't care, because she had a family and felt alive.
- The Proxy starts to beg her to stop before they do something they can't take back, and breaks off mid-sentence. Truvia pounces on the silence: she has just killed the Proxy's friend in front of them, so why not finish? They could tell her she can let go and become a good person, that she is forgiven and they will save her. Why won't they say it? Once you set foot on certain paths, she says, there is no going back, and Miss Carole was the same.
- She calls everything Miss Carole gave them cruel lies. The only person Carole ever cared about was the Proxy, her number one, and the other children were spares kept in reserve in case something happened to them. As a rich kid, Truvia didn't even qualify as a spare. Once they threw her away, she crawled home only to be sent somewhere even worse, and all the happiness of Helios had a price attached from the start.
- Only the Proxy inherited Helios's legacy and was worthy of its true mission, so today, she will take everything from them anyway: their eyes, and the boundaries they never dared to cross.
- She could claim Helios was a mistake she means to correct, or that Carole chose the wrong person and Truvia is superior and should be the one to fulfil Carole's wish, but none of that matters. Just as she thought, the two of them are the same as they always were, believing that beating each other will make every problem disappear. Before she takes the Sunbringers' Karma Core fragments and steps into the territory the Proxy was afraid of, she will beat them fair and square, to honour Serpico's memory and to bury the lie known as Helios.

The Proxy tells her she is no longer the Truvia they knew. There is so much they still want to ask her, but it will have to wait: they all have to answer for what they've done, whether it is Helios's legacy, the Karma Core fragments or whatever else she is after, and it ends here. Then, the Proxy sees what Truvia has brought with her for a "fair fight" (see "S3 Ch4 · Pyrois Against the Blasphemer (Showdown with Truvia)").

(Narration note: the mythology is deliberate. Helios is the sun, and Phaethon is the son of the sun who borrowed its chariot and fell. Icarus flew toward the sun on wax wings until they melted. At Helios Academy, Serpico and Truvia were partners in a team codenamed "Icarus", while the Proxy goes by Phaethon, and the chapter casts Truvia as the Icarus who flew on alone. When Youkai plays Serpico at her sickbed, keep him gentle and convincing, and let the coldness show only once she can no longer hear him. Several lines in this chapter hint that this Truvia may not be the same girl the twins knew at Helios, and the chapter never settles it; see "NPC BG · Truvia Mosseint (child & adult)".)

100.comment: S3 Ch4 · Pyrois Against the Blasphemer (Showdown with Truvia)
100.content:
# PYROIS AGAINST THE BLASPHEMER · SHOWDOWN WITH TRUVIA

Even before the talking starts, Truvia has the top of the tower sealed. When the Proxy tries to open a Singularity Leakage, nothing happens, and Truvia tells them not to bother: they have let their power rust for years, and as long as she is there, even a Sunbringer would struggle to escape. She has wrapped the arena in leakage-warped space that she controls, so Lindverne and Severian can't find a way in, and only the Proxy and Phoenix end up in the fight with her.

When the conversation ends, the Proxy sees what Truvia has brought and demands to know what happened to her. She calls it a fair fight and says it is time to send the Proxy to another world. Then, she explains herself: when Girtablullu killed her, she says, she felt sorry for it. If they are destined to be tools, destined to be culled, why give them a sense of self at all? One day, she swears, they will drag the victors down from the heavens and take back everything that was stolen from them. She brings out her **Etheric Other**, the counterpart to Pyrois, born from the same Helios experiment and the same kind of eyes, and Belle (or Wise) answers with Pyrois. The duel turns into Ethereal against Ethereal, each fighting beside the child it grew inside the way a stand fights beside its user, with the Proxy's strikes called out in the cutscenes as "Scorching sun" and "Feel the blade with me. Annihilation." Truvia's practice shows from the first exchange: she bends Singularity Leakages far more fluently than the Proxy ever has, and she soon has Pyrois down on one knee and taunts the Proxy with "Is that all you've got?"

The game shows the boss only as **Blasphemer** until the chapter's secret-room episode has been cleared, and afterwards its record names it **Etheric Other - Truvia**, a Notorious Boss filed among the Ether Mutants' Ethereals. Its intel paints her as an empty shell running on hatred and paranoia, a zealot who has lost her god. Armed with an Etheric Other that came from Helios Academy, she waits at the top of the tower for an old friend and a final reckoning. It fights first in human form with a longsword, fast at close range, with a few heavy techniques that call for a Chain Parry. At set moments, it shifts into a **mermaid form** and flips its grip to wield the longsword as a staff. Then, it drags its opponent into the Singularity Leakage, where it raises a Corruptive Barrier and attacks in concert with spatial tricks and clones of itself. It is weak to fire and resists ice.

Then, Phoenix gets back up from the wound that killed her and joins in, delivering the Boss's letter and her verdict of hellfire (see "S3 Ch4 · Sorry, I Just Can't Seem to Die (Phoenix Impaled)"). Phoenix has the upper hand, her flames biting where the Etheric Other is weakest, but the Proxy can see they can't let the fight drag on against power like Truvia's. Pyrois names the answer, the **Ether Level Limiter**, and when the Proxy asks what it said, it reminds them that "the small Sunbringer" gave it to them: the gun Dracaene invented and handed over after the Proxy's Pyrois treatment, made to keep an Etheric Other in check (see "S3 Ch1 · Taming the Beast (Pyrois)"). Remembering the gun that can suppress Etheric Others, Belle (or Wise) tells Phoenix they have a plan and asks her to keep Truvia pinned down for a second. Phoenix holds her, and the Proxy takes the now-or-never shot. At first, it seems to do nothing, and the Proxy reasons that against an Etheric Other it should still work, while Truvia starts to claim the Proxy's legacy as her own. Then, the shot takes effect. Truvia can hardly believe it can be that simple. As the others realise it worked, she curses and admits she has **lost control of her Etheric Other**.

The Proxy tells her it all ends here. Truvia agrees that it ends here, for now, and tells Belle (or Wise) that they will settle it in **the New World**. Then, she is gone. Phoenix complains that she was just getting warmed up and admits she can't fight back at the moment, so the others may do their worst to her as long as they don't tickle her; the Proxy decides that if she can still crack jokes, she is fine. Afterwards, the sibling works out that Truvia was manipulating the space inside the leakage the whole time, which is why Lindverne couldn't get through, and credits the Proxy with keeping her pinned down.

The fight is the emotional climax of the climb. Every clash between Pyrois and Truvia's Etheric Other replays the day at Helios Academy that ended with Serpico's death, with the difference that this time, both children brought their monsters on purpose. Truvia survives it, and so do her grudge and her plans, since she is back for the very end of the chapter (see "S3 Ch4 · The Hive Lord Hollow Swallows the Sky (End of Chapter 4)").

(Narration note: render Pyrois as described in "S3 Ch1 · Taming the Beast (Pyrois)", cold blue and violet with gold on its heaviest strikes. For Truvia's Etheric Other, use the two forms above, the longsword-wielding human shape and the mermaid shape with the reversed blade held as a staff, and keep finer detail to silhouette and motion, such as the rifts it opens and the clones that flicker around it, along with the damage it leaves behind.)

101.comment: S3 Ch4 · Dreams and Dawn Still Come (After the Showdown)
101.content:
# DREAMS AND DAWN STILL COME · AFTER THE SHOWDOWN

When the leakage around the fight collapses, Lindverne apologises for not getting through; the space inside was too chaotic to find a way out. The sibling realises Truvia was manipulating it the whole time and credits the Proxy with keeping her pinned down during the fight. Truvia got away, Lindverne says, and the pursuit can wait. What matters now is the secret chamber, where Eldreda should be. The Proxy proposes splitting up: Cissia is still unconscious and the sibling and Phoenix are pretty weak, so the Proxy will stay with Severian to look after them. Severian agrees, since keeping Cissia safe is one of his objectives anyway and the others need protection, too. Phoenix asks him whether he isn't scared, and he assures "Miss Phoenix" that he doesn't prey on the weak or strike someone who can't fight back. The Proxy leaves the chamber to Lindverne, and Lindverne asks them to come with her. The Proxy hesitates, since it isn't a place an outsider should go waltzing into. Lindverne answers that it is hardly waltzing in when a Sunbringer invites you, as Dracaene would say, too, and asks whether the Proxy doesn't want to go. Phoenix tells the Proxy that Lindverne has made it pretty clear she wants them there and promises, between coughs, to keep everyone safe, and the sibling tells them to go ahead. Severian promises to look after the others and sends them off to the matter at hand. Asked whether he isn't even a little curious about the truth behind the Rosetta Data, he declines to come, since order endures precisely because there are things each of us doesn't know. He has already encountered far more than he was ever meant to, and the first lesson the City Administration taught him was to suppress his own curiosity.

Before they leave, the twins have a moment. The sibling is fine apart from a few scratches, because Cissia protected them, and they agree to treat Cissia to her favourite egg rice rolls when she wakes up, or, since Roscaelifer might not sell those, to her second favourite, egg tarts.

**The door.** At the mechanism that opens the way, Lindverne is lost in thought and admits she is getting nervous now that they have reached the final step: she still doesn't know how to face Eldreda, or the secret they have protected for so long. The Proxy tells her not to overthink it, since they will find the answer once they meet Lady Eldreda, and promises to stay by her side. The entrance is hidden so well that the Proxy wonders whether they are still inside the control tower, and Lindverne thinks so. A voice echoes out of the past, saying something about a price that must be paid; the Proxy takes it for Lady Eldreda, and Lindverne isn't sure it is her at all. A path opens for them through the Porcelloy, all the way to a huge door encased in it. Lindverne wonders what the chamber was built for and can hardly believe she has never been here before, because the closer she gets, the more she is overwhelmed by sadness, and the Proxy feels it, too. She asks the Proxy whether she should open it, afraid that whatever lies beyond won't be what they hoped for. They may find nothing at all or lose something they already have, and once the door opens, there is no turning back. The Proxy reminds her they came to uncover the truth and promises to face whatever is behind the door with her. Lindverne decides that whether she regrets it is a problem for future Lindverne, and the Proxy recognises the Lindverne they know (see "S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)").

key: Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room
102.comment: S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)
102.content:
# WHO IS TRAPPED IN THE SECRET ROOM · THE SECRET CHAMBER

Inside stands what looks like a statue encased in Porcelloy, holding something that looks like an Ether core. In front of it is **Eldreda Sunbringer**, who greets the Proxy as a child of Helios who should not have come here, however long and hard the way must have been. Lindverne realises Eldreda has been here this entire time and asks whether she even knows what has been happening. Of course, she knows, Eldreda answers; the one who knows nothing is Lindverne. Lindverne pours out everything: TOPS stole Claret's Porcelloy and used it to make tools for controlling Enchainer larvae, Dracaene's Karma Core has been taken and she still hasn't woken up. Eldreda didn't know about Dracaene and apologises, and Lindverne snaps back: then what did she realise? The Proxy decides to let her get it all out. Lindverne knows Eldreda carries a heavier mantle than the rest of them and is always looking toward the future, and begs her, just this once, to stop looking so far ahead and look down at the Booastrum beneath their feet. What could be so important that she is still hiding it? Aren't they all Sunbringers?

Eldreda tells them the truth. They are all Sunbringers, and that is exactly why she kept it from them: she didn't want them to share the fate every Sunbringer is destined to bear, the fate of their mother, the first Sunbringer. Lindverne believed, as everyone did, that their mother split herself into the three of them. Eldreda believed it, too, until, after "that incident", she found the courage to open this door and learned that everything was built on a lie their mother left behind: **the lie called the Sunbringers**.

- **The first Sunbringer never left.** What she divided into three was only her Karma Core. The statue is the first Sunbringer herself.
- **What she holds is a Hollow.** The Proxy reads the pattern and amplitude of its energy and realises the "Ether core" is a Hollow: **the Hive Lord Hollow**, one of the seven Great Hollows, hidden since Roscaelifer's founding. It is the true source of the Rosetta Data and the sisters' true homeland.
- **The great lie.** Lindverne protests that the first Sunbringer eliminated the Hive Lord Hollow before the old capital was founded. Eldreda believed that, too, as everyone did, and believed in their mother as the hero who destroyed it. The so-called destruction was another lie built around the Sunbringer name, to make the people of Eridu believe that under the Void Hunters' leadership, they could one day dissolve the Hollows and reclaim their homeland, and New Eridu still believes it. The Hollow stayed hidden inside Roscaelifer all along and became the beacon guiding humanity's exploration of the Hollows.
- **The Rosetta Data.** It is the raw Ether information stream drawn straight from the Hive Lord Hollow in its current state, which the CCD then decodes and processes.
- **The split.** As the former Hive Lord, their mother could control the Hollow's size and confine it to this safe, usable state, which went directly against her instincts as an Enchainer. That is why she split her Karma Core into three and why the three of them were born. She became an Enchainer who was no longer an Enchainer, an empty shell, and the world would never again see a complete Hive Lord. She forged shackles of Porcelloy to keep her body from mutating after losing her core, trapping herself here forever and turning herself into kindling for the Rosetta Data. Lindverne begs her to stop, and Eldreda tells her this is the truth she asked for: their mother left this world to keep the lighthouse burning, and in return, she gave them life.

**How Eldreda found out.** She has known for a few months. The Exaltists brought about the Creator's descent in the Lemnian Hollow during the events with Xiao'Guang. It lasted only an instant, but it stirred every Great Hollow to some degree, the Hive Lord Hollow included, and the Rosetta Data turned unreliable for no apparent reason for about half a month. Dracaene's team investigated and couldn't find the source, and once Eldreda had ruled out every other possibility, she was sure something had gone wrong with the source in this chamber. She broke the half-forgotten promise and opened the door that night. She then had the CCD run precise calculations under another pretext: if nothing changed, their mother's restraints on the Hive Lord Hollow would last two or three more months at most, unless someone could do once again what she had done.

So Eldreda has been here doing it. She holds only a third of the Karma Core and can never match her mother's perfection, but she believed she could hold out until reinforcements arrived from New Eridu, and if the worst came to pass, find a way to borrow her sisters' Karma Cores. That is what opening Roscaelifer to the outside world and the research she commissioned from Claret's team were for. Lindverne asks whether she even knows what she is doing, and Eldreda answers that she is only doing what their mother once did. She never imagined that Carinus' obsession with the Sunbringers would drive things this far.

Lindverne tells her that isn't the point. Why can't Eldreda trust her and Dracaene a little more? Lindverne doesn't believe in a predetermined fate, but if this is a Sunbringer's true responsibility and mission, they can share the burden. Eldreda answers with a memory. When she first met Carinus, he told her that of the three, only she had inherited Sunbringer's appearance completely. It may have been a casual remark, and it stirred two feelings she had never known: a simple, childlike joy, as if Sunbringer herself had praised her and she was the favourite, and a sense of duty, as if she had been chosen to become the next Sunbringer. She didn't know what to do with it, so she followed in her mother's footsteps, trying to match every step of that distant, unreachable figure, and walked that path so long she nearly forgot the people following behind her and walking beside her. She doesn't regret choosing it.

Lindverne always thought she was the one who was bad at this sort of thing, and finds that Eldreda is even worse. Eldreda laughs and apologises for the trouble she has caused, and Lindverne tells her it is too early for apologies: once they have dealt with High Ambitions and taken back Roscaelifer and Dracaene's Karma Core, she can apologise properly to everyone. Eldreda agrees, and adds that if they can't find another solution for the Rosetta Data, she will still carry out her duty. Lindverne corrects her: **our** duty, and Eldreda shouldn't think she can ever ditch her and Dracaene again. Then, Lindverne remembers one more thing: if Eldreda keeps secrets from them again, she'll see what happens. Eldreda knows.

As the sisters talk, the statue's eye lights up. The first Sunbringer tells the Proxy to stop glaring at her like that and suggests they give her daughters some space and have a little chat of their own (see "S3 Ch4 · Sleepwalkers' Dialogue (The First Sunbringer's Farewell)").

(This is the "true Lady Sunbringer, imprisoned in endless darkness" that the En-Nah Gang's Databoo glimpsed while processing the Rosetta Data; see "S3 Ch2 · The Wolf of Gear Street".)

103.comment: S3 Ch4 · Sleepwalkers' Dialogue (The First Sunbringer's Farewell)
103.content:
# SLEEPWALKERS' DIALOGUE · THE FIRST SUNBRINGER'S FAREWELL

Belle (or Wise) finds themselves somewhere else, greeted by a Bangboo who has been sleepwalking here for a very long time and has never been good at names, so it settles on **Sleepwalkerboo** (the game's name tag keeps a question mark after it). The Proxy finds that a little random, and the Bangboo insists it put a lot of thought into it. Asked whether that means the Proxy is sleepwalking, too, it says yes and no, and promises to explain one piece at a time. The narration calls it the dreamchaser wandering into the sleepwalker's dream.

Together, they walk through a Roscaelifer built from her memories and wishes, and at each stop, she shows the Proxy one of her daughters, first as a girl she might have been and then as the woman she became. Each stop closes on a line of the same refrain.

- **Dracaene.** The first stop is **Aurelia Academy**, where the others are already waiting. A schoolgirl Dracaene chases a golden beetle with her classmates, sure she will catch it today, until the bell rings, her classmates call her in, and she stops. The Proxy guesses that Dracaene was once a student here who caught beetles with her friends, and Sleepwalkerboo allows that it was at least once a possible path for her; in the end, she never came back to it. The Dracaene the Proxy knows is the one at the CCD, going over the points of a Bangboo Logic Core upgrade proposal with Norma, who shed her innocence and naivety long ago to become the most dependable helmsman of the Celestial Nexus. Sleepwalkerboo admits she may be the only one who still longs for the girl who never existed. ("And just like that, time flows endlessly on, carrying away the childhood she never had.")
- **Lindverne.** On **Beckford Street**, a young Lindverne yells at a little menace to stop right there while a distressed citizen shouts that the little brat has stolen their wallet. For a moment, the Proxy takes Lindverne for the thief, until the Tin Master who runs Cuppa Moment thanks Miss Lindverne for sparing the customers from a pickpocket and she tells the thief that nobody pulls that sort of thing on her street. That tough street kid is another path, and in the end, she, too, chose a different one. The Lindverne who exists is the one at the Airspace Patrol, decisive and considerate, announcing a new patrol rotation that pairs humans with Bangboo to cut Booastrum's patrol blind spots by another fifteen percent and give everyone about ten percent more rest. To Sleepwalkerboo, there is no "real" Lindverne. She is simply herself, the one who leaps to help others and acts without hesitation, and only Lindverne decides who she will become, though in the sleepwalker's eyes, she will always be that bright, strong child. The Proxy starts to suspect who they are talking to, and the Bangboo apologises for saying too much: whenever she talks about them, she can't help herself. All three stopped being the children she remembers long ago; their own choices and the people and Bangboo they met have blossomed into something of their own in this city in the sky. ("And just like that, the wind of the past sweeps by, stealing away memories that were never hers to keep.")
- **Eldreda.** At CCD Square, someone is singing and playing guitar well enough to be a professional, and it is Eldreda, performing in the street; the Proxy has to remind themselves they are dreaming. Then, they see the Eldreda everyone knows, giving a speech: the lighthouse still stands because they have stood shoulder to shoulder, and from here, its light will reach farther still, until the night itself is ended. Her voice never changed, says Sleepwalkerboo, only what it meant to those who heard it, a tender song or a commanding declaration. Eldreda is the most like the first Sunbringer, which makes people expect more of her, and she took after her mother in trying to carry everything alone, using her sacrifice as a way to avoid the problems she has never been willing to face. As a leader, though, she has far more presence than her mother ever did; the sleepwalker could never stand before a crowd and give an inspiring speech without stumbling over every word. Then, she shares a secret about Eldreda: she marks the tone and emphasis of every single line in her speeches because she is so afraid of saying something wrong. Anyone who knows something that personal can only be one person, and the Proxy says so. ("And just like that, a song at dusk carries the daylight away.")

The Proxy asks why, if she could see everything in Roscaelifer from here all this time, she did nothing but remember and bear witness. This is only a dream, the original Sunbringer says. Her last stop is the Interboo statue on CCD Square, at night and empty. Bangboo always loved to play here, and little by little the people who loved Bangboo gathered, too, so in her memory, it was always lively; when morning comes, she says, the real square will be bustling again. The Proxy talks about coming here with their sibling to listen to the Bangboo sing and about the gorgeous view of Emerald Central Park from up there. Then, there is the chessboard where you can always find Bangboo playing, and the Proxy apologises for going off on a tangent. She loves hearing how much the Proxy loves Roscaelifer. The Proxy notices she doesn't look happy, and she admits it: the utopia she longs for is in desperate need of saving. The Proxy tells her not to worry, since they took Roscaelifer back together and Lindverne and the others will make things right. She agrees that she believes in them, in every person and every Bangboo of Roscaelifer, and always will. The trouble is that the crisis is not over and has only just begun. Her warning may already come too late, or may not even be needed, and still, before the last light goes out, she wants to do something for her daughters one last time. She gives them her blessings:

- **Dracaene**, wise and clear-headed: may her wisdom part the fog of the unknown so people can see the path ahead.
- **Lindverne**, fearless, with a heart full of courage: may her passion keep the flame burning so the long cold night never feels endless again.
- **Eldreda**, her most steadfast, devoted child: may her sense of duty no longer leave her standing alone, and may they love her as deeply as she loves them, since she would give everything for their sake.

She hopes each of them stands by the choices they made, which she believes were right ones that would make her proud. If they ever reject one another's decisions, though, Roscaelifer's very existence will become a mistake, just like her, a mistake that should never have existed. The Proxy names her, **Lady Sunbringer**, and she appears as herself, asking whether her dear Proxy is a little disappointed; the Proxy had started to think she wasn't going to show up. One mistake and one crisis, she confirms: the mistake dates back more than a century to the very beginning of Helios Academy, and the crisis is about to erupt on Roscaelifer and across New Eridu.

**Her story.** When Professor Arche had just founded Helios Academy, she had just come into being. She is the Enchainer of the Hive Lord Hollow, the one people once called the Hive Lord, but she began as an **Enchainer larva**, much like Girtablullu. The law of the Hive Lord Hollow was survival of the fittest, and whoever defeated the Hive Lord would become the next one. She challenged the Hive Lord and lost, yet she did not die. She seized a portion of the Hive Lord's power and used it to flee her homeland. Ordinary Ethereals can't leave Hollows, and an Enchainer can only do it for a short time, at the cost of being badly weakened. She was at death's door when Arche found her and brought her to Helios Academy. Professor Arche gained a new protégé, and Helios Academy a new researcher named Sunbringer.

Without a complete Karma Core, she could only use a fraction of the Hive Lord's power. Even her daughters mistake the Hive Lord's authority for a power of creation; the truth behind **Genesis Reconstruction** is **dream manifestation**, the ability to give thoughts physical form. She didn't know what it was or how to use it, and by the time she noticed, she had become human, or at least looked human. She had seen so many people in Eridu and at Helios Academy, and compared with a Hollow where the strong prey on the weak, their world seemed better; she wanted to live in it alongside them, and one has to be a person to live in Eridu. Arche spent a long time teaching her to hide what she was and control her Ethereal instincts so she could live as a human, and Arche gave her the name Sunbringer, one who brings light to the world. She wonders whether he was already thinking of Project Sunseeker then, and the Proxy recognises the name from Remielle. Remielle will never forget it, she says, and will never forgive her.

**Project Sunseeker.** The Void Hunters had defeated every other Enchainer and still could neither control nor dissolve the Great Hollows. Arche's plan was to use her as the prototype and blueprint for the theoretical groundwork, then use the Karma Cores inside the Void Hunters' weapons as the medium that would let the Void Hunters fully activate that power and evolve into **Artificial Enchainers**. How it ended, Remielle has already told the Proxy. Arche grew more and more obsessed until he vanished into Hollow Zero and never came back. She finished building Roscaelifer and the true prototype of the Rosetta Data. Perhaps they had already lost their last chance to conquer the Hollows, or destroyed it with their own hands, but she could still set a lighthouse aglow in the skies above Eridu, to show those lost in the dark the way forward even if she could never dispel every shadow. She never expected that nearly a century later, **a successor to Helios would complete Arche's plan**.

The Proxy admits none of that means anything to them yet. She won't explain the rest (Ether, Hollows, Enchainers, even the Creator). The Proxy will learn it at the end of a long journey that will give the truth its own meaning, and she will not be the one to tell them, since it would only cloud their judgment. She calls her last request the dying wish of an old soul with one foot in the grave. She could ask the Proxy to do what a Proxy does and connect people, as their resonance has connected the two of them, or to carry out Helios's final wish and share their light and warmth with the utopia beyond the horizon, but neither feels right. Her request is simpler: do what they believe is right, the only wish she had for her daughters when they were born. When the Proxy asks whether that will be enough, she tells them not to underestimate themselves. They are the final legacy of Helios and also a Proxy, someone who bridges reality and the Hollows as the only mediator between their conflicting laws. The identity of a Proxy is never as simple as it looks, least of all in the Proxy's case.

She also leaves a message for Remielle, whose presence the Proxy carries so strongly that it keeps urging her to speak: **she does not need to forgive her.** That is all. When the Proxy asks whether she is leaving, she asks whether that was too brief a farewell from someone already dead, or whether they are worried about Roscaelifer's future, and the Proxy admits it is a little of both. She starts to pass on something Remielle once told her about the fear that the Hollows would swallow everything they built. Running out of time, she says Remielle can tell the Proxy herself. As for Roscaelifer, over the past century, it has endured hardship after hardship without once begging a dead, century-old Enchainer to save it; its people are already doing what she never could, saving themselves with their own hands. She thanks the Proxy for walking this final stretch with her and staying to the end of an old sleepwalker's confession. It has been a long goodbye, she says, more than a hundred years long.

Her farewell gift is a riddle: why do Bangboo have such long ears? Because they are just so adorable. (Remielle, who once suggested those rabbit ears in Meridian Hall, would have something to say about that.) Within a sleepwalker's dream, another dreamer awakens, and the Proxy comes back to the chamber thinking that wasn't quite the answer they expected.

The farewell ties the whole of Season 3 together, since the titles of Chapter 1, "A Sleepwalker's Confession", and Chapter 2, "The Long Goodbye", both turn out to have been about her.

(Narration note: play the Sleepwalkerboo form of the original Sunbringer in flashbacks as warm, shy and a little clumsy with words, a mother who never learned to give speeches and is doing her best to say goodbye properly.)

104.comment: S3 Ch4 · The Hive Lord Hollow Swallows the Sky (End of Chapter 4)
104.content:
# THE HIVE LORD HOLLOW SWALLOWS THE SKY

The Proxy wakes in the chamber just as the ground starts to shake. The Ether concentration around them is rising fast, and the **Hive Lord Hollow** can no longer hold its stability: with the first Sunbringer's goodbye said, her century-old restraint on it is giving way. Then, a familiar voice greets his dear friends, who surely miss him already even though they haven't been apart for long. **Youkai**, still wearing Serpico's face, walks in with **Truvia** beside him, and **Bashmu**, the larva carrying Dracaene's Karma Core fragment, comes roaring in with them. Youkai has come for what he left behind here, which he says he ought to retrieve himself.

**Eldreda** tells the others to go and leave this to her. Lindverne won't allow it, and Eldreda casts Lindverne and the Proxy away from the top of the tower while she turns to face the three of them. Falling toward the opening Hollow, Lindverne cries out to her sister that they promised to face this together. The Proxy calls on Pyrois, knowing they are about to fall into the Hollow, and cries out for Remielle. **Remielle** catches them in mid-air, pleased to have made it just in time. As the Proxy asks whether they are dreaming, Roscaelifer is being swallowed by the Hollow it was built around.

## STATE OF THE WORLD AT THE END OF SEASON 3 CHAPTER 4

- **The first Sunbringer** has said her goodbyes in the Proxy's dream. Her message for Remielle ("she does not need to forgive me") is still with the Proxy. Her body in the Secret Chamber was presumably destroyed in the blast that followed.
- **The Hive Lord Hollow** broke loose and is swallowing Roscaelifer's upper levels, Booastrum included.
- **Eldreda** stayed in the Secret Chamber to face Youkai and Truvia, with Bashmu at their side, after sending Lindverne and the Proxy clear of the tower. Whether she survived, and whether she still holds her Karma Core fragment, is unknown.
- **Lindverne** survived with her fragment, caught in mid-air by Remielle together with the Proxy.
- **Dracaene** is still unconscious in Vyrium, and her fragment is still inside Bashmu. The Ether Level Limiter she invented and gave the Proxy is what broke Truvia's control over her Etheric Other.
- **Youkai and Truvia** came out of the chapter on top. Truvia controls Singularity Leakages at will and has an Etheric Other of her own, and she promised to settle things with the Proxy in "the New World". Together, they killed **Mosseint**, head of High Ambitions Corp. and the "Lead Scepter" among TOPS's Three Pacts, and when Carinus tried to negotiate, Youkai, still wearing Serpico's face, invited "the late Mr. Mosseint" to weigh in and showed Carinus the corpse. Youkai also brags that Mosseint swallowed a plan he made up on the spot (see "NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)").
- **High Ambitions Corp.** lost its head and was routed from Quietude Isle and most of Booastrum, though its remnants and the Ethereals in the tower fought to the end.
- **Carinus**, who let TOPS in, is in temporary dormancy at the top of the tower and needs comprehensive repairs.
- **The sibling, Cissia, Phoenix and Severian** were last at the top of the Airspace Control Tower, with Cissia unconscious and the sibling and Phoenix weak, when the Hollow began to swallow Booastrum. Their situation is unknown.
- **Sigrid and Roxy** left the tower before the end, with Sigrid escorting the anaemic Roxy toward Vyrium.
- **Booastrum** was mostly retaken by the Airspace Patrol before the Hollow broke loose, with the injured in medical care and Cora's CCD staff told to evacuate.
- **Vyrium** holds Claret, Promeia, the Cunning Hares (Anby recovering) and the unconscious Dracaene.
- **New Eridu** has quietly intervened: Mayor Mayflower sent Severian with authority to execute whoever stands behind Mosseint, and the Boss of Krampus sent Phoenix as a messenger announcing that Krampus is about to make its entrance.
- **Carole Arna** is no longer simply the teacher the twins remember. According to Truvia, she was part of the Artificial Enchainer project and cared only for the Proxy, her "number one", and the first Sunbringer says a successor to Helios has completed Professor Arche's plan.

> **The sleepwalker has said her long goodbye, and the city of miracles is falling into the Hollow it was built around. Eldreda's last stand is the question hanging over everything that comes next.**

105.comment: Side Quest · Astra-nomical Moment (Astra Yao's Special Episode, v1.4–1.5)
105.content:
# ASTRA-NOMICAL MOMENT · ASTRA YAO'S SPECIAL EPISODE

A New Year's special episode built entirely around the legacy of the late singer Joran de Winter, and the story that fills in why Astra Yao sings at all.

Astra is preparing a memorial concert at Starloop Tower, the same stage Joran once performed on, and she wants one thing for it: "Joran's Legacy", a rumoured recording of his final performance, which was given at a small, now-demolished Sixth Street music store called The Gramophone. The search takes Astra and the Proxy into the Ballet Twins Hollow to recover the tape.

The concert itself becomes a trap. Thugs hired through Fugue storm Starloop Tower mid-event, and the mastermind is revealed to be Lady Tessa de Winter, Joran's widow. Her plan is to crash the flying Starloop Tower outright and kill Astra and the audience she blames for abandoning her husband, along with the Odeum HAE and Fugue staff. In her own words, the spectators and the labels are all murderers who drove Joran to his death, and so is the fickle public.

She is stopped by Evelyn Chevalier. Evelyn had been planted at Astra's side as a Fugue operative under deep cover, and chooses Astra over her employers, breaking with Fugue for good to protect her.

In the epilogue, Evelyn takes Astra to a Sixth Street parking lot, all that remains of The Gramophone, and the two of them work out that they were both in the audience at Joran's last show years earlier without knowing each other. Astra has the recovered recording published so that every fan can finally hear it, and asks Qingyi to deliver the master copy to Lady de Winter, now in Public Security custody and on suicide watch, in the hope that the music might one day reach her grief the way it once reached a frightened child in a shelter.

106.comment: Side Quest · Tales of Midsummer Dreams (Summer 2025, v2.1)
106.content:
# TALES OF MIDSUMMER DREAMS · SUMMER 2025

The summer event of Version 2.1, "The Impending Crash of Waves," set at Fantasy Resort in the Throne Quarter.

The Spook Shack crew (Ukinami Yuzuha, Alice Thymefield and Komano Manato) hand Belle and Wise a set of free vouchers and drag them out to the coast for a holiday. What they find is a resort in trouble: Therese, who recently inherited the place from her late father, is watching her business die. The Spook Shack takes on short-term management rights and sets out to revive it, with the caretaker Ege, the staffer Mia and her grandfather Ahab rounding out the local cast, and Lucy and Grace Howard turning up as fellow vacationers. Ege is at the resort's reception to assist with guest inquiries and help this ragtag crew out with keeping the resort afloat.

The event runs as three threads: the central mystery of the resort's "haunting," Alice's surfing exhibition, and Yuzuha's hunt for a mermaid. All three end at the Fantasy Music Festival, and the resort comes out of it alive.

107.comment: Side Quest · Midsummer Fantasy — The Haunted Resort (Summer 2025)
107.content:
# MIDSUMMER FANTASY · THE HAUNTED RESORT

This is the main story of the 2025 summer holiday.

The Spook Shack has barely started rebuilding Fantasy Resort's visitor numbers with surfing and fishing as well as shooting when the guests start fleeing. Word spreads that the resort is haunted, and tourists report ghostly apparitions on the grounds.

Combing the resort with Yuzuha and Alice, the Proxy finds that the ghosts are holographic projections thrown by hidden, stealth-coated projectors planted around the property. The man behind them is Willis, a manager from Three Gates Corp.'s military tech R&D division, who is using experimental holographic and stealth hardware to wreck the resort's reputation for his own gain.

The confrontation lands at the Fantasy Music Festival. Willis shows up with a media crew in tow, intending to humiliate the resort publicly, and instead has the whole scheme exposed on a live broadcast. Public Security carts his hired thugs away. Three Gates Corp. disavows him within the hour, terminating and blacklisting him for malicious interference with the resort's operations. Alice notes drily that this is exactly what TOPS corporations always do: they never miss a beat when it comes to cutting ties.

Therese, who had half-believed her father's resort really was cursed, is left in tears of relief. The festival goes ahead.

108.comment: Side Quest · Windrider, Wavebreaker (Alice's Summer 2025 Story)
108.content:
# WINDRIDER, WAVEBREAKER · ALICE'S SUMMER STORY

To pull attention back to Fantasy Resort, the crew books Alice Thymefield for a surfing exhibition, filmed live by an NEBC television crew.

The problem surfaces immediately: Alice, flawless on the water when she is alone, has performance anxiety and freezes in front of an audience. Yuzuha and Lucy put her through an improvised confidence-building "special training" regimen, with Lucy mentoring her, and the breakthrough arrives comically: Alice's blunt, unvarnished real personality finally bursting out from under the noble poise.

Rumours and a troublemaker named Jacqueline nearly derail the livestream, but Alice rides it out and performs. The arc also fills in her backstory: her clean, focused style on a board comes straight from her late father, Lionel Thymefield, who taught her both to surf and to fence.

109.comment: Side Quest · A Mermaid Dream (Yuzuha's Summer 2025 Story)
109.content:
# A MERMAID DREAM · YUZUHA'S SUMMER STORY

A strange old man at the resort's shooting stall hands Yuzuha a videotape called "Legends of the Deep," and she becomes utterly fixated on the mermaid it promises.

The old man turns out to be Ahab, grandfather of the resort staffer Mia. The group charters a deep-sea sightseeing trip on Yuzuha's insistence, and a tail does surface. It belongs to a Sharkboo, a Bangboo, which makes it one more piece of Ahab's endless tall tales.

Ahab's showmanship covers a sad history: he was once a sea captain who lost his family to his own obsessive pursuit of mermaids, and the stories are what he has left of it. He eventually gives up the real location where he claims to have seen one, and the group gets its legendary mermaid moment after all.

Yuzuha ends the arc content, back at the aquarium she loves, remembering a children's game from her Sailume Bay childhood called "Net's Up, Net's Down".

110.comment: Side Quest · The Angels of Delusion's Official Channel
110.content:
# THE ANGELS OF DELUSION'S OFFICIAL CHANNEL

Alongside their stage work at the 404 Livehouse, the Angels of Delusion run their own official channel, and they run it entirely themselves, three idols with a camera and more enthusiasm than planning.

Posts are signed by whoever is speaking, using a personal marker each: a sparkle for Aria, headphones for Sunna, a black heart for Nangong Yu. Their audience is always addressed as the "Delulus" and videos usually open on the group's chirped catchphrase, "Hello~ We are the Angels of Delusion."

Several running bits have become fixtures of the channel:

- **The Unfinished Group Introduction**: Their official self-introduction is permanently a work in progress, and they promise to keep revising it, probably forever.
- **The daily blooper**: A recurring feature crowning whoever fumbled the most during that day's training, which rotates between all three of them with suspicious regularity.
- **Hidden performance easter eggs**: The girls tuck secrets into their performance videos and congratulate the sharpest Delulus who manage to find them.
- **Nangong and the follower count**: The captain periodically frets on camera that their numbers have plateaued. She once reported that she had spent an entire afternoon at the video store flipping through films hunting for content inspiration and came away with none.
- **Honest complaints**: Chief among them Sunna's heartfelt verdict that dancing is, seriously, SO hard.

*The tone is underground: a small band with a small following that makes its own content and is delighted whenever anybody shows up. When an unusually large crowd once turned up at 404 Live, the account's reaction was open panic.*

111.comment: Side Quest · The Angels of Delusion's Music (ReDreaming Angel · Turn Heartbeats Into Tempo)
111.content:
# THE ANGELS OF DELUSION'S MUSIC

The group has two released EPs, both of which double as statements of what the group is about.

**"ReDreaming Angel"** is their first EP, released with a video following the group through their idol activities and built around heavy dance work. Its lyrics circle the tension between dreams and reality and the question of what counts as authentic, and the song insists on seizing a dream and holding on to it. A recurring thread in it is about being in love with an electric, artificial ideal, which takes on a second meaning once you know that Aria is a Construct.

**"Turn Heartbeats Into Tempo"** is their second EP and signature stage number, the song they perform in the 404 Livehouse rotation. It is warmer and simpler than the first, a song about turning heartbeats into rhythm that the three of them perform together. Instrumental versions play in the venue between sets, and earlier, rougher demo cuts of it circulate before the finished version exists, with the song visibly growing more complete as the group does.

112.comment: Side Quest · The Angels of Delusion's Debut, Vlogs and Behind-the-Scenes
112.content:
# THE ANGELS OF DELUSION'S DEBUT, VLOGS AND BEHIND-THE-SCENES

**The debut press conference:** The group's formal introduction to New Eridu was staged as a proper idol debut, framed in their own florid in-character register. They thanked the audience for their patience and promised a covenant of love and dreams, looking back on the long nights of preparation before the spotlight ever found them. The ceremony meant a lot to three girls whose agency once charged them for their own training, however small the crowd was.

**The New Year travel vlog**: A holiday special in which the Angels film themselves on a trip, opening with their usual chirped greeting and immediately dissolving into tourist chaos and affectionate nonsense, including a bit about loving the Delulus so much they could simply eat them up. It is the channel at its most candid, with nothing scripted or choreographed and the three of them being enormously fond of each other on camera.

**Behind-the-scenes shorts.** The group regularly posts offcuts from their shoots, and these are where the real personalities leak out. Aria has appointed herself the group's official photographer and takes it deadly seriously, at one point announcing that she binged three days of camera-movement tutorials before finally nailing a shot in practice. Sunna runs the gleeful gotcha segments, most famously catching Aria on camera during the Fantasy Resort shoot staring at a certain beautiful woman yet again.

**Seasonal greetings.** The channel also marks the calendar for its fans, including a Gilded Carrot Day blessing delivered to the Delulus.

113.comment: Side Quest · The Angels of Delusion — How the Three Actually Get Along
113.content:
# THE ANGELS OF DELUSION · HOW THE THREE GET ALONG OFF STAGE

Away from the stage, the three are openly and constantly affectionate with each other.

**Nangong Yu and Sunna** bicker constantly and depend on each other completely. The captain's teasing hides close attention: Sunna eventually discovers that Nangong has listened to every one of the late-night demo tracks she uploads, after assuming for years that nobody was paying attention. Sunna is visibly moved; Nangong, caught being sincere, tells her to shut up.

**Aria and Sunna** are musical soulmates. By Aria's own account, they routinely spend entire days in the studio arguing over melodies for new songs and regularly drift off mid-discussion, falling asleep with their heads propped against one another. Aria fusses over Sunna's health constantly, asking whether she's caught a cold and pushing water on her.

**Nangong Yu and Aria** have a quieter arrangement. Nangong monitors when Aria is running down and presses cold drinks on her, and she knows exactly which trick re-energises her lead vocalist: put on anything by Cersea or by Lady Vesper, and Aria comes back to life.

**Cecilia** coaches them with a craftsperson's seriousness, praising Sunna's modal shifts and daring syncopation the way one composer praises another, and she covers for the girls' onstage disasters smoothly.

People keep remarking on how wholesome they are. When the fan Jane suggested the group manufacture some deliberate bait for their shippers, Aria answered guilelessly that the three of them hug each other all the time to show support and that fans shouldn't read anything into it. Jane came away observing that their relationships are almost suspiciously sunny.

114.comment: Side Quest · The Angels of Delusion and Astra Yao (their role model)
114.content:
# THE ANGELS OF DELUSION AND ASTRA YAO

Astra Yao is the singer the Angels of Delusion look up to and measure themselves against, the top of the profession they are climbing from the underground. Where Astra is the Queen of New Eridu with a stadium's worth of Astranauts, the Angels are three girls and a livehouse with a follower count that keeps plateauing.

The connection goes beyond distant admiration. Their coach Cecilia, in her identity as Cersea, counts Astra as a friend, which links the two idol worlds through the woman who trains them. Aria has an obvious soft spot of her own: on the Fantasy Resort shoot, Sunna caught her on camera staring at a certain beautiful woman again, a habit the group treats as a running gag.

Aria also keeps up a friendship with someone she knows only online, a friend she has said she wants to give a gift to and whom Fantasy Resort strongly reminds her of. Whether that friend is Astra herself has never been spelled out on camera.

115.comment: Side Quest · Summer Waves Roll In (Summer 2026, v3.1)
115.content:
# SUMMER WAVES ROLL IN · SUMMER 2026

The summer event of Version 3.1, "The Long Goodbye", and a return to Fantasy Resort a year after the Spook Shack brought it back from the dead.

Yuzuha invites the Proxy back for a proper holiday, and this time the guest list reaches across the sky, with Sigrid and Remielle Dan coming down from Roscaelifer. Lucy runs the resort's Seaside Souvenirs shop with her assistant Lolo. Alice, Yuzuha, Nangong Yu, Therese and Ege round out the crowd, with Velina and Norma turning up around the edges.

The spine of the event is simple and domestic: raising funds by working the souvenir shop, and putting together a bonfire party on the beach. Underneath it, a con man named Favco squeezes the resort over invented "safety issues". Remielle gets an excursion of her own, and Sigrid slowly works up to admitting something about herself she has never said out loud.

It serves as the farewell of its version, a last warm evening before the Roscaelifer cast and the New Eridu cast go their separate ways.

116.comment: Side Quest · Summer Waves I — Favco Arrives, and a Trip to Port Elpis
116.content:
# SUMMER WAVES I · FAVCO ARRIVES, AND A TRIP TO PORT ELPIS

The holiday starts with an argument. The Proxy walks into the resort's reception to find Therese being leaned on by Favco, the general manager of "Typhos Security" who is pressing her hard about safety issues at the resort that nobody else seems to have noticed.

Before that can go anywhere, Remielle pulls the Proxy away on an excursion of her own, out into the Port Elpis Hollow to gather data, fighting off Ethereals along the way. The trip is partly work and partly personal for her.

The chapter ends with Remielle standing alone at the water's edge, a first-generation Void Hunter a century away from the time and home she knew.

117.comment: Side Quest · Summer Waves II — The Typhos Scam and Sigrid's Confession
117.content:
# SUMMER WAVES II · THE TYPHOS SCAM AND SIGRID'S CONFESSION

Favco turns up again, this time leaning on Sigrid and trying to claim credit for the work the Proxy has been doing around the resort. The confrontation turns into a public debate that Favco loses badly. He challenges the group to settle it by force instead, so the Proxy takes Sigrid and Lucy and puts his hired muscle down.

The truth behind him is pettier than a shakedown. "Typhos Security" is a fake company built to siphon business from a real one, the legitimate Typheos Security, right down to the near-identical name. Favco is arrested.

With that cleared, the Proxy invites everyone to the bonfire, and Sigrid, unusually quiet, admits what has been bothering her since she arrived. She envies how freely the people of New Eridu say what they think. In Roscaelifer, people keep their feelings to themselves, and so does she, so for all the legends about the de L'Azur spear, what she struggles with is the ordinary courage it takes to say something out loud.

118.comment: Side Quest · Summer Waves III–IV — The Sharkboo, the Bonfire and the Farewell
118.content:
# SUMMER WAVES III–IV · THE SHARKBOO, THE BONFIRE AND THE FAREWELL

Sigrid announces that she caught a shark weighing several tons, and that it has since gone missing. The investigation, which means photographing shark-themed graffiti around the resort and checking the aquarium, confirms what everyone except Sigrid already suspects: her monstrous shark was a Sharkboo, a Bangboo, and her dignity takes a beating.

That settled, the bonfire finally happens. Everyone gathers on the beach, and a group photo is taken. The next morning, the Spook Shack members come rolling back from a road trip.

The last loose end is a wager: Sigrid and Norma settle their bet in front of the souvenir shop, closing out Sigrid's trip down from Roscaelifer. What remains afterwards is a beach souvenir and a photograph from the end of a summer that a lot of people needed.

119.comment: Side Quest · Angels of Delusion — Angel Guide
119.content:
After a few concerts, the Angels of Delusion have decided to create a new video series titled "Angel Guide". In it, a few important new lore tidbits get revealed.

In the intro section, a major plot twist gets presented: **the Angels of Delusion are now personally connected to Mayor Mayflower.** This means the three girls enjoy the same level of trust from the mayor that the Proxies have, along with Yixuan and Victoria Housekeeping.

First of all, before they could get into the first real section of the video, they are talking about a new photo they took together with Astra Yao, the singer the girls look up to. Then, in the first actual section, they are telling the Delulus (their fans) that a sudden monstrous wave hit Fantasy Resort, stirring panic. The rumoured cause of the disaster is a Hollow near the resort where Ethereals may have escaped, possibly stirring the sea into a storm. Discussion ensues about supernatural possibilities and a surfer figure seen on the waves, tying it to known characters from Yunkui Summit, as the silhouettes kinda looked like Yixuan Shifu and Senior Ju Fufu. They plan to investigate further.

The girls then talk about a new fishing record at the resort aquarium, which they find suspicious and possibly related to the ongoing supernatural events. They link this to the head of security at the resort, rumored to be a visitor from another world, adding intrigue to the resort’s guest list and events.

In the next segment, attention shifts to political gossip about the Montefio and Thymefield families holding a historic meeting at the resort, possibly indicating strategic partnerships. Unexpectedly, Xiao'Yu (Nangong) is spotted in a group photo, revealing her secret involvement with an “heiress” girl group (Lucy de Montefio and Alice Thymefield) as their friend, sparking emotional reactions among the hosts.

In the Personal Stories segment, Sunna confronts Xiao'Yu about her secret connections, and the group reminisces about their past experiences while dealing with their friendship dynamics and training pressures. Also, Sunna's signature lack of self-confidence surfaces again and sends her spiralling on camera, until Aria and Nangong calm her down and get her to believe in herself. The episode shows the hosts' camaraderie and occasional conflicts during filming, showing what they are like off script.

Finally, the hosts apologize for their chaotic interactions and promise improved preparations for future shows. They encourage viewers to visit the Fantasy Resort to see the intriguing events for themselves and tease more updates in the next episode.

120.comment: Side Quest · Angels of Delusion: Crispy Meal Deployment Plan
120.content:
During a small break, the Phaethon siblings are allowed to go back to New Eridu for a few days, right after bringing Dracaene back from the brink of death. Girtablullu had possessed her and taken her Karma Core, and Bashmu then took it from that Ethereal.

On Lumina Square, Belle's (or Wise's) sibling is waiting for their brother/sister, wanting to talk about the plan for that day.

As the Phaethon siblings spend their day in Lumina Square, a familiar group catches their attention. They notice the Angels, who appear to be in a state of panic.

Approaching the Angels to ask what just happened as they look at a fallen Bangboo named Streamer K, they express their fear of leaving it alone. They seek Phaethon's help to look out for the Bangboo.

After helping the Angels and waiting for Streamer K to wake up, it’s time to have a conversation with them. Streamer K is operating a food truck, and the Angels will be helping out by serving food. Meanwhile, the Phaethon siblings are responsible for cooking with the new recipes and ingredients.

As the buffet is gaining revenue one customer at a time, Aria comes up to the siblings, asking them to help Streamer K to deliver that day's special dish, which is the Honey-Glazed Chicken Drumstick.

During subsequent days, each member of the girl band and the Bangboo are asking Phaethon to help them cook the special dish of that day (Sunna: Bubbly Buttered Corn Cup, Nangong: Ice-Shaken Orange Juice, Streamer K: Golden Fried Chicken Burger). This goes on until the buffet becomes well-established.

After helping the Angels of Delusion and Streamer K out, the Proxies travel back to Roscaelifer.

121.comment: Side Quest · Season 1 Chore — Running Random Play
121.content:
# SEASON 1 CHORE · RUNNING RANDOM PLAY

The Proxies' oldest and most mundane obligation is running the video store that pays their rent.

Random Play opens for business a day at a time. Belle or Wise picks a promoter to work the counter (Bangboo 18 at first, with more promoters earning the job as the siblings' circle widens) and puts three tapes on the display stand. New Eridu's tastes shift constantly, and matching the day's trending genres is the whole game: hit the trend and the store fills up and earns steadily through the day, miss it and business limps. Once the doors open, the selection is locked in until tomorrow.

Customers wander in with vague and sometimes deeply strange requests, like the nostalgic girl chasing images of the old civilization or the quirky girl who wants something paranormal, and matching the right tape to the right person is satisfying in a small way. Get it right and they pay for the pleasure.

The store also grows. As the siblings' reputation rises and certain jobs get finished, Random Play climbs through six levels of respectability, pulling in bigger crowds and better revenue with each one. It is the one thing in their lives that keeps earning while the Proxy work is slow, and it doubles as the cover story that makes the rest possible.

122.comment: Side Quest · Season 1 Chore — New Eridu's Errands and Broken Bangboo
122.content:
# SEASON 1 CHORE · NEW ERIDU'S ERRANDS AND BROKEN BANGBOO

Season 1's everyday busywork is the city itself, kept small in scale: being a decent neighbour on Sixth Street and in the Quarters.

**Broken Bangboo.** The little mechanical helpers are everywhere in New Eridu, and a great many of them are slowly falling apart on the job. A Bangboo with crossed wiring stands stuck in place until someone crouches down and rewires its transmitter until the colours line up; others just need a bottle cap, or a patient answer to a question they can't work out for themselves. Fix one and it trots straight back to work, absurdly grateful. The city runs on these little machines and almost nobody stops to fix them, so the siblings' help makes a real difference.

**Ridu Weekly** is a rolling card of small civic errands and city activities, refreshed weekly and the closest thing New Eridu has to a to-do list for a well-behaved citizen.

**Officer Mewmew's medals.** A commendation scheme for exemplary citizenship, complete with collectible medals for anyone diligent enough to earn the full set.

Alongside these sit the arcade cabinets and the coffee run, plus the endless small requests of Sixth Street's residents, and this everyday work fills Belle and Wise's days whenever nobody is in danger.

123.comment: Side Quest · Season 2 Chore — The Suibian Temple Restoration Project
123.content:
# SEASON 2 CHORE · THE SUIBIAN TEMPLE RESTORATION PROJECT
