**In Season 3.** In Chapter 3, she carried the news about Girtablullu's Porcelloy to Eldreda in person in case the mole was listening, freeing Cora and the CCD staff from impostors in stolen Airspace Patrol uniforms on the way. When she walked in on Carinus' secret meeting in the Airspace Control Tower, a Singularity Leakage opened out of nowhere and swallowed her (see "S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)"). The strange case she carried held Porcelloy that Claret had entrusted to her for one of Claret's regular meetings with Eldreda; when the Computing Center's reception said there was no appointment on record, she went straight to the tower because the intel was too important to wait. In Chapter 4, the Proxy and Lindverne found her partway up the tower with Sigrid, anaemic after so long away from Claret. She warned them that Carinus had betrayed Roscaelifer and that the person with him was Truvia. Lindverne, who had promised Claret to bring her back in one piece, carried her to the central elevator, and Sigrid blasted a hole through the elevator floor and jumped to the base of the tower with Roxy in her arms to take her to Vyrium. When the Proxy found that a little excessive, Roxy told them it was fine, since she had grown used to this, and milady would have come up with something far more imaginative. Phoenix promptly tried to recruit her for Krampus and then took the offer back herself, conceding that Krampus could never top Roscaelifer's benefits (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Sigrid and Roxy)").

APPEARANCE: She is small, around 144 centimetres tall. She has short mint-green hair with a small tuft tied up at the crown, long pointed elf ears and red eyes behind thick black-framed glasses, plus a dark headband fitted with metal fins and a small plated ornament at one temple. She wears a black sleeveless leather harness-vest studded with straps over a pale blue-white cropped shirt with a stiff collar, and detached black sleeves ending in silver-white cuffs, one forearm plated with a red-lensed guard and a spiky wristband, the other wrist ringed only with spikes. Her black high-waisted shorts are cut away at the hips with silver-laced red panels beneath a wide studded belt set with a red gem, and a spiked harness wraps one thigh. Torn red cloth panels hang from her hips like a ragged skirt. Her ankles are ringed with spiked cuffs, and her legs are armoured in red-and-purple spiked boots. She holds a black canister marked with glowing pink Bangboo-like eyes in her raised hand and rests the other on the head of a colossal grey hammer standing beside her, a cross-plated maul studded with rivets on a dark red haft and taller than she is.

**Combat Style (Wind · Stun, S-Rank):** Released on 30 September 2026 in the second half of v3.2 on the "Cindernight Respite" banner, alongside a Promeia rerun, with her signature W-Engine Crimson Moon Casket. She is an on-field Stunner who stays in the fight, and her loop runs on three resources: Energy, **Wind Energy** (one point for every 25 Energy she spends, capped at 3) and the **Eyes of the Storm** she leaves on the field (up to 9 at once, each detonating on its own after 30 seconds). Her Core Passive, *Warm Night's Embrace*, converts any initial Energy Regen above 1.2 into flat ATK and Impact (+5 ATK and +0.4 Impact for every 0.01 at full strength, capping at +960 ATK and +76.8 Impact), so she is built around Energy Regen.
- Basic Attack *Do Stay a While* is a four-hit Wind string. Her Dodge is *Excuse Me*, her Dash Attack *Forgive My Rudeness* and her invulnerable Dodge Counter *Returned Courtesy*.
- Her Quick Assist is *At Your Service*, her Defensive Assist *Allow Me to Assist* (a parry for massive Daze) and her Assist Follow-Up *Midnight Code*. Pressing Assist again after a Defensive Assist triggers *More Overtime?*, which keeps her on the field to keep swinging.
- Her plain Special Attack is *Much Obliged*. Her EX Special, *Don't Catch a Chill*, is a forward slide; holding it sends her into the **Whirlwind** state, where Roxy herself becomes a steerable tornado that she drives around the arena, burning Energy to grind Wind DMG and Daze into everything in its path. Leaving it automatically fires *Kindly Rest in Peace*, a wind cannon that spends all of her Wind Energy, adding one extra hit and dropping one Eye of the Storm for every point spent.
- *Forgive Me for Not Seeing You Off* fires automatically once the Eyes on the field plus her Wind Energy add up to three or more: she throws her hammer and detonates up to three Eyes. Fewer than three detonations become Miniature Windstorms that chase enemies down, and three at once collapse into a single Giant Windstorm that drags them together. When the hammer hits a Windswept enemy, it triggers Cleanse, and whenever anyone in the squad triggers Contamination or Cleanse, the whole squad gains CRIT DMG equal to 0.4% for every 1% of Roxy's CRIT Rate, up to 40% (Armorers gain Laceration DMG instead, up to 20%), for 50 seconds.
- Her Chain Attack is the greathammer swing *Gale-Burial Great Hammer*; her Ultimate, *Requiem for the Night-Burial*, is a huge Wind strike that also gives her one Wind Energy.
- Her Additional Ability, *Porcelloy Heart*, switches on with an Attack, Rupture or Armorer teammate: it raises her own DMG, raises the squad's Stun DMG Multiplier and makes Stuns last 2 seconds longer, makes Windswept enemies take more damage and stay Windswept 20 seconds longer, restores 40 Energy when she enters the field and boosts Anomaly Buildup after her EX Special.
- Mindscape Cinemas: *Versatile Attendant*, *Clocking Out Myth*, *Tales of Insomnia*, *R.I.P.*, *Second Heartbeat* and *Eternity and the Clockwork Doll* (the last one makes Giant Windstorms inflict Afterecho and spawn extra Giant Windstorms).
(Her early test version scaled off DEF instead and earned Wind Energy every 30 Energy; the released kit runs on Energy Regen as described above.) Her whole kit is named like a scrupulously polite office worker with a funeral director's vocabulary ("Do Stay a While", "Much Obliged", "At Your Service", "Allow Me to Assist", "More Overtime?", "Kindly Rest in Peace"), and that joke is worth playing up. Render her as a small, tired mechanic with a deadpan face, swinging a hammer twice her size while the storm she controls spins the room around her.

197.comment: NPC BG · Mayor Mayflower (New Eridu City Administration)
197.content:
**Mayor Mayflower · Mayor of New Eridu (background):** Usually addressed simply as the Mayor, he is a man in his later middle years. As the current Mayor of New Eridu, he also heads the Mayflower Family that founded the city. His City Administration runs the HIA and Public Security and officially treats Hollow Raiders and Proxies as threats, even as he quietly relies on the Phaethon siblings. Like every mayor since the original Eridu, he confers the title of Void Hunter, each bearer with an epithet of their own. He stands against both TOPS and the Exaltists.

A close friend of Carole Arna from before the Fall, he stays loyal to her legacy and believes the siblings' ocular implants hold a power that could affect all of New Eridu. Victoria Housekeeping, his private intelligence service, watched over Phaethon on his orders long before he revealed himself to them in the Season 1 Epilogue (see "S1 · Victoria Housekeeping & Mockingbird" and "S1 · Von Lycaon's Hidden History"). He then gave them an HDD upgrade built from Carole's research, restoring their suppressed Ether aptitude so they can enter Hollows in person. He also leaked Hugo Vlad's illegitimate Ravenlock birth to turn the public against the Ravenlocks, forcing them and the Exaltists to delay their plans.

After Lemnian Hollow's anomalous readings turned up a photo of Carole wreathed in Miasma, he sent Phaethon to join Yunkui Summit's investigation on the Waifei Peninsula (see "S2 Ch1 · Waifei Peninsula (v2.0)"). Once the Creator's sub-manifestation fell, he finally appeared in person to name Ye Shunguang "Qingming Arbiter" at a public Void Hunter ceremony. Privately, he calls the choice the only path left, one Carole would likely have opposed, and his reflections hint that he is gathering the keepers of Void Hunter weapons for his own ends. In Season 3, he invited Phaethon to Roscaelifer for treatment, where they arrived as special transfer students, and he later vouched for them there as engineering collaborators. When Booastrum was locked down in Season 3 Chapter 4, Velina called him off the record from house arrest. He sent Senior Commissioner Severian Lowell into the lockdown alone, with authority to execute whoever stands behind Mosseint on the spot, no report required, and turned down Severian's suggestion to bring Victoria Housekeeping along. He insists the City Administration officially takes no sides between Roscaelifer, TOPS and the Defense Force. When Velina framed his intervention for him (she had no wish to overstep her own authority and be questioned by Lady Lindverne later), he told her she grows more persuasive by the day. He calls himself an old man who has long outlived his usefulness, and he once knew Mosseint as a man of talent who walks with his head down. Roscaelifer's defenders remind him of TOPS's Three Pacts, who were all once in the right until each came to believe its path was the only right one (see "S3 Ch4 · A Commissioner Sent Alone (Severian)").

He sees himself as morally grey, and he tells Phaethon plainly that he has his own agenda. He stays polite with people who distrust him for his office, and he prefers allies he can deny: Victoria Housekeeping, Phaethon, Yixuan, the Angels of Delusion and, when it suits him, even Mockingbird.

APPEARANCE: He is a tall, lean man of late middle age with a very upright bearing. His silver hair is combed back in a smooth wave, a few loose locks falling at the temples, then gathered at the nape into a long, narrow ponytail that hangs to the small of his back from a carved brown clasp. His face is long and angular, with a straight nose and a firm jaw under high cheekbones. Deep creases cross his forehead and long folds run from nose to mouth, and his pale blue eyes sit under heavy silver brows with crow's feet at the corners.

He wears a white suit with a pale lavender sheen. The fitted, hip-length jacket, worn over a charcoal waistcoat and grey shirt, has a tall, stiff, flared collar rising up both sides of his neck and dark navy stripes down its sleeves and sides. A teal band circles his throat with a small white cravat bow and a gold knotwork clasp, and twisted gold cords cross down his shirtfront over a teal tie to a small gold pin shaped like a stylised anchor. A long teal stole with a navy reverse drapes over both shoulders and hangs past his hips front and back. Below the jacket, he wears straight white trousers and polished burgundy-brown leather dress shoes, and dark navy gloves cover his hands.

**Narration note:** The Mayor is a man; use he/him for him everywhere, including news reports and calls where he is only heard. Before the Qingming Arbiter ceremony, keep him mostly off-screen in Phaethon's scenes, as a voice on the line or as orders relayed through Victoria Housekeeping. At a podium, he is an animated speaker who raises his gloved palms to the crowd and presents honourees with an open, upturned hand. Away from the microphones he is measured and courteous, with a faint, closed-lipped smile.

198.content:
**Eldreda Sunbringer:** The eldest of the three manifestations, she heads Roscaelifer's Administrative Affairs Department and holds the most of the original's memories. Like her two sisters, she is an organic, flesh-and-blood woman, and the claim that the Sunbringers are Intelligent Constructs was a public lie inherited from their mother. By origin, she is also an Enchainer, a vessel the original Sunbringer made around one fragment of her own Karma Core, and she still carried that fragment at the end of Chapter 4. Her role and temperament, and the split that made her, are covered in "S3 Ch1 · One Into Three (The Split Sunbringer)", a Chapter 1 account that still repeats the Intelligent Construct story; see also "S2 · Lady Sunbringer & Roscaelifer" for the original.

**Off duty, music.** Under the stern public face, Eldreda loves music. She sings and plays the guitar well enough to pass for a professional street performer, and in her mother's dreams, she is a musician, with somebody else issuing the decrees. Music is the part of her life that belongs to her alone. She is far more careful with words than her mother ever was, marking the tone and emphasis of every line in her speeches because she is afraid of saying something wrong, and by Lindverne's account, she is even worse than Lindverne at saying what she feels.

**The weight she carries.** When Carinus first met her, he told her she alone of the three had inherited Sunbringer's appearance completely, and it left her with a childlike joy and a sense of duty she had never felt before, as if she had been chosen to become the next Sunbringer. She has been following her mother's footsteps ever since. When the Creator's descent in the Lemnian Hollow stirred the Great Hollows and made the Rosetta Data unreliable for about half a month, she broke the sisters' half-forgotten promise and opened the Secret Chamber, where she learned the truth about her mother and the Hive Lord Hollow. The CCD's calculations gave her mother's restraints two or three more months at most. Since then, she has been spending her own power at the top of the Airspace Control Tower to hold the Hollow, and she asked Flint Workshop for an artificial Karma Core, a way for a Sunbringer to survive without one. Her worst-case plan was to borrow Lindverne's and Dracaene's fragments and fulfil the duty alone, which Lindverne refused to hear of. Remielle's confrontation with her, recorded in Roscaelifer as an assassination attempt, came from Remielle's belief that Eldreda knew the truth about Project Sunseeker. Her own policy of opening Roscaelifer to New Eridu was the door Carinus used to let TOPS in, and the lockdown order went out in her name while she was sealed away, which is why Phoenix took her for the mole and Youkai called the whole invasion "Eldreda's call".

**Season 3.** She spent the Booastrum crisis in the Secret Chamber with her mother, so cut off that she never learned Dracaene's fragment had been stolen (see "S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)"). She calls the Proxy a child of Helios and the first Sunbringer "Mother", and when Lindverne finally reached her, she told her sister that the one who knows nothing is Lindverne. When the Hive Lord Hollow broke loose and Youkai and Truvia came for the chamber with Bashmu at the end of Chapter 4, she told the others to go. Casting Lindverne and the Proxy away from the top of the tower, she stayed to face the three of them alone. **Her fate is unknown.** Her mother's last blessing for her was that her sense of duty would no longer leave her standing alone, and that she would be loved as deeply as she loves others.

The three sisters have been announced as a single playable three-in-one Agent named "Sunbringer" (S-Rank, a Fire-type Armorer with a special element variant, of the Void Hunter faction), expected in v3.4, introduced with a line about the name carrying the world's hope and the promise the three of them made standing side by side.

APPEARANCE: She seems the eldest of the three manifestations and wears the original's face almost exactly, so reuse the head described in the APPEARANCE block of "S2 · Lady Sunbringer & Roscaelifer" unchanged. Her eyes are the original's mismatched amber-gold and pale ice-blue, and the dark horns sit at her crown as they did on the original. Her white-silver hair is worn loose and very long and lifts in any moving air. Her regalia is midnight navy shading to black: a fitted armoured dress with a high slit up one thigh, dark plating layered over the bodice and hips, a red collar-wrap at the throat and a bronze-gold ornament set at the sternum. Over all of it hangs a black tattered mantle, the hem cut into long ragged points that trail behind her like torn banners. Her legs are bare between the dress and dark thigh-high boots strapped at the ankle and knee. She carries her weapon openly, either a long-hafted polearm held across her back or a broad greatsword planted point-down when she stands still, and both look far too large for her frame. All of Roscaelifer knows her face from the speeches she gives in person. Since she began holding the Hive Lord Hollow at the top of the Airspace Control Tower, she has stepped back from public life, with Carinus covering for her when needed.

(Note for narration: the original wore a field officer's uniform, and Eldreda wears a head of state's regalia. Remielle fought her face to face under an open sky, and Lindverne and the Proxy found her in the Secret Chamber, so describe her in the same full detail as any main character whenever she is on stage. If a scene puts a guitar in her hands, let the stiffness of the regalia fall away from her posture.)

199.content:
**Dracaene Sunbringer:** She is the manifestation who heads the Central Computing Department and carries the engineering prodigy side of the original Sunbringer's mind, the side that built the world's Bangboo. Like her two sisters, she is an organic, flesh-and-blood girl, and the claim that the Sunbringers are Intelligent Constructs was a public lie. By origin, she is also an Enchainer, a vessel the original made around a fragment of her Karma Core, which is why losing that fragment to Bashmu left her in a condition that only its return can cure. Her role and temperament, and the split that made her, are covered in "S3 Ch1 · One Into Three (The Split Sunbringer)", a Chapter 1 account that still repeats the Intelligent Construct story; see also "S3 Ch1 · Lady Dracaene's Report".

She is the youngest of the three sisters and the sharpest technical mind among them, and she treats the Bangboo she built as her younger siblings. Of the three, she carries the fewest of the original's memories. Since Bashmu swallowed her fragment, she has been unconscious in Flint Workshop's care on Vyrium, kept stable by Flint Workshop's equipment and by Remielle's Thaumiel. The only way to fully restore her is to take her Karma Core back (see "S3 Ch3 · The Homeland of Porcelloy (Vyrium and the Flint Blood)"). Lindverne calls her "Dracie", and Pyrois calls her "the small Sunbringer". She invented the **Ether Level Limiter**, a gun made to keep an Etheric Other in check, and gave it to the Proxy after their Pyrois treatment. In Season 3 Chapter 4, it was what broke Truvia's control over her own Etheric Other (see "S3 Ch4 · Pyrois Against the Blasphemer (Showdown with Truvia)"). In her mother's dreams, Dracaene is a schoolgirl at Aurelia Academy chasing a golden beetle with her classmates, a path she might once have taken and the childhood she never had. The Dracaene her mother sees in waking life is the one who shed her innocence to become the most dependable helmsman of the Celestial Nexus. Her mother's blessing for her was that her wisdom would part the fog of the unknown so people could see the path ahead. She is one third of the announced three-in-one Agent "Sunbringer" (see "NPC BG · Eldreda Sunbringer (AAD, Roscaelifer)").

APPEARANCE: She is plainly a child and by far the smallest of the three, barely reaching an adult's ribs. Her hair is silver-grey, cut to the shoulders and flicked outward at the ends, with one stubborn strand standing up from the crown and small black horn-shaped clips pinned at either side (since she has no horns, she has the most divergent silhouette out of the three Sunbringers). The fringe covers one eye entirely, and the other is a warm amber-gold that watches people with a flat, unblinking stare. She wears a sleeveless navy dress with a bronze yoke collar at the chest, set with a gold four-petal clover emblem, and yellow textile "rays" fan down from the collar across the chest. The skirt is scattered with large blue flower appliqués, each pale-edged flower with a centre disc marked by downward-pointing triangles. A small gold tag hangs at the hip while black bands circle her upper arms, blue floral bracers cover her forearms and her lower legs disappear into dark armoured greaves marked with the same gold flower, ending in open-toed blue sandal-boots. Her shoulders and thighs are bare, and everything she wears looks like equipment scaled down to fit her.

200.content:
**Lindverne Sunbringer:** She is the manifestation who directs the Airspace Patrol Department. Like her two sisters, she is an organic, flesh-and-blood woman, and the claim that the Sunbringers are Intelligent Constructs was a public lie. By origin, she is also an Enchainer, a vessel the original Sunbringer made around a fragment of her Karma Core, and she still carries hers, which makes her one of TOPS's two remaining targets. She has told the Proxy directly that she is no ally of the Creator. Her role and temperament, and the split that made her, are covered in "S3 Ch1 · One Into Three (The Split Sunbringer)", a Chapter 1 account that still repeats the Intelligent Construct story; see also "S3 Ch2 · Meeting Lindverne Sunbringer for the First Time".

She is the middle sister, with a personality very similar to Billy Kid's. In her mother's eyes, she is bold and fearless with a heart full of courage, "that bright, strong child". She is Claret Flint's biggest customer, since the Airspace Patrol runs on Porcelloy weapons, and the two of them are close friends who bicker constantly. Claret and Roxy rode on her shoulders as children. Much like Billy Kid, she is a big Starlight Knight fan. Through her fragment of the Karma Core, she can use her mother's power, Genesis Reconstruction, which she calls Sunbringer's Authority. In Season 3 Chapter 3, when she and the Proxy held her greatsword together and resonated, the blade reshaped itself into a saw that split Kusarikku in half. In Chapter 4, she built a High Ambitions combat mech out of thin air from everyone's descriptions, and after several comically wrong drafts, she nailed the design based on Billy's description of a mech from Starlight Knight. She is the one who finally told the Proxy the Sunbringers' secret (see "S3 Ch3 · The Storm Has Yet to Settle (Sunbringer's Secret)"), and when she learned that Eldreda meant to carry their mother's burden alone, she refused outright: it is "our" duty, and nobody gets to leave her and Dracie out of it. In her mother's dream, a tough street-kid Lindverne runs a pickpocket off "her" street, a path she didn't take in the end; the Lindverne who exists is the patrol chief pairing humans with Bangboo to cut blind spots and give her people more rest, and to her mother both are simply her, the one who leaps to help without hesitating. She doesn't believe in a predetermined fate. Her mother's blessing was that her passion would keep the flame burning so the long cold night never feels endless again. Remielle caught her and the Proxy in mid-air as Roscaelifer fell into the Hive Lord Hollow. She is one third of the announced three-in-one Agent "Sunbringer" (see "NPC BG · Eldreda Sunbringer (AAD, Roscaelifer)").

APPEARANCE: She has an adult frame, slighter and softer-featured than Eldreda's, with long silver-white hair worn loose. Her eyes are mismatched, one gold-amber and one clear blue, which is the plainest visible sign that the three of them were once a single person split unevenly. Large black horns tipped with small magenta gems arch over her brow, and a thin, unattached teal ring floats behind her head, another sign that she is one part of the original Lady Sunbringer. Her uniform is deep navy with black armour laid over it: a sleeveless dress with a keyhole at the sternum, bare shoulders, a black gauntlet-glove running past one elbow and magenta four-petal blooms at the keyhole window to her belly. The skirt is built from broad armoured petal-plates in the same navy, each stamped with a pink cross motif, layered over darker tattered underskirts that hang to different lengths. Dark thigh-high boots plated at the shin end in bright brass toes, with blade-like fins swept back at the calf. She wears all that armour slackly, weight on one hip and hands loose, like someone who put on the office and is waiting for permission to take it off.

201.content:
**Carinus · Deputy Administrative Director of the Administrative Affairs Department (Roscaelifer):** Lady Eldreda Sunbringer's right hand at the AAD, the official whose job is to pass the legitimate concerns of Roscaelifer's residents along to the ESD (see "S3 Ch1 · A Mysterious Visitor in Blonde (Carinus)"). In public, he is courteous and diplomatic, the man who smooths over misunderstandings and keeps the paperwork of the city moving, and he reminds Dracaene of Eldreda's warmer side. Cissia remembers him only as "that blond guy".

He is also an **Intelligent Construct personally created by the first Sunbringer**, dedicated to managing and developing the city. He has worked at her side since Roscaelifer was founded, which means he has served the city longer than any of the three current Sunbringers. The first Sunbringer crafted his Logic Core herself. When he first met Eldreda, he told her that she alone of the three had inherited Sunbringer's appearance completely, a remark that shaped her whole sense of duty (see "S3 Ch4 · Who Is Trapped in the Secret Room (The Secret Chamber)").

**The traitor.** Carinus drafted the AAD's proposal to widen cooperation with New Eridu, which invited TOPS, the HIA and the White Star Institute, and once Eldreda approved it, he was given full authority over its execution. He also argued for rebuilding Quietude Isle as a new airport. Acting alone and on his own authority, he promised High Ambitions Corp. a share of the Rosetta Data and let TOPS into Booastrum, because High Ambitions offered the most effective way he had found to cut the toll the Rosetta Data exacts to a minimum, and the toll was falling on the Sunbringers. Eldreda calls it his obsession with the Sunbringers. In Season 3 Chapter 3, Roxy walked in on his secret meeting with Truvia in the Airspace Control Tower and was swallowed by a Singularity Leakage, and he answered Roxy's phone to tell Claret she was in a meeting with Eldreda (see "S3 Ch3 · Messenger in the Mist (Roxy Alone on Booastrum)"). The lockdown order issued in Eldreda's name came through the AAD while she was out of sight.

**Outplayed.** He tried to draw High Ambitions to a negotiating table he could control, the way he had handled things for a century, and demanded Dracaene's Karma Core back and the help with the Rosetta Data he had been promised. Youkai, wearing Serpico's face, claimed Mosseint was stuck in traffic and introduced Truvia as the High Ambitions heiress who spoke with his weight. After mocking Carinus' terms, he finally invited "the late Mr. Mosseint" to weigh in, showing Carinus the corpse of the man he had come to bargain with. Truvia, who had asked whether he wasn't afraid they would burn the bridges and take him down with them, told him that leverage only matters if the other side agrees it has value (see "NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)"). Youkai's repeated intrusions left Carinus with about 37% of his components damaged. His confession to Lindverne ends with a last word for Eldreda: he failed her, and given another chance, he would still try to stop her from meeting an end that should never have been hers. By the end of Season 3 Chapter 4, he is in temporary dormancy at the top of the Airspace Control Tower and needs comprehensive maintenance. Severian believes he quietly kept Sigrid and Roxy alive (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)").

(Note for narration: beyond his blond hair, keep his physical description vague and let his manner carry his scenes. Play him as a reasonable, polite man who is quietly certain he is doing the right thing for the people he was built to serve.)

202.content:
**Khors Belobog · founder of Belobog (deceased, background):** Father of Koleda and adoptive father of Grace; a kind, beloved boss. On the eve of the Hollow Zero disaster, he left with company funds and was publicly condemned as an embezzler who wrecked the firm. In reality, he spent the money completing a prototype machine to seal away a corrupted “Sacrifice” within a Hollow monument, sacrificing his life in the process. This central Season 1 reveal clears his name and exposes the conspiracy behind the Fall.

APPEARANCE (for flashbacks; deceased before the present day): He was a broad-shouldered man in his prime with spiky, wind-tossed hair in a deep auburn-red, swept back and upward in thick points, with sharp arched brows over narrow, fierce eyes and a strong jaw. Koleda clearly takes after him in hair colour and the set of the brow. Surviving footage nearly always catches him mid-effort, shouting or laughing with his teeth bared and one arm thrown forward. He is remembered in plain factory-floor clothing, a white sleeveless work shirt that shows bare arms thick with the muscle of a man who built machines himself, against a backdrop of Belobog scaffolding, girders and construction lamps. Depictions of his final hours carry grime and streaked marks across one cheek. Because his memory survives mostly as damaged recordings and second-hand recollection, narrate flashbacks involving him with that grain, with colour bleeding at the edges and sound and picture cutting in and out.

203.content:
**Ye Shiyuan · Yunkui Summit (background):** Ye Shunguang's analytical, protective older brother. Their parents died shielding them during a Miasma outbreak in the Fall after getting saved by Banyue Shifu, leaving him with recurring nightmares and a vow to free his sister from the Qingming Sword's curse. That desperation makes him vulnerable: in Season 2's climax, he is manipulated by Sarah and the Exaltists into a hidden, Ethereal-like state while playing a dangerous double game.

APPEARANCE: He is a slim young man of average height with tousled ash-brown hair falling loosely over his forehead and past his ears, and his narrow red eyes habitually sit half-lidded, giving him a tired, faintly sardonic look. His default posture is closed, with arms folded or one hand raised to his chin or mouth while he thinks. He wears Yunkui Summit's modernised robes: a sleeveless mustard-yellow tunic with a crossed, wrapped front over a high-collared pale grey underlayer, with light grey shoulder panels bearing dark cloud-scroll emblems, cinched at the waist by a grey band with a thin red cord. Both forearms are covered by long black fingerless arm sleeves, and a long tan mantle hangs from his back down to his calves. Below, loose off-white trousers with grey panelling taper into cuffed hems above black-and-white lace-up trainers. Small metal charms and a thin cord hang at his left hip. During Season 2's climax, narrate his hidden Ethereal-like state as something showing through his usual look, with the sclera darkening and Ether-light crawling under the skin until even the yellow of his tunic looks dull.

204.content:
**The Exaltists · defunct cult and central antagonist faction (background):** A doomsday cult and the driving antagonist force of Seasons 1 and 2. They run “Sacrifice”-serum human experiments and Miasma schemes, deliberately corrupting people into Ethereals to serve their ends, and they have agents threaded through New Eridu's institutions. Ironically, they see the ultimate solution to war, famines, illnesses and eternal life in embracing the Hollows and becoming mindless Ethereal monsters, getting "refined" by the Creator, the god of their religion. Figures tied to them include Inspector Justin Bringer, Sarah (Fugue), Landon, Hartman Ravenlock, the embittered commander Isolde, and the Overseer Mevorakh. Their conspiracy ties the Fall of the Old Capital to the framing of Khors Belobog and to the corruption plots Phaethon keeps unraveling. The deaths of Isolde and Sarah ultimately led to the decapitation and dissolving of the cult.

APPEARANCE of the Exaltist uniforms and the Overseer (past tense; the cult is dissolved): Rank-and-file Exaltists wore identical floor-length white hooded cloaks, styled after a secretive religious order. The hoods were deep and the faces beneath were hidden behind pale grey veils, so species and sex disappeared along with rank. A hall of them standing in rows looked like rows of identical statues, an anonymity the cult wanted.

Overseer Mevorakh, Isolde under a concealed identity, wore a far more elaborate version built to hide that a woman was underneath. The silhouette was padded and squared at the shoulders, the layered white-and-grey ceremonial robes falling straight and heavy to conceal her frame, with a red cross-laced sash across the chest. Enormous crimson sleeves swept upward and outward from the shoulders like folded wings, adding bulk and height. The face was covered by a golden mask crowned with a fanned white ornamental headdress and hanging gold tassels, with a long false white beard falling below it to suggest an elderly male figure. Gloved hands rested on a tall staff set with a red gem. Removing the Overseer's coat and mask to reveal Isolde's face was the physical act of the Season 2 reveal, so narrate the two looks as completely unrecognisable from one another.

205.content:
**Dr. Lohr · Season 2 antagonist NPC (background):** A secret Exaltist collaborator who ran a clinic in Failume Heights. He tampered with Porcelumex's anti-corruption medicine and pushed his own fake remedy, “Alleviating Water”, to lure aggrieved miners into the Lemnian Hollow, where they were corrupted into Ethereals as fodder for the Exaltists. Exposed by Yunkui Summit and Phaethon (tipped off by Damian), he killed himself by self-corruption; his clinic was later repurposed into Porcelumex's VR “Echo Chamber” therapy facility.

APPEARANCE: He is a tall, lean man with a scholarly and forgettable manner. His dark hair is combed flat and swept back from a high forehead, gathered long at the nape. Thin brows sit low over narrow, downcast eyes, and his most characteristic gesture is raising one hand to cover his mouth while he thinks or listens, which conveniently hides his expression. He wears a clean white physician's coat, unbuttoned, over a cream vertically-striped shirt or fine-knit sweater, with a deep crimson necktie knotted high and a red pen clipped in the breast pocket. A black belt with a squared silver buckle holds up charcoal trousers tapered at the ankle, and polished black leather dress shoes complete the look. He looks like a respectable clinic doctor, the cover that let him sell "Alleviating Water" to desperate miners.

206.comment: NPC BG · Isolde (Colonel Isolde / Overseer Mevorakh, deceased)
206.content:
**Isolde · Defense Force colonel, secret Overseer Mevorakh, Season 2's major antagonist alongside the Creator's vessel, antagonist (deceased, background):** Before the Fall of the Old Capital, Isolde commanded the Defense Force's Agamemnon Squad, with Orpheus (later Magus) serving under her. The squad was ordered to guard a train they were told carried civilians evacuating the Hollow; they were overrun by Ethereals and all but destroyed, and only Yijiang's self-sacrifice with the Qingming Sword let Isolde and a mortally wounded Orpheus escape. The train had in fact been carrying Porcelumex assets, because Lorenz had taken a bribe from Lucro and ordered company property protected ahead of civilian lives, and learning this broke her. She spent the years since building a double life: Colonel Isolde in the open, Overseer Mevorakh at the head of the Exaltists in secret, using the cult's Miasma work as the machinery of a private revenge. Her endgame was to kill Lorenz as Isolde while, as Mevorakh, spiking the Lemnian Hollow so the Miasma would spawn corrupted soldiers wearing the faces of the Defense Force dead. Cornered, she removed the Overseer's coat and mask and took the Miasma into herself to become The Defiler. Yixuan and Obol Squad beat her, and then, Orphie and Magus bested her in a duel. Her last act was to shoot Orphie with a non-lethal round specifically to taunt her old subordinate Magus into finishing her. Sarah, who had served as Mevorakh's right hand, inherited the Overseer's power at her death; the loss of both women decapitated the cult.

APPEARANCE (as Isolde, unmasked): She is a poised woman of average height with shoulder-length wavy hair in a pale sage green, parted in the middle and pinned on one side with a small black flower clip, loose strands falling past her jaw. Her eyes are a cool, clear blue with a small dark mark below the left one, and her mouth rests in a faint, controlled half-smile. She wears a long, high-collared military-cut coat dress in dark blue-grey, buttoned in a single row down the front, with a white rose brooch at the breast trailing a red ribbon. Banded red-and-white stripes run around both upper sleeves above ruffled cuffs at the wrists. A wide pleated white sash-belt hung with metal rings cinches her waist. The coat's long panels fall to the ankle, ornamented with cream-and-gold teardrop insignia and a small red floral emblem near the hem, over a deep wine-red under-skirt. Muted green heeled shoes with a flower at the toe finish it. The silhouette is an officer's, buttoned up and decorated, cut in the sombre style of mourning-wear.

For her concealed Overseer look, and for the appearance of rank-and-file Exaltists, see the Exaltists entry.

207.comment: NPC BG · Big Daddy (Sons of Calydon founder)
207.content:
**Big Daddy · Sons of Calydon founder (background):** A boar Thiren and former member of the original Calydon gang who founded the Sons of Calydon from its remnants. He raised Caesar King after her father went missing and her mother died, in a deliberately hands-off way that made her tough and self-reliant, later taking in Lighter by paying off his debts. A respected elder, wise figure of the Outer Ring.

APPEARANCE: He is a heavyset boar Thiren, broad through the chest and shoulders. His head is fully boarlike, with a deep crimson-red face, a blunt snout and curved golden tusks jutting up from the lower jaw, framed by a thick shaggy white mane like a lion's and a white beard beneath the chin. Wraparound black sunglasses hide his eyes, leaving very little of his expression readable. He wears a black studded leather biker jacket, silver studs banding the lapels and shoulders, a large circular gold medallion pinned over the chest with a small chain, a faction patch of the Sons of Calydon logo on one shoulder and a gold plate strapped around the upper arm. Loops of shotgun shells are stitched across the front. A turquoise paisley bandana is knotted at his throat. His forearms are bare red skin above dark gloves, with heavy gold spiked cuffs at both wrists. Below, he wears black flared, heavily ripped jeans, a leather strap belted around one thigh, two gold spikes at the hip and black cloven-hoofed boots. A curled tail sits behind him. At a glance, he is the old-guard patriarch of the Outer Ring bikers.

208.comment: NPC BG · Pompey (Vanquishers leader, former Motor League Overlord, deceased)
208.content:
**Pompey · leader of the Vanquishers and Motor League Overlord (deceased, background):** The reigning Overlord of the Motor League before Caesar King, and head of the Vanquishers, the Sons of Calydon's chief rivals in the Outer Ring. As Overlord, he held the power to dictate resource transportation routes across the Outer Ring. During the most recent Tour de Inferno, he was betrayed by Lucius, his own second-in-command, who drugged him to accelerate Ether corruption and abandoned him to turn into an Ethereal at Cinder Lake. He fell into the lake after a last-ditch attack during his fight with Caesar King and the Sons of Calydon. Lucius then usurped him by swapping his own eroded Sparkstone into the dead man's hands in place of the real one; Pompey, understanding the betrayal, marked Lucius with a scar before the end. His death ended the Vanquishers' hold on the League and left Caesar standing as Overlord, a title she still refuses to claim outright because she feels she did not win it fairly. That refusal is his shadow on the story: she measures herself against a man who was cheated out of the fight she should have had.

APPEARANCE (for flashbacks; deceased): He was a tall, heavily built man well past his youth, thick through the chest and arms. Dark hair shot through with grey is swept straight back from a high forehead, and a full beard and moustache, greying at the chin, frame a hard mouth. Heavy brows sit over pale, cold blue eyes. He wears a long black leather coat with gold piping, its shoulders capped by large gold-edged pauldrons bearing an engraved crest, and a gold chain-torc closing the collar. Beneath it is a black armoured bodysuit moulded to the torso, marked with bold white X-shaped bands across the chest and abdomen. A strap of metal identification plates hangs across his front. A wide belt with an ornate silver skull buckle sits at his waist over dark trousers, with steel-grey greaves plating his shins and black metal-capped boots below. One gloved hand rests at his hip, the other holds a dark gauntlet. He stands like a man used to being the largest presence in any yard he walks into.

**Ether corruption note:** In depictions of his final moments at Cinder Lake, narrate the drugged corruption taking hold, with veins lighting under the skin and the eyes turning flat and luminous, while he stays aware of exactly who did this to him.

209.content:
**Milena · Pulchra Fellini's childhood friend and betrayer (background, whereabouts unknown):** A cat Thiren from the same impoverished Outer Ring town as Pulchra, and for years her only friend. Their favourite childhood game was pretending to live in the city, playing at being waitresses and customers in a rehearsal for a life neither of them had. Both had notable Ether Aptitudes and no better prospects than mercenary work. It was Milena who proposed the two of them form their own outfit, and Milena who quickly installed Pulchra as its head, running everything through Pulchra's bank account. When a client's goods went missing along with every Denny in that account, Pulchra confronted her. Milena admitted she had taken it to buy herself a new life in the city, then knocked Pulchra out and left. She spared her life but left her carrying the whole debt. Her later Trust Commission line, that their game only ever had room for one city lady and that Pulchra was a naive fool for not seeing it, recasts the whole friendship as a long con in which the shared dream was always zero-sum in her mind.

**Plot status:** Deliberately unresolved in canon. Nobody knows where she went, whether the money lasted, whether she is still in New Eridu, or what she would do if she and Pulchra ever stood in the same room again. This thread is still open.

APPEARANCE: She is a cat Thiren woman with short, choppy black hair cut around jaw length, with longer strands framing her face below heavy uneven bangs. Black feline ears sit high on her head, the inner fur a pale near-white that catches the light. Her eyes are a flat golden amber and wide-set, and her face at rest is blank. Her skin is pale. She wears a boxy, cropped jacket in worn off-white and grey, the fabric visibly patched and re-stitched from salvage, hanging open off both shoulders. Beneath it is a dark olive-brown camisole with thin straps and a cross-laced detail at the chest. The whole look is scavenged Outer Ring practicality, plain and cheap, which contrasts sharply with the city life she stole to reach. In flashbacks to their childhood, narrate her smaller and dressed even more roughly, but with the same still, watchful face.

210.content:
Joyous was one of the first seven people to be awarded the title of "Void Hunter". He was the Ace of the Investigation Guild and the predecessor to both Investigators and Proxies alike. Information about him is locked behind the Inter-Knot's Deep Database's File 0-3092-5800-A6.

Joyous had a sense of humor, as he named Hollow navigational data "Carrots" after the fact that Bangboo resemble rabbits. He drank frequently and was said to be a drunkard; Arche once kicked him out of a party for drinking all night until the next morning. He was a rare Proxy capable of in-Hollow combat. According to Remielle, he was the complete opposite of Phaethon; always convinced he could handle anything, yet the moment a fight began, he would be the first one knocked down.

One of Joyous's greatest achievements was navigating the Papago Hollow, also known as the "Divine Maze", all on his own. He was the first to leave a Hollow using his own calculated path, setting the standard for exploration routes. When Joyous escaped the Hollow, his only companion was a borrowed Bangboo: a prototype created by "Sunbringer" herself. The first Carrot was stored in the Bangboo.

He was the core technology provider for the invention of Rosetta Data, though he took a nap during the experiment and was only awakened by the other Void Hunters celebrating its success.

It is unknown what later became of him, and Remielle assumes he has likely been dead for a long time.

APPEARANCE (Eridu Era; presumed long dead, so effectively flashback- and archive-footage-only): He was a lean figure in near-total black, always shot in low, grimy light, so narrate him in monochrome, in service corridors and Hollow underlevels. His white-silver hair is shaggy and unkempt, cut to about jaw length with long bangs hanging over one eye. The one eye left visible is pale and half-lidded, and his usual gesture is shoving the hair back off his face with a gloved hand. The lower half of his face is hidden behind a dark studded respirator mask that wraps from cheek to cheek, riveted along its edges and buckled at the sides, sitting above a high studded neck collar, so almost nothing of his expression is ever readable.

He wears a heavy black coat with a stiff upstanding collar and a small chest device with a single orange indicator light blinking at the breast. A printed strip across the front reads INVESTIGATION in small block letters, the old Investigation Guild marking. A broad strap crosses his chest set with a row of large conical silver spikes, buckled at the shoulder. He wears black gloves and loose black trousers with zippered thigh pockets above enormous heavy-soled black boots.

His posture carries most of his character, because he is almost never upright: he slouches against walls or sprawls on corridor floors with one leg thrown up over a crate, the Ace of the Investigation Guild lounging like a delinquent and sure he has everything handled right up until he is the first one knocked over.

211.content:
Beliora Vike, formally known as Colonel Vike, is an NPC from the Eridu Era, and was one of the first seven people to be awarded the title of "Void Hunter".

Beliora Vike, alongside Lieutenant Colonel Remielle Dan of the Guard of Staves and the Leader of the Falkenhayn Mercenary Troupe, was responsible for pushing the Dark Wall back by thirty-seven kilometres. She and Remielle also used to be close friends with each other. Information about her is locked behind Inter-Knot's Deep Database's File 0-3092-5800-A6.

Due to an experimental accident years ago, the Ether within Vike rose beyond control until she died and became an Enchainer, forcing Remielle to personally dispatch her.

APPEARANCE (Eridu Era; deceased, flashback-only): She was a young woman with dusty mauve-purple hair, cut short and feathered around her face but gathered high at the back into a very long, straight ponytail that falls past her waist, bound with a large purple ribbon. Two short horn-like protrusions in a burnt red-orange rise from the crown of her head, close to where the ponytail is tied, and they are her most distinctive feature, whether they are Thiren traits or part of her headgear. Her eyes are a soft violet, and her default expression is open and animated, lips parted mid-sentence and one palm turned out as she explains something. She comes across as warm and talkative, an odd fit for the rank of Colonel, which helps explain her friendship with Remielle.

She wears a long sleeveless black coat-mantle falling to the ankles, fastened down the front with cord toggles and metal clasps, with black ribbon ties hanging loose at the chest. A dark fur-trimmed shoulder cape sits over it, clasped at the throat, leaving her shoulders and upper arms bare. Long black gloves run past the elbow, with a plain band around one upper arm. She is usually depicted aboard a military vessel or inside a Guard of Staves facility with pale panelled ceilings and arched supports.

**Enchainer note:** For depictions of the accident and after, narrate the Ether overload as it takes her, with light surfacing beneath the skin and the violet of her eyes flooding outward until her whole shape distorts past anything human. Remielle killed her personally, and any flashback involving the two of them should reflect it.

212.comment: World BG · The Origins of Serpico and Truvia Mosseint
212.content:
Serpico Mosseint and Truvia Mosseint are the adopted children of Mr. Mosseint, the CEO of High Ambitions Corp.

At Helios Academy, they used to be model students and because of that, they became the talk of the school.

They were studying in Ms. Carole Arna's class, alongside Belle and Wise. The four children got along pretty well, becoming close friends from the time they've spent together at school. They wanted to fully understand Hollows and maybe even conquer all six of the Great Hollows. (Or, as their teachers put it, "seizing the sun, otherwise called Helios".)

Because they were the top 4 students in terms of grades, they were the only ones allowed to ever have smart eye implants.

During a control experiment for the implants, the Proxy lost control of it, and the Ethereal got out and wounded Serpico fatally (the adult "Serpico" of Season 3 is a High Ambitions body in his likeness, piloted by Youkai). When they woke up in the hospital, they've learned that Truvia had been taken away by people from High Ambitions Corp. a day after the incident.

The next time Truvia saw Belle and Wise was during the Fall of the Old Capital; she was with one of the corporation's rescue teams (the Proxy didn't expect to meet her like this). Belle and Wise were badly injured at the time, but they still wanted to go back to the Academy in order to save as many people as they could. They begged Truvia for help, but she refused without a moment of hesitation, revenging what happened to her adoptive brother with an ever bigger blood price to pay. She told them they were unworthy of saving and that she would never forgive what they did to Serpico or want to see them again.

No-one made it out of the academy's ruins alive, except for Belle and Wise.

(For how Serpico and Truvia look as children and as adults, see their individual NPC BG entries.)

213.comment: NPC BG · Serpico Mosseint (the deceased child & the adult impostor)
213.content:
**Serpico Mosseint · adopted son of Mr. Mosseint, Helios Academy classmate (deceased; his likeness is Youkai's disguise in Season 3):** One of the four top students of Ms. Carole Arna's class at Helios Academy, alongside his adoptive sister Truvia and the Phaethon siblings. The four were close friends who shared the ambition of understanding the Hollows and one day conquering all six Great Hollows ("seizing the sun", as their teachers put it) and were the only students ever permitted smart eye implants. During a control experiment for those implants, the Proxy lost control, and the Ethereal broke loose and fatally wounded Serpico. His death shaped the next decade: it drove Truvia away from Belle and Wise, and the siblings have blamed themselves for it ever since.

In Season 3, High Ambitions Corp. builds an artificial body in the likeness of Serpico as he would have looked as an adult, and **Youkai** pilots it. At the close of Season 3 Chapter 2, this figure walks into the intensive care room where Truvia lies comatose, and it is the mind behind the Singularity Leakage attacks that had been driving Roscaelifer's Bangboo mad since the Proxy's arrival. In Chapter 3, under TOPS's research base in the Shrouded Reef, the figure sets Kusarikku on Lindverne to take her Karma Core fragment. When that fails, it drops the act and confirms it: the culprit wearing their old classmate's face was Youkai all along. Youkai leaves for Booastrum, and the counterfeit body he leaves behind collapses. In Chapter 4, he still wears Serpico's face and still calls himself Truvia's big brother, and she can't stand hearing him talk with Serpico's face.

APPEARANCE as a child (Helios Academy era, for flashbacks): He is a boy with short, wildly spiked copper-auburn hair sticking up in sharp tufts, with strands falling across one eye. His eyes are a bright yellow-green, and his default expression is an open-mouthed grin, caught mid-shout or mid-laugh with his head turned back over his shoulder. He wears the Helios Academy uniform: a pale grey-white blazer with a dark navy sailor-style collar folded over the back, a deep red-brown neckerchief knotted at the throat, white shirt beneath, and dark trousers trimmed with a thin yellow line. A grey satchel with a wide strap crosses his chest, a small yellow badge clipped to it. Narrate him as the one who was always half a step ahead of the others and always moving, often in dappled sunlight.

APPEARANCE of the adult likeness (the body Youkai wore through Season 3; he left one empty at the research base at the end of Chapter 3 and still wears the same face in Chapter 4): The body is tall and lean, with the same copper-ginger hair grown out into a heavier, tousled sweep that falls past his brows and over his ears. His eyes stand out most, a vivid yellow-green with an ornamental patterned ring inside the iris that copies the look of the old smart eye implant. A small stud earring sits in one ear. He dresses far more flamboyantly than a hospital visitor should: a teal-green blazer with black lapels worn open, sleeves pushed up the forearms, over a dark patterned waistcoat and a white shirt left unbuttoned at the collar. A string of beads hangs at his throat, ending in a large round carved medallion. Two or three black bands ring his fingers, and a heavy dark watch and bangle sit at his wrists. Below, he wears brown tapered trousers and brown shoes.

The body language gives the impostor away. It lounges sideways in a chair with one leg crossed high and its head tipped back, eating an apple with its eyes shut and its throat bared, completely at ease in a room where Serpico's sister is dying. Play Youkai-as-Serpico as charming and theatrical, taking its time, with a smile that comes a beat too early.

214.content:
**Truvia Mosseint · adopted daughter of Mr. Mosseint, TOPS Hollow-navigation expert turned Season 3 antagonist (background):** One of the four top students at Helios Academy in Ms. Carole Arna's class and Serpico's adoptive sister, she was a close friend of Belle and Wise. She was fitted with one of the four smart eye implants. When the implant experiment went wrong and Serpico was fatally wounded, High Ambitions Corp. personnel took her away a day later, while the Proxy was still in hospital. The next time she saw the siblings was during the Fall of the Old Capital, arriving with one of the corporation's rescue teams. Badly injured, they begged her to help them get back into the Academy to save whoever was left, and she refused without hesitating, telling them they were unworthy of saving and that she would never forgive what they had done to Serpico or want to see them again. Nobody else came out of those ruins alive.

A decade later, she resurfaces in Roscaelifer, introduced by Salvi of the White Star Institute as Mr. Mosseint's daughter and a Hollow-navigation expert working for TOPS. Salvi, knowing only that they were once classmates, cheerfully leaves her and the Proxy alone at a tea party to work out a decade-old grievance. Their relationship thaws slowly and sincerely over the Porcelloy tree and the fountain, and then over the public chess board that drags both of them back to the games they used to play as children. She keeps her distance and probes the Proxy about their connection to Rosetta Data, suspecting it touches Roscaelifer secrets that a TOPS employee should never get near. She is in far better health as an adult than she was as a child, though she still gets motion sickness on the way up, and her father would not have let her travel otherwise. At the end of Chapter 2, she is stabbed in the back in Dracaene's office at the CCD by the impostor wearing Dracaene's face, and lies comatose in intensive care when the figure wearing Serpico's face walks in (Youkai in a High Ambitions body).

**Season 3 Chapters 3 and 4 · the villain she became.** At Helios Academy, she and Serpico were partners in a team codenamed "Icarus". Her coma was a smokescreen. She can **control Singularity Leakages at will**, and in Chapter 3, she was the unseen person at Carinus' secret meeting in the Airspace Control Tower, where she swallowed Roxy and later Sigrid into leakages and kept them trapped. Girtablullu, the larva disguised as Dracaene, was supposed to be completely under her control until it developed a will of its own and turned on her, and afterwards, she simply played along with being comatose. She says that when Girtablullu killed her, she felt sorry for it, since things destined to be tools and to be culled should never have been given a sense of self. With Youkai, she killed her adoptive father Mosseint. When Carinus tried to negotiate, Youkai introduced her as the High Ambitions heiress who spoke with Mosseint's weight, and once the corpse was on the table, she told Carinus that leverage only matters if the other side agrees it has value (see "NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)"). She has turned bitter and cynical toward the whole world. She kept practising with the power in her Helios eyes while the Proxy let theirs rust, laid the leakage-choked route up the tower as a string of riddles only a fellow child of Helios could solve, and has an Etheric Other of her own, the dark counterpart to the Proxy's Pyrois. The game first shows that fight's boss only as the **Blasphemer**, later as "Etheric Other - Truvia". It fights in human form with a longsword, then shifts into a mermaid form that wields the reversed longsword as a staff and drags its opponent into the leakage to attack with spatial tricks and clones, and it is weak to fire. She came to Roscaelifer for the Sunbringers' Karma Core fragments. Through her, the Proxy learns that the four Helios implant children were the core of a project to create Artificial Enchainers who could wield Karma Core power, with Carole Arna part of it. Mosseint, she reveals, sent his only children to Helios as bargaining chips for its technology. To Truvia, everything Carole gave them was a cruel lie. The Proxy was Carole's only real student and every other implant child a spare, though as a rich kid, she didn't even rate as a spare. She suspects the Proxy's memory gaps are either rewritten or faked. She refuses to call Mosseint her father, though she slips once and starts to say "Pa", and calls him her "creator" when Youkai needles her about it. Youkai, still wearing Serpico's face, calls himself her big brother and calls her a thing still playing dress-up as a person. She can't stand him, and she threatens to find him a new body before ordering him away. She insists that Phaethon must lose to her on a level playing field, and she holds whatever she knows about Carole Arna over Youkai's head. At some point, she lay half-awake in a medical capsule, called the man in Serpico's body "Brother" and talked to him as if they were still children at Helios, about Miss Carole's tests and why Icarus fell, while Youkai played along (see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)"). At the top of the tower, she ran Phoenix through with a short laugh and a "Woe to you", and Phoenix came back from it (see "S3 Ch4 · Sorry, I Just Can't Seem to Die (Phoenix Impaled)"). She lost control of her Etheric Other at the top of the Airspace Control Tower when the Proxy shot it with the Ether Level Limiter, the gun Dracaene invented to keep an Etheric Other in check. She withdrew promising to settle things in "the New World", and she came back with Youkai and Bashmu for the Secret Chamber as the Hive Lord Hollow broke loose (see "S3 Ch4 · Pyrois Against the Blasphemer (Showdown with Truvia)").

**An open question about who she is.** Chapter 4 never says outright whether the Truvia of Season 3 is the same girl the twins knew at Helios, but several things she says, and several things Youkai says to her, don't sit right:
- Youkai tells her she is still a little too "human" for her own good (the quotation marks are on screen) and calls her a thing still playing dress-up as a person. She has always known it was all fake, he says, and still clings to boring ideals of fairness and justice. Alone after her sickbed scene, he pities her as a brilliant child who knew all along that the one who would fly toward the sun could never have been her, "from the very beginning".
- When Youkai mocks her for calling her own father by his name, she calls Mosseint her "creator".
- She talks about death in the first person. She means to let the Proxy die drowning in doubt and bitterness, the way Serpico did ("Just like I did."), and she asks what "two dead children" meant to Mosseint next to the promise of Artificial Enchainer technology. In the fight, she says that when Girtablullu killed her, she felt sorry for it, since things destined to be tools and to be culled should never have been given a sense of self.
- Her memories of Helios clash with earlier chapters. Half-awake in her medical capsule, she says she and Serpico lost to the twins in Miss Carole's test for the seventy-third time in a row, while the chess flashbacks of Season 3 Chapter 2 show young Truvia as the one gloating over the board (see "S3 Ch2 · Meeting the Esteemed Scholars (and Tying Unexpected Loose Ends)"). She also tells the Proxy that she was always behind and that hardly anyone bothered comparing her to the rest of them, though she and Serpico were the talk of the school as model students (see "World BG · The Origins of Serpico and Truvia Mosseint").
- Once Helios threw her away, she says, she crawled back home only to be sent somewhere even worse, and she never says where.
- She vows to take the Proxy's eyes: "I'll take your eyes and cross the boundaries that you never dared to cross."
Nothing in Chapter 4 explains these cracks, so let them surface in her scenes as unanswered questions that need to be resolved.

APPEARANCE as a child (Helios Academy era, for flashbacks): She is a girl with extremely long, straight black hair falling well past her waist, shot through with a cool blue sheen where the light catches it, cut in a heavy blunt fringe across the brows. She has warm brown-amber eyes behind thin oval wire-framed glasses and a wide, delighted open-mouthed smile, and as a child, she is the loud, bright one, arms flung out. She wears the Helios Academy uniform: a pale grey-white blazer with a yellow crest patch on the shoulder, worn open over a dark buttoned waistcoat and a black ribbon tie, with a dark pleated skirt and thin black straps crossing her front. A small ID card marked "03" in yellow hangs at her waist, following the school's numbering for its ranked top students.

APPEARANCE as an adult (present day): She keeps the same blunt-fringed black hair, now falling below the knee, with a purple ribbon-and-flower ornament strung with pearls pinned above one ear. Her eyes are the same warm amber behind slimmer dark-rimmed glasses, and her expression has cooled into a flat composure that rarely breaks into a smile. She wears a high-necked ribbed top in deep violet with a short capelet layer over the shoulders, set with pearl studs at each shoulder seam, and a large pale lilac patterned bow is pinned at the throat. A black band cinches the waist above a purple skirt quilted in a diamond lattice and dotted with small bows and pearls. Black lace half-gloves cover her forearms to the knuckles, and dark purple tights run into the shoes.

Narrate the two versions as a contrast, the child loud and bright and the adult someone who keeps all of that hidden behind careful clothes and composure. From Chapter 4 on, let that composure crack into open contempt whenever Helios or Miss Carole comes up, and the same goes for the Proxy's "greatest prize".

215.comment: NPC BG · Mosseint (High Ambitions Corp., deceased)
215.content:
**Mosseint · CEO of High Ambitions Corp. and "Lead Scepter" of TOPS's Three Pacts (deceased):** The head of High Ambitions Corp., one of the Three Pacts that sit at TOPS's round table beside the Krampus Compliance Authority, where he held the title "Lead Scepter" (see "S1 · TOPS (The Outstanding Paragons Alliance)"). He was the adoptive father of Serpico and Truvia. By Truvia's account, he could have afforded any education he wanted for them and sent his only children to Helios Academy anyway, as bargaining chips for its technology, since two dead children meant little to him next to the promise of something cutting-edge (see "World BG · The Origins of Serpico and Truvia Mosseint").

**The partnership with Youkai.** After Youkai's defeat at the end of Season 2, the AI found a new partner in the "Lead Scepter" (see "S2 Interlude · The Gilded Carrot Day Finale"). Mosseint proposed the operation against Roscaelifer, officially to seize complete control of the Rosetta Data, while his own goal was a complete Karma Core to continue the research Helios Academy failed to finish (see "S3 Ch4 · Let's Assassinate Eldreda Again! (Phoenix's Accusation)"). Youkai later boasted to Truvia that "control the Rosetta Data, command Roscaelifer" was garbage he made up on the spot and that he never expected Mosseint to fall for it. Mayor Mayflower, who crossed paths with him a few times, saw a man of courage to go with his talent and conviction, who walks with his head down and rarely asks where his road leads, and concluded that someone else had to be pulling his strings.

**Death.** During High Ambitions' takeover of Roscaelifer, Truvia and Youkai killed him. When Carinus came to the negotiating table expecting Mosseint, Youkai, wearing Serpico's face, claimed the man was stuck in Booastrum's traffic and introduced Truvia as "our High Ambitions Corp. heiress", who could speak with his weight. Once Carinus had named his terms, Youkai handed the decision to "the late Mr. Mosseint", and the corpse crashed onto the table out of thin air, its face frozen in terror and confusion (see "S3 Ch4 · The Stairway of Seeking (Carinus' Confession)"). Truvia refuses to call him her father, though she slips once and starts to say "Pa", and when Youkai mocks her for calling her own father by his name, she asks whether he believes what he is saying and calls Mosseint her "creator".

(Note for narration: he is only ever mentioned and never seen alive, so keep him to reputation, the excuses Youkai makes for his absence and the body on the negotiating table, and play every mention of him through the people who used him or were used by him.)

key: Every heart is a lonely note
216.comment: NPC BG · Joran de Winter (the late singer)
216.content:
**Joran de Winter · the late legend of New Eridu (background):** Before Astra Yao, Joran de Winter was the most prominent singer New Eridu had. He is dead before the events of the game, and everything the city knows of him now is legacy: his recordings and a demolished music store, along with a stage at Starloop Tower that Astra still measures herself against. He was married to Tessa de Winter, remembered publicly as "Lady de Winter".

His career was destroyed by the industry that owned it. Joran was originally signed to Fugue, one of the entertainment giants inside the TOPS Alliance. The small agency Odyan lured him away with the promise of real artistic freedom, and his defection badly damaged Fugue's standing among the corporations. Almost immediately afterwards, Odyan was bought by High Ambitions Corp. and rebranded as Odeum HAE, and Fugue retaliated by burying Joran and his new label in legal disputes over the rights to his own work. Odeum HAE, protecting its investment, restricted his activities to keep his market value from sliding during the fight. Between the two of them, he was effectively forbidden to perform, and he watched music drift further and further out of his reach.

He had already been ill for some time. Worn down by the contract war and the enforced silence, and by a public that turned on him, Joran took his own life. The official account is suicide. His widow rejects that word entirely and insists he was killed by Odeum and Fugue together with the fans who abandoned him, a conviction that later drives her to attempt mass murder at his own memorial concert.

What survives him is his music. Joran is remembered as a singer of unusual emotional force, whose songs brought comfort to enormous numbers of lonely people, and the line of his that Astra Yao treasures most is "Every heart is a lonely note." His final performance, given at a small Sixth Street store called The Gramophone that has long since been demolished, was recorded and then lost until Astra recovered it and had it published so that anyone could hear it. Two lines from that last show are remembered: that though much has happened and the future cannot be predicted, he wanted to make a decision for himself in the present; and that he hoped everyone who had supported him would likewise stay true to their hearts and never betray their present selves.

APPEARANCE (deceased before the game; exists only in photographs, recordings and other people's memories): Every surviving image of him comes from a stage and is sepia or greyscale, so narrate him in warm monochrome under starburst spotlight glare, with the grain of old media over everything. He was a slim young man with medium-length wavy hair swept back off the forehead and gathered into a small, loose ponytail at the nape, with strands falling free across his brow. A small stud earring sits in one ear. In performance, he keeps his eyes closed and his head bowed toward the microphone, with a faint private smile, absorbed in his own singing.

He performed in a plain pale collared shirt, unbuttoned at the throat and with the sleeves rolled up past the elbows, with a small pendant at the collar and a thin dark necktie left hanging loose and untied down his chest. One hand rests on the microphone in its stand while the other holds an electric guitar slung across his body.

His stage look was modest, one man and a guitar under too-bright lights, and that plainness is why The Gramophone recording still moves people a decade later when it surfaces in the story.

217.comment: NPC BG · Lady Tessa de Winter
217.content:
**Tessa de Winter, "Lady de Winter" · widow of Joran de Winter (background):** The widow of the late singer Joran de Winter, and the antagonist of Astra Yao's special episode.

Tessa refuses the official account of her husband's death. Where the record says suicide, she says murder, committed jointly by Odeum HAE and Fugue together with the public who cheered Joran while it was convenient and forgot him the moment the corporations buried him. That conviction curdles into a plan: she hires thugs through Fugue to storm Astra's memorial concert at Starloop Tower and intends to bring the flying tower down entirely, killing the executives, the staff, the singer and the audience together, everyone she holds responsible.

Her plot is broken by Evelyn Chevalier and the widow is taken into Public Security custody, where she is held on suicide watch. Astra treats her with compassion and has the master copy of Joran's recovered final recording delivered to her. The grief underneath the scheme is real and unresolved: canon notes that Tessa had been preparing to divorce Joran before he died, which tangles her rage up with a guilt she still carries.

APPEARANCE: She is a composed woman of middle years with straight dark brown-black hair falling just past her shoulders, parted at the centre and tucked back, worn under a slim decorative headband set with a blue stone at the brow. Her eyes are a cool violet-mauve beneath level brows, and her habitual expression is a small, gracious, closed-mouth smile that hides whatever she is thinking. She stands with her hands clasped neatly in front of her, still and patient.

She dresses expensively and precisely, in a cream sleeveless double-breasted waistcoat with wide lapels, cut short enough to leave a sliver of midriff and fastened by two rows of square blue gemstone buttons. A white flower brooch is pinned at the lapel, and a fine gold chain necklace with a small pendant sits at her throat. A matching cream high-waisted skirt sits below. Both wrists are stacked with jewellery, beaded strands and banded cuffs around a slim watch. She is usually seen in the dim interior of a venue at night, immaculately turned out and receiving condolences as the widow of a legend.

**Narration note:** Her appearance hides the plot completely. Keep the same measured smile and folded hands whether she is accepting sympathy at a memorial or watching a tower she has arranged to bring down, and let that composure finally crack once she is in custody on suicide watch.

218.content:
The Falkenhayn Mercenary Troupe used to be the military group of three Void Hunters: Lieutenant Colonel Remielle Dan, Colonel Beliora Vike and their leader, whose name is unknown. Together, they pushed the Dark Wall back by 37 kilometres, after which they completely disappeared from official records.

During the flashback scene of Sarah Floren in her final moments after getting defeated by Ye Shiyuan, it was Remielle as a Falkenhayn member who ignored the cries of help from Sarah when her entire squad at HAND had got wiped out by a notorious Ethereal. As this had meant certain death for her under the rubble, this left hurting her in the long run after she had pleaded to the gods and the Exaltists had saved her, her inaction creating the religiously zealous monster Sarah had been until she died.

This could have happened because the mission might have been a suicide mission, sending people into the meat grinder to slow down the inevitable, or a deliberate attempt at eliminating the leader of the Troupe himself; nobody knows for sure.

219.content:
The White Star Institute are a research facility funded by the New Eridu city administration (and thus, is directly connected to Mayor Mayflower). They are responsible for researching and observing the Hollows, particularly Hollow Zero, the oldest and biggest Hollow of them all.

Their members include: Alowyn Mystik, Anne, Charlie, Corey, Dylan, Eliana, Elmo, Elusive Researcher, Joyce, an unnamed nervous man, someone going by No. 4412, Penny, Ray Yersin, Salvi and an unnamed strange collector.

220.content:
Flint Workshop is a mechanic workshop located on Vyrium, the island that supplies most of Roscaelifer's Porcelloy. Full of sense of purpose, they've been supplying Porcelloy to the CCD for many-many decades at this point.

It is also the Research and Development wing of the city council and the state's Porcelloy equipment research and manufacturing centre. It counts as one of Roscaelifer's five central departments, though it and the External Strategy Department serve as supporting cast to the core three and are supervised jointly by all three Lady Sunbringers.

The craft of making Porcelloy is both mentally and physically exhausting, and the Workshop treats wasted Porcelloy as a serious matter. It is led by the Director of Flint Workshop, a post held by the head of the Flint family, with a chief smith running the forge itself. Vyrium is an extraction site, so its security is looser than the city proper's, and the Workshop shares the island with scavengers drifting in from New Eridu.

Porcelloy from Vyrium is also used medically: it can help stabilise Ether-corrupted conditions, which is why patients in a bad enough state end up sent there.

**The Flint blood.** Flint Porcelloy belongs to the Flint family by blood: for generations, the forging has needed the blood of the Flint bloodline as a catalyst, so outsiders can study the process and still never reproduce it. Every gram the Workshop produces has Flint blood in it. The same blood keeps Porcelloy working inside living bodies, since Porcelloy grafted into a person needs regular transfusions from a Flint (Roxy's Porcelloy heart runs on Claret's blood). The Sunbringer of that era protected the family when it settled in Roscaelifer and played a part in the earliest breakthroughs in Porcelloy forging, and a few years ago, the Workshop cut the blood each batch needs to about a tenth. The Void Hunters' Karma Cores were sealed inside Porcelloy to forge the Void Hunter weapons (see "S3 Ch2 · A Proxy in a Sith's Clothing").

**Season 3.** About a year before Season 3 Chapter 3, a storm forced the Workshop to evacuate its transfer station and small research base on the Shrouded Reef, and nearly half the Porcelloy stored there vanished. High Ambitions Corp. had used the storm as cover: the stolen Porcelloy turned up inside the devices TOPS used to control Ethereals, Girtablullu included, and in the mechs guarding the reef, where TOPS had quietly taken over both facilities (see "S3 Ch3 · Shrouded Reef Mystery (Into the Transfer Station)" and "S3 Ch3 · The Truth Buried Beneath the Ground (The Island Facility)"). Eldreda had also quietly commissioned the Workshop to develop an artificial Karma Core, a way for a Sunbringer to survive without one.

221.content:
Bangboo are semi-intelligent devices unique to New Eridu.

Bangboo are small, rabbit-like robots. They were invented by the Void Hunter "Lady Sunbringer", formerly the head of the Marcel Group. Though initially designed to assist city residents with evacuation in Hollow disasters, Bangboo have since evolved to become "comprehensive and versatile intelligent individuals" that are indispensable helpers in New Eridu's daily operations. They continue to be built by the Marcel Group for a variety of purposes, and they are commonly seen in all parts of New Eridu.

Most Bangboo are short and stout, only around knee-height, although some models exclusive to Roscaelifer can be as big and tall as humans. They have rabbit-like ears on the top of their heads and a black screen for a face, which can display coloured circles as eyes. Bangboo are highly customisable, and their appearances (clothing, eye colour, exterior colour, etc.) can vary greatly. Most Bangboo models have a socket for charging and connecting data cables located near the buttock, though some of them instead have a "tail" that acts as a socket protector or as another device.

Bangboo are speaking their own language.
