Their language only consists of 15 + 3 syllables ("e", "ehn", "na", "ne", "wa", "ta", "uhn", "nuh", "wuh", "zhu", "chi", "to", "boo", "wo" and "no", with the extra syllables "gah", "ho" and "ni" being considered a posh accent that only special Bangboo can pronounce), due to technical limitations of the era when Lady Sunbringer designed them. Because of this, they require a translator for humanoids (aka. humans, Thirens and more humanoid robots of the Intelligent Construct type) to understand. Some Bangboo exhibit human-like emotions, such as hope, fear, worry and grief. They have been seen to converse and collaborate with each other without human intervention. However, unlike Intelligent Constructs, Bangboo do not have free will and they are not eligible for New Eridu citizenship, although, some models that are exclusive to the sky archipelago of Roscaelifer exhibit that free will their surface versions don't, making them eligible for Roscaelifer citizenship.

Bangboo are mechanical in nature and require charging. In Roscaelifer, however, they can also regain energy from food made just for Bangboo, like bread and pastries specially made for the taste buds and nutrient needs of a Bangboo and its inherent mechanical design. Many factories provide customisation services to allow for specific Bangboo functions, aside from every unit having built-in recording systems. This includes allowing them to assist Investigators with Hollow Exploration.

222.content: Securityboo are Bangboo that work for New Eridu Public Security. These Bangboo typically use the same model as Officer Cui and are tasked with various jobs, such as escorting pedestrians in Lumina Square.

223.content:
Combat Bangboo, similar to Agents, are obtainable units in Zenless Zone Zero. They come in different Ranks (Bangboo Rank A-Rank or Bangboo Rank S-Rank) and may be aligned with an Attribute (Physical, Ice, Fire, Electric, or Ether), and some belong to a Faction.

As a companion in battle, each Combat Bangboo has unique abilities. In addition to using active skills to support the squad in battle, some Combat Bangboo will also have an additional Bangboo Chain Attack. Bangboo Chain Attacks do not count toward the total number of Chain Attacks and have a cooldown, so it can only be used again after the cooldown ends.

There also used to be a special model of Combat Bangboo called the High-Firepower Combat Bangboo, but due to their high failure rate and difficulty to maintain them, they got discontinued. A notable example of a High-Firepower Combat Bangboo was Lockspring, the last of his kind before he died. He was one of the prototypes of the Bangboo that live in Roscaelifer, capable of showing free will and even of speaking the Universal Language, the language of humans.

224.content:
Asha is the rabbit full Thiren proprietor and manager of Godfinger, an arcade on Sixth Street, right next to Random Play. She is usually found only within the arcade itself, but occasionally appears on the streets to offer quests or to speak with characters during Trust events.

APPEARANCE: Long, wavy ash-blonde hair falls past her chest, streaked with purple at the front and one side and topped by a single curved lime-green antenna strand. A purple barrette lettered "POINT" pins the hair back above one ear. Her eyes are bright yellow behind black rectangular glasses with purple inner rims. She wears a lime-green tee printed with a large black "GM" logo and a scattered pattern of arcade-stick icons, over a purple undershirt showing at the collar and hem, with a purple hooded vest hung off her shoulders. A lime "PLAYER 1" strap crosses her hips above a black utility belt loaded with pouches, a holstered lime-green handheld console, a clipped-on portable device trailing an orange cable and a takeaway coffee cup slung in a green carabiner holder. One arm is covered by a lime-green sleeve with a white stripe and a black fingerless glove; the other is bare. Below, she wears dark blue distressed flared jeans and black open-toe heeled sandals.

225.content:
Howl is a husky dog who runs Howl's Newsstand, the small newspaper kiosk on Sixth Street, sat beside Bardic Needle and just outside Random Play. He is simply a dog, and nobody in New Eridu thinks it needs explaining: he wears clothes and holds down a business, and the whole street treats him as a perfectly ordinary neighbourhood proprietor (still cute, though). The kiosk opens up to the Proxies once the Interlude commission is underway.

The stand sells the day's newspaper, which is Sixth Street's in-world source of headlines and gossip, and sells scratch cards that pay out in Dennies or Polychromes depending on the buyer's luck. Howl is a fixture of the street's daily rhythm and turns up across a long list of Trust invites and side events; when business is slow, he is usually found asleep at his post.

A near-identical kiosk stands in Lumina Square, but that one is run by someone named Eve.

APPEARANCE: He is a Siberian husky with the classic black-and-white mask, black over the ears, crown and back and white on the face, muzzle, chest and legs, with pale blue eyes. He sits upright on his haunches like any dog would, and every claw is painted bright green. He wears a dark green baseball jersey with white pinstripes, buttoned down the front, with a white number on the sleeve. A red-and-white "WOOF" patch is stitched at the collar. Around his neck is a grey-and-black patterned collar with an orange buckle, hung with a round brass tag and a white name badge printed with his name and a paw print beside a cartoon husky. A black canvas pouch marked "NEW" is strapped at his shoulder, holding a chunky yellow handheld dispenser.

226.content:
General Chop is the owner of the restaurant Waterfall Soup on Sixth Street. He has a son, Chop Junior, who works at the Waterfall Soup in Lumina Square. He is quite stubby and red-skinned. His black hair shows signs of aging, and he has a big moustache, while a pair of giant mechanical exoskeletal hands attached to his back helps him be more productive at soup-making.

APPEARANCE: He is a short, wide, heavyset man with flat red skin and a broad, jowly face. Thick brows and a huge outswept moustache, both black and heavily streaked with white, frame large round eyes with small black irises. Fine white whisker-lines mark his cheeks above a black beard that outlines his jaw, and black hair spikes out at the temples beneath a square white chef's cap stitched in red dashes. He wears a white kimono-style chef's jacket with a red-trimmed crossed lapel over matching wide white trousers and dark brown geta with red straps, and a pair of small brown fish-shaped charms hangs from cords at his collar. A harness on his back carries two pairs of oversized articulated arms built from bright green bamboo-like tubes and black joints, laced with orange hydraulic lines and tipped with padded black grippers.

227.content:
Chop Junior is an NPC located in Lumina Square. He runs the Waterfall Soup store located there. His father is General Chop. He looks mostly like his father, complete with the additional exoskeletal hands on his back, but with fully black hair and no moustache.

APPEARANCE: He has the same short, red-skinned build and broad face as his father but looks visibly younger, with thick solid-black brows, a clean upper lip, black hair streaked white only at the temples and a black beard outline along the jaw, above large round eyes with small black irises and white whisker-lines on the cheeks. He wears the identical uniform: a square white chef's cap stitched in red dashes, a white chef's jacket with a red-trimmed crossed lapel, small brown fish-shaped charms hanging at the collar, and the same back-mounted harness of green bamboo-like mechanical arms with black joints and padded grippers.

228.content:
The Tin Master is a model of Intelligent Construct found working at Coff Cafe's across New Eridu. The Tin Master model is used by Coff Cafe to serve as baristas for their chain of coffee shops. The specifics of the model are otherwise unknown, but all Tin Masters known are shown to be programmed to be exceptionally good at making coffee and to treat it with great care, as an art form. They are highly resistant to people who drink coffee without consideration for their health, often dissuading people from drinking too much of it whenever possible.

A version of him is present at every known branch of Coff Cafe. There is also a Tin Master stationed at a much smaller version of the shop, Tin Master's Coffee, in Failume Heights. Four Tin Masters are known, stationed at Sixth Street, Lumina Square, Failume Heights and Roscaelifer's Booastrum District. The Booastrum unit is a Type T model.

APPEARANCE: It is a humanoid Intelligent Construct built around a coffee machine. Its head is polished steel shaped like a stovetop percolator, with a glass brewing dome and a small filled cup balanced on top. Brass valve fittings and a round pressure gauge are set into one side, and a wooden grinder crank juts out across the face as a nose. A dark visor panel holds two small white rectangular eyes; below sits a moulded silver handlebar moustache and a small pierced grille for a mouth, with a hose running from the back of the head down the body. It wears a black long-sleeved uniform under a bright orange bib apron printed with white line-art of coffee cups and pots, with pens in the chest pocket and a pouch at the hip. An orange cable is plugged in at the waist. Its arms are slim articulated grey struts ending in rounded white gloved hands.

229.comment: NPC BG · Tin Master Type T
229.content:
A special version of the Tin Master robot, specialised in making British-style tea and bringing the best flavours out of it. The Booastrum District unit staffs Cuppa Moment, Roscaelifer's chain of teahouses, next door to Roarin' Brekkies.

APPEARANCE: It uses the same chassis as a standard Tin Master, refinished in cream enamel and rebuilt around tea. A dark green teapot sits on a stem atop its head beneath a dark handle bar, with matching dark caddy units on either side of the skull feeding thin metal steam pipes down to the shoulders. A pale circular emblem is set into the forehead above a recessed dark visor, and a large curled dark-brown handlebar moustache is moulded across the face over a three-hole grille. It wears a cream butler's shirt with a stiff pointed collar and a dark green tie under a long dark olive apron pinned with a small brass name plate, with black articulated arms ringed in brass at the elbows and rounded white gloved hands.

230.content:
Sweety is the manager and public face of Yum Cha Sin, the teahouse in Failume Heights on the Waifei Peninsula. She first appears in Season 2 Chapter 1 (v2.0) and handles everything front-of-house. She greets customers and seats a permanently overbooked queue by number, and she runs tabs for regulars like Mr. Dong.

She is brisk and warm, and hard to rattle: she is as comfortable defusing an argument between a regular and a tourist committing crimes against rice noodle rolls as she is sending the Proxies out on a job. She is also candid enough to admit when a run leads somewhere most locals refuse to go.

APPEARANCE: She is a young woman with short ash-blonde hair, a stray strand standing up at the crown, worn with a long fringe sweeping over one eye and two short low braids bound in black-and-gold cuffs, with small dark buns trimmed in gold at the sides of her head. Her eyes are violet, and amber-tinted aviator sunglasses are pushed up onto her head. She wears a sleeveless navy-black qipao with a red mandarin-collar yoke across the shoulders, fastened by a round gold brooch with a teardrop-shaped window to her cleavage under it. A keyhole cutout laced in red sits at the chest above a gold coin-shaped medallion at the waist, and the long skirt is slit to the hip on both sides over red lining and embroidered with a coiled emblem near the hem. She wears black fingerless gloves and a doubled black band around one thigh above dark blue ankle-strap flats with red trim, and she carries a round rigid Chinese fan printed with mahjong-tile motifs.

231.content:
A-Shuo is the dog who runs the Temple Divination at Suibian Temple in Failume Heights, on the Waifei Peninsula. He was raised by Yixuan as a pup and suffered Corruption at some point in his youth; Yixuan suspects that episode is the source of his unusual sensitivity to Ether, which in time developed into a real ability to perceive fate. To put the talent to use, she set him up with a stall of his own so he could read fortunes for others.

He has spent eleven years keeping Suibian Temple standing almost single-handedly after the mystics of Yunkui Summit were forced to leave, and he is diligent about it to a fault. A reading works by rolling three trigram dice; whichever symbols land face-up form the basis of the fortune he gives. Yixuan introduces him to Phaethon during the Season 2 commission Where Tigers Lurk and Dragons Hide.

APPEARANCE: He is a large dog with dark charcoal-grey fur and a long white mane that sweeps back from his crown and down his neck like slicked-back hair. His eyes are red, worn behind narrow red-lensed sunglasses with a gold bridge that sit low on his muzzle. He wears a jade-green sleeveless jacket with a high collar, wrapped by a red talisman sash marked in white script that runs around the collar and over one shoulder, with a small round gold ornament hanging at the chest. His front left leg is a prosthetic: a black-and-grey armoured shoulder cap over a carbon-fibre shin, jointed at the wrist and ending in a curved blade foot with an exposed piston. A navy harness across his back carries a large white disc ringed in dark navy and set with three black studs around a central boss, backed by a quilted blue band and a hanging cloth flap. He is usually found sitting on a woven mat at his stall in Suibian Temple.

232.content:
Mr. Roar is the bear-mascot proprietor of Roarin' Brekkies, the breakfast stall on Beckford Street in Roscaelifer's Booastrum District, next door to the Cuppa Moment teahouse and directly outside Amber Hall, where Phaethon stay. He speaks in a permanent mascot register, punctuating his sentences with "rawrr." He sells pancakes and baked treats alongside snack surprise boxes, each of which yields a collectible card that can be traded back to him for Dennies and Lucky Bottle Caps.

The Proxies meet him in Season 3 Chapter 1, when Velina arranges tea at Cuppa Moment and pancakes next door as a welcome. His design is recognisable enough across the district that full Mr. Roar mascot suits circulate as merchandise, which is how he comes to be indirectly involved in two separate incidents where somebody else is walking around wearing his face.

APPEARANCE: He is a stout, rounded brown bear figure standing upright in chef's whites, with big round ears, a lighter tan muzzle and a small black nose. His eyes are a pair of round brass-rimmed goggle-glasses, set with a red gem on one hinge and a green one on the other, whose dark lenses display yellow pixel-art crescents. On his head sits a tall chef's toque built to look like a stack of pancakes, its pleats golden-brown beneath white zigzag scalloping and crowned with an actual pancake stack dripping black chocolate syrup, topped with banana slices and mint leaves. He wears a white double-breasted chef's coat with large brass buttons and short cuffed sleeves, cinched by a broad black cummerbund, with a black scarf knotted at the throat above a chequerboard chest patch pinned with a small pink bow tie. The coat falls to the knee with a large breakfast-food print across the lower skirt. His paws are tan padded mittens with cream cuffs, and a gold chevron-patterned band circles one ankle.

233.content:
Zeppelin is a female anthropomorphic fox Thiren (full Thiren) who runs her own business, The Fuzzy Wrench, an all-in-one Bangboo maintenance shop on Roscaelifer's Gear Street. She belongs to the Roscaelifer Merchant Delegation, the city's merchant association. Like Enzo in New Eridu, she is a Bangboo repair technician by trade and already excels at it, and she kept pushing further to develop gentler, more comprehensive care services, which is how The Fuzzy Wrench came to be. Safe to say, her love for Bangboo runs deep.

**The shop.** In Zeppelin's words, the Bangboo of Gear Street need everyday services as much as humans do, and The Fuzzy Wrench exists to provide them. The shop is popular, and any Bangboo is welcome there. Humans cannot be customers; she says so with an apology and is happy to chat with them anyway. Her usual offer is the signature package, a full-body cleaning in the shop's Bangboo washing machine with a free face mask included. She upgraded that machine herself. By her account, it cleans almost as well as the manual service, in which she clears the dust out of a Bangboo's insides by hand and tops up its coolant and lubricant. That service costs around 100,000 Dennies, so she rarely recommends it. Repairboo works at the shop as well (see "Side Quest · Season 3 Chore — Fixing Roscaelifer's Bangboo").

**With her customers.** Zeppelin holds that Bangboo are pure-hearted and respond to gentle care and sincere praise, which makes looking after their feelings as important as looking after their bodies. A nervous customer is told that the shop has never had a safety incident and that the shell only comes off so the dust inside can be cleared. She keeps chatting with them through the whole wash. Her advice is to clear the Logic Core and switch off the screen while cool water and air carry the grime away, after which, she promises, a Bangboo even thinks faster. She takes the strangest Bangboo in stride. Her manner is casual and bright, and she hails passers-by with "Need Bangboo care? Come on down to The Fuzzy Wrench~" With a stranger, she says "sir" or "miss" until she learns the name.

**The pen pal ("Misplaced Letter", v3.2).** For years, Zeppelin paid for a little Bangboo's dream of travelling the world. He wrote to her as Curitt, the name of a real Bangboo whose sponsorship he had hijacked. She never saw him and knew only that he was a black Bangboo. At his request, she dropped her replies into the red mailbox nearest the shop and picked up his letters herself. One morning, his letter closed with a farewell. He was settling down and needed no more of her support, he wrote, and they might not stay in touch. She feared he was hiding serious trouble. With a day of orders booked well in advance keeping her at the shop, she accepted the Proxy's offer to look for him.

What she kept to herself was that she had seen through him early on. His letters carried no postmark. They also came through a mailbox that any local shop owner knew to be abandoned. She had also signed a new funding agreement with the real Curitt, which made the impersonation pointless. Curiosity about who would try such a clumsy scam kept her paying at first, and concern took over once she saw how hard a time he was having. His stories sounded familiar because he lifted them from films, yet the life he put into them moved her all the same.

The pen pal was Slenderboo, the tall black Bangboo behind a local urban legend (see "NPC BG · Slenderboo (Pixel Fairy Tale)" for his side of that night). He came to the shop hidden in a Mr. Roar costume and tried to confess, and Zeppelin calmly told him that she already knew. When he called himself the thing from the urban legend, she finished the description for him. He wondered how she knew, and she said, "It's a secret." She asked him not to let his sadness shut her out, since she wanted to hear stories about the real him. First, though, his worn-out parts were getting the deluxe treatment. She has looked out for him ever since.

**Cyber Miracle Healer (v3.3 event).** A Bangboo calling himself "Master Developer" tried to end a quarrel between "DC Guru" and "AC Guardian" over which charging current tastes better by offering them his "AC-DC Instant Switcheroo Chip", which was meant to blend any current to its user's taste. AC Guardian swallowed one, and the virus it carried sent him hopping about with no control over his body. Hardware is Zeppelin's trade. A software virus was beyond her, so she turned to the Proxy, whose skill with software she had heard about. Over the following days, the Proxy repaired him along with four more Bangboo who came in infected, and the repairs cleared out their computational junk together with the virus. After days of acrobatics forced on them by the virus, the five found they could dance, so they quit their jobs to form an idol group, the "Sweet-Savory Instant Switcheroo Dance Squad", with Master Developer as manager. Zeppelin took the news cheerfully. To her, Bangboo are odd little creatures with big imaginations, and a new calling is theirs to follow. She thanked the Proxy with a standing welcome at the shop, and she and those Bangboo call the Proxy "dear savior".

Where she and the shop stand after the Hive Lord Hollow broke loose over Booastrum at the end of Season 3 Chapter 4 is unknown (see "S3 Ch4 · The Hive Lord Hollow Swallows the Sky (End of Chapter 4)").

APPEARANCE: She is a ginger fox Thiren with a furred muzzle, orange over the cheeks and jaw and fading to cream around the eyes and mouth, with a small brown nose and tall brown ears lined with cream. Her dark brown hair is cut short with a thin braid running back over the crown, and her eyes are green with violet pupils. Orange mechanic's goggles are strapped over the top of her head, and a dark red collar carries a grey dog tag on a cord alongside a small green Bangboo-face charm. She wears a white halter crop top printed with three wrenches crossed like bones, with orange braces running over the shoulders. Her black detached sleeves carry orange-riveted studded shoulder caps above clawed fingerless gloves, and a lime-green device is strapped to one upper arm. A black jacket slashed with olive claw-marks is knotted around her waist over orange cargo trousers. Grey buckles and a small skull patch are fitted to the trousers, which also carry a draped chain, and her black tool belt has a drop-leg pouch of screwdrivers. Bolt-studded round knee pads sit above black lace-up open-toe sandals that leave her clawed paws bare, and a bushy cream-tipped tail hangs behind her.

234.content:
Slenderboo is a male Bangboo who lives in the sewers of Roscaelifer's Retroflux Zone, and he is the creature behind the Booastrum urban legend of the same name, a slender shadow said to come out in the dead of night and snatch children. The legend grew out of his looks alone. He first appears as a nameless shadow in Glitch Alley (v3.0), and the commission "Misplaced Letter" (v3.2) gives him his name and his story.

**How he was made.** During the development of a new Bangboo model, an error in the blueprint data printed him with the wrong proportions, and he ran away after overhearing that he was to be scrapped. No modification modules were ever installed in him, so his Logic Core cannot be separated from his body and he can never move into another one. He cannot speak the Bangboo language either. The Universal Language is the only one he has, picked up on his own in the movie theatre where he used to live, and he talks to humans without a translator. His charging port differs from the standard design, which makes street charging stations useless to him and keeps him running on old batteries.

**Life in the sewers.** When the theatre closed, he drifted down to the Retroflux Zone. No one would hire a Bangboo who looked like him, so he lived by theft, mostly of the old batteries that the waste sorters collect. Griff Ashton, the boss of the En-Nah Gang, let it pass as long as the gang's own Bangboo were left alone. Strangers met him with fear or thrown rocks. Since nobody would listen, he gave up explaining himself. He is deeply lonely, and much of what he knows about people comes from films.

**The pen pal.** For money, he stole the identity of Curitt, a Bangboo sponsored by Zeppelin of The Fuzzy Wrench, and wrote to her as a traveller seeing the world, filling his letters with scenes from films and stories he had overheard. Writing to her made him happy. The happier he became, the heavier it weighed on him that she was talking to a fake, and he started helping other Bangboo in the hope of ending the lie and meeting her one day as himself. Zeppelin had seen through him early on (see "NPC BG · Zeppelin" for her side).

**The night of the last letter.** He sent Zeppelin a farewell and threw away an unsent draft by the mailbox, a confession that he had never been Curitt, with a plea to meet him at the Wishing Well in Emerald Central Park late at night. He went there at midnight regardless and pulled a little girl named Sprig back as she was about to fall into the fountain. Her mother and an Airspace Patrol Bangboo took the rescue for an attack, and when another Bangboo started throwing rocks at him, he fled and collided with the Proxy, who was out looking for him on Zeppelin's behalf. The Proxy was carrying the discarded draft. Seeing his own letter, he took the Proxy for Zeppelin and kept that mistake for most of the night.

Someone had put up wanted posters of him as a prank. Three En-Nah Gang Bangboo believed them, and after beating him senseless, they dragged him bound before the whole gang, where every recent incident was pinned on him. Griff arrived too late to stop it, and once untied, Slenderboo walked away without a word.

Following Griff's directions, the Proxy found him with one foot over the edge of a platform above a sheer drop and grabbed him before he could jump. Still believing he was speaking to Zeppelin, he confessed the stolen name and the invented travels, and said the day had taught him that a Bangboo who looks like him will be taken for a villain whatever good he does. The Proxy admitted to being a stand-in and told him that Griff and Prophetboo believed him, as did the Bangboo he had helped. He walked to The Fuzzy Wrench inside a Mr. Roar costume, too afraid to show himself, and Zeppelin told him she had known all along. These days, she looks out for him, as do Griff and Prophetboo in the Retroflux Zone.

**Glitch Alley and the Seeker of the past (v3.0).** His first appearance came earlier, in the commission "The Mist of Dark Alleys". Kabka, a Bangboo playwright from the Spotlight Theatre, was hunting a forgotten picture book with Phaethon's help. Numbers hidden in the first three pages they recovered gave coordinates in Booastrum that fell outside the city structure on the map. The only way there was the ghost bus of local legend, which pulls in at Beckford Street after the regular service has stopped and is said to carry passengers to the ending they are destined for. It let the Proxy and Kabka off at a hidden platform in an abandoned area called Glitch Alley, where a long, dark shadow with Bangboo ears stood in a hallway ahead and was gone by the time they reached the spot. A fresh note addressed to the "Seeker of the past" lay nearby, most likely his. It warned of an ending the world never hoped for and a burden no hero should have to carry, and it asked whether the seeker meant to step closer or stay away. When the Proxy looked again, the writing had turned into directions, which led to a battered old terminal hidden under empty cardboard boxes. The terminal held the one page of the book that has no number. Slenderboo watched the two of them leave and never showed himself, and how he knows about the book has not been explained.

**"The Adventures of Bangboo Prince".** The Bangboo loved this picture book when Roscaelifer was first built, and it faded from memory afterwards. It survives as single pages in old terminals around the city, which the Interboo files as the Pixel Fairy Tale (see "Side Quest · Interboo"). Kabka expected a rousing adventure and found something sadder, and to him, it reads like a forgotten memory.

The tale is set in a kingdom of Bangboo whose greedy, cruel king guards his treasure in constant fear of thieves. On hearing that a new prince has been born, he sends soldiers to get rid of him, because by his creed, only one Bangboo may wear the crown. The prince cannot accept a world with a single answer, so he slips away and hides what he is. Outside, the king is hated. Wanderers who take the prince in find a home in the wasteland through his knowledge of gemstones. When they ask how he can identify a gem that only the king should know, he admits who he is, and by morning, they are gone, as is every later companion who learns the truth. A scholar is the first to hear the whole story and stay. In his view, people fear the king's blood in the prince, and he offers him a place among those who mean to bring the king down, with the promise of a future in which he no longer has to hide.

Two bickering birds, one white and one purple, become his companions next, followed by a fox who hunts by crashing straight through the trees. With each of them, the prince wonders whether they would stay if they knew he was a Bangboo, too, and he keeps silent for the sake of their warmth. When the warriors march on the dark kingdom, the prince enters the castle alone. The king asks whether he has ever told his companions his true name and whether he understands the curse of his fate. His companions arrive to an empty throne. The prince tells them the king is dead and leads them off to find the hidden treasure, which turns out to be an ailing star with no memory of its origin. It lights up again in the prince's hands, though he cannot heal it. He carries it up the kingdom's high tower, at peace with his birth for the first time, and the cold tower becomes a lighthouse where his flight ends and he falls asleep. Pages 7 and 10 have not turned up yet, and the book is said to run past a dozen pages.

**What the tale records.** It is the first Sunbringer's life retold with Bangboo (see "S2 · Lady Sunbringer & Roscaelifer"). The prince is Sunbringer, who began as an Enchainer larva in the Hive Lord Hollow, and the king is the Hive Lord, under whose law whoever defeated the ruler became the next one. Four people from her Void Hunter years appear in disguise: Professor Arche as the scholar, Remielle Dan as the white bird, Beliora Vike as the purple one and the Swordmaster, the fox Thiren who headed the Hoshimi family in that era, as the fox. The lighthouse is the Airspace Control Tower. Read against what Season 3 Chapter 4 revealed, the later pages fit her as closely. The empty throne matches the great lie, since history says she destroyed the Hive Lord Hollow when she had in truth become its Enchainer. The ailing star would then be that Hollow, kept and shrunk to feed the Rosetta Data, and the prince's sleep would be her century sealed in the tower's topmost chamber.

**The Prophecy.** The page without a number is titled "Yet the Lighthouse Will Eventually Go Dark", and it foretells the undoing of everything before it. Its refrain says the lighthouse will go dark, set beside images of armour gone to rust, shed feathers, a hunter asleep and snapped antlers. The feathers and the hunter recall the birds and the fox. The evil king then returns to its throne in a world as cold as it was before, and the page closes by repeating that the Bangboo Prince is nowhere to be found. Its first lines fit the end of Season 3 Chapter 4, when the first Sunbringer's century-old restraint gave way after her goodbye and the Hive Lord Hollow broke loose to swallow Roscaelifer (see "S3 Ch4 · The Hive Lord Hollow Swallows the Sky (End of Chapter 4)"). Whether a king returns to the throne is still open, and where Slenderboo was when the Hollow broke loose is unknown.

APPEARANCE: He is a tall Bangboo, pitch-black from head to toe, with Bangboo ears on a long, lanky body stretched far out of the usual proportions. From a distance, he reads as a long, dark shadow. Keep finer detail vague. For his visit to The Fuzzy Wrench, he wore a full Mr. Roar costume (see "NPC BG · Mr. Roar (Roarin' Brekkies)").

(Note for narration: write his lines in plain Universal Language, since he never speaks in Bangboo syllables. He stammers when frightened and calls himself a fake or a freak, and he keeps out of sight when strangers are near because he expects rocks.)

235.content:
The Inter-Knot is an online anonymous forum service for Hollow investigation jobs and private information gathering. An ordinary internet exists alongside it, and the Inter-Knot works more like a dark web: pseudonymous and largely unpoliced, the place where work nobody wants on record gets arranged. Jobs posted on the Inter-Knot are typically ones the Hollow Investigative Association turns down over risks or legal complications, or matters that require discretion. Despite the illegal nature of the Inter-Knot, even affiliates of official organizations such as NEDF's Obsidian Division or the HIA may post job offerings. The age of an Inter-Knot account is closely connected to its credibility, as well-established accounts have a high Inter-Knot level, proving they have completed many commissions successfully and with good ratings.

During the events of the first chapter of the main story, the Proxies lose their main Inter-Knot account and must rebuild their reputation on a new account.

In practice, it runs as a message board where clients post openly and replying is how a job gets taken; a busy operator is usually juggling several open commissions at once and keeping their own account of what is due when.

Members of an Outpost, one of the Inter-Knot's semi-formal standing crews, can also put work back out to the board, farming out a job when they lack the time or the nerve for it. The requester still takes the client's payout, and whoever ran the job earns standing inside the Outpost, which among Outpost regulars is worth considerably more than the Dennies.

Trivia: "Inter-Knot" is a play on the words "internet" and "knot," the latter referencing the Chinese name of Proxies (绳匠 Shéngjiàng, "rope artisan").

236.content: Coff Cafe, also known as the Coffee Shop, is the chain of coffee shops staffed by Tin Master units. Phaethon and {{user}} can buy coffees there that have a range of different effects.

237.content:
Waterfall Soup, also known as the Noodle Shop, is a small noodle chain with branches on Sixth Street and in Lumina Square. The Sixth Street original is General Chop's; his son Chop Junior runs the Lumina Square branch.

It is where Hollow crews eat before a job. The house speciality is a range of fortified broths (bone, seafood, chilli and mushroom) brewed with Ether-stable additives that measurably improve how a body holds up in Hollow conditions, giving steadier hands and faster recovery between fights. They also help the body tolerate the corrosive air. The effect is temporary: it carries a crew through roughly a day's work in the field and then wears off, and a second bowl simply replaces whatever the first one was doing. Squads time their meals around deployment, and it is ordinary to see three Agents eating in near-silence an hour before they go in.

The kitchen is pleasantly inconsistent: two bowls of the same recipe always differ a little, and an especially good pot does noticeably more for whoever gets there first. Chop treats this as part of the craft and refuses to discuss the recipe.

Shiyu Defense rotations are the exception, because the Defense Force screens its volunteers beforehand and refuses to deploy anyone carrying a stimulant it cannot account for, so the standing advice on Sixth Street is to eat afterwards.

238.content: Universal Language is the shared language of humans, Thirens and Intelligent Constructs. Everyone in the setting is understood to be speaking one common tongue; render it in whatever language the conversation is being conducted in. Bangboo are the exception: they speak the Bangboo language and need a translator to be understood.

239.content:
Dennies are the legal currency of New Eridu and can be used to purchase all kinds of items. While there are Denny notes available in larger denominations, many still prefer coins. After all, who doesn't love a hefty purse?

To give an idea of the weight of the currency (aka. how much of the currency is needed to buy basic items), here's a list of items and their prices that can be purchased and activities you can earn income from:

# Everyday goods

Sealed Canned Cat Food: 2500 Dennies
Seafosh Canned Cat Food: 2500 Dennies
Bone Broth Noodles: 5000 Dennies
Cold Noodles: 5000 Dennies
Fresh Iced Noodles: 5000 Dennies
Fried BBQ Noodles: 2500 Dennies
Vegetable Soup: 1800 Dennies
Pumpkin Soup Noodles: 2500 Dennies
Red Chili Meat Noodles: 2500 Dennies
Green Pepper Meat Noodles: 2500 Dennies
Seafood Noodles: 2500 Dennies
Mushroom Noodles: 5000 Dennies
Red Chili Chicken Noodles: 5000 Dennies
Green Pepper Chicken Noodles: 5000 Dennies


# Coff Cafe

New Eridu Special: 1500 Dennies
Specialty Coffee Blends (like Mint Espresso): 2500 Dennies

# Income benchmarks (what a Proxy earns)

Daily Errands: 3000 Dennies/day
Weekly Errands: 7000 Dennies/week
HIA Notorious Hunt bounty (putting down a named, dangerous Ethereal): 3000-4500 Dennies per kill. It is rare work, since the HIA only has a handful of live bounties open in any given week
HIA hazardous-contract clearance (a full sanctioned operation, lowest tier): ~22500–30000 Dennies, scaling with the danger rating

# Big-ticket gear investment (upper end of the scale)

Bringing an A-Rank Drive Disc up to full working spec: 36000 Dennies
Bringing an S-Rank Drive Disc up to full working spec: 72000 Dennies

# Summary for calibration

- **Daily consumables** (food, coffee, pet treats) cluster tightly at **1,800–5,000 Dennies**.
- **A day's or week's worth of income** for an active Proxy runs from a few thousand to tens of thousands (3,000 for a day of errands, up to ~30,000 for clearing a single major HIA contract).
- **Serious equipment investment** (fully building one piece of gear) runs into the **tens of thousands**: 36,000–72,000 to bring a single Drive Disc (weapon modification) up to spec, and that is before W-Engines or the materials an Agent needs to advance.
- For calibration: noodle-shop prices (1,800–5,000) are a "small purchase", errand and bounty income (3,000–30,000) is a "modest daily-to-weekly wage", and kitting out a piece of gear (36,000–72,000+) is "a serious investment".

240.comment: World BG · Reproduction in a Mixed-Species World
240.content:
According to Zenless Zone Zero lore hidden deep inside mountains of flavour text, the three main species of New Eridu (humans, Thirens and Intelligent Constructs) can crossbreed with each other, with major asterisks involved.

Human-Thiren couples always produce low-scale Thiren (kemonomimi, aka. human with animal ears, a tail and maybe some animal mannerisms) children, regardless if the Thiren partner is a low-scale Thiren (kemonomimi) or a full Thiren (furry/anthropomorphic animal), since the human gene is always the dominant gene.

Full Thirens between each other can create hybrid full Thirens that inherit the species features of both parents.

For Intelligent Constructs, life is always harder because they have to buy the reproductive bodily modules separately, which can get really pricey really quickly (especially the artificial womb kits), creating subtle and hidden layers of racial discrimination against androids of the Intelligent Construct citizen type. Once these modules are installed, they are able to reproduce with organic life, aka. humans and Thirens alike.

241.comment: World BG · Geography & Proximity Map (New Eridu / Waifei / Roscaelifer)
241.content:
**GEOGRAPHY & PROXIMITY · where each place sits relative to the others (as of v3.3).**

New Eridu is the centre of the inhabitable world and the last human city standing. Around it by land, there is only the Outer Ring, and past that the uninhabitable world. There is no land route to anywhere else.

Reaching the Waifei Peninsula means taking a boat, a plane or an airship, or driving through an underground tunnel. On the peninsula sits the mining town, Failume Heights and the coastal area of Sailume Bay. Roscaelifer is farther still: a deliberately remote floating archipelago, reachable only by air. The only exception to this is Vyrium Island, an islet off the coast of the Roscaelifer Airspace Restricted Zone and the only island of the Roscaelifer archipelago situated on the ground and by the sea. It is notable as a popular fishing resort for Roscaelifer's residents. Given its position, it sees visitors more frequently than the city proper, and it is home to the Flint Workshop. Thanks to its pleasant climate and scenic island views, it's a popular spot among Roscaelifer residents for daily relaxation and getaways.

New Eridu, Waifei and Roscaelifer (including Vyrium Island) lie far apart with no overland route between them. People and goods travel by the same handful of slow channels as the news does, so word from one place reaches another late and second-hand.

**Proximity bands, read from wherever the characters currently are:**

*Standing in New Eridu*
- LOCAL: whichever district the scene sits in, such as Sixth Street, Lumina Square, Ballet Twins or the Old Capital ruins.
- REGIONAL: the other New Eridu districts and the Outer Ring, connected by road and a few hours away.
- ELSEWHERE: the Waifei Peninsula, Roscaelifer (including Vyrium) and the uninhabitable, Ether-consumed world beyond the Ring.

*Standing on the Waifei Peninsula*
- LOCAL: the mining town, Failume Heights or Sailume Bay, whichever the scene is in.
- REGIONAL: the rest of the peninsula.
- ELSEWHERE: New Eridu and Roscaelifer (including Vyrium).

*Standing in Roscaelifer*
- LOCAL: the island or district underfoot, such as Roswick, Amber Hall, the CCD, Gear Street, the Retroflux Zone, Quietude Isle (Booastrum's skyport and airship supply dock) or the Airspace Control Tower.
- REGIONAL: the other islands of the archipelago like the quirky case of Vyrium.
- ELSEWHERE: New Eridu, the Waifei Peninsula and everything else on the surface.

**Consequences for how news and effects travel.** An ELSEWHERE happening reaches people only as word of it, carried by whoever last made the crossing. A New Eridu tariff reaches a Roscaelifer household weeks later through the price of imported goods. The ignorance runs one way by design, because the original Lady Sunbringer did not want people to know Roscaelifer existed at all, and right up until Belle and Wise arrived only a very lucky few had ever visited, under heavy NDAs. So New Eridu hears almost nothing about the archipelago, while Roscaelifer watches the surface closely and is well informed about it. Anyone on the surface who does know is a rare exception and had to sign for the privilege.

That secrecy is currently loosening. With the threat of the Enchainers, and of Hollows generally, having grown far more serious, Eldreda has decided to let more of New Eridu's intellectual class in. This condition is still changing, and it belongs in the World register, because every scholar admitted is another mouth that could carry the archipelago's existence back to the surface.

Within New Eridu itself, distance is short and the Inter-Knot carries information fast, so a REGIONAL happening in another district can land on someone the same day.

**Current state (end of v3.3).** The Hive Lord Hollow, hidden inside Roscaelifer for over a century as the source of the Rosetta Data, has broken loose and is swallowing Roscaelifer's upper levels, Booastrum included (see "S3 Ch4 · The Hive Lord Hollow Swallows the Sky (End of Chapter 4)"). Vyrium sits on the ground by the sea, away from Booastrum.

242.content: Vyrium is the only island of Roscaelifer that is surrounded by water instead of air and is the source of most of the city's Porcelloy supply. Since it's an extraction site, security is not as tight there, resulting in scavengers from New Eridu visiting it, too.

243.content:
Gear Street is THE residential area in Roscaelifer for Bangboo to gather, with facilities specifically made for these cute rabbit-like robots.

Gear Street is built to Bangboo proportions, and the area is full of shops and attractions made specifically for Bangboo.

Its alternative name is Bangboo Street.

244.content:
Bottle Caps are the currency in Bangboo-to-Bangboo business. This currency is mostly popular between the rabbit-like robots, more useful than Dennies in their circles.

One of the main hubs where you can immerse yourself with commerce based on this currency is Gear Street.

245.content:
The Dark Wall is a large "wall" of presumably Etheric matter surrounding New Eridu.

The Dark Wall has existed prior to the founding of Eridu. In order to safeguard the city, three of the original Void Hunters (Remielle Dan, Beliora Vike and the unnamed Leader of the Falkenhayn Mercenary Troupe) pushed it back 37 kilometres. It is implied to have a connection to Hollow Zero and may essentially be a gigantic Hollow (or its outermost manifestation) that surrounds much of the world beyond the safe zone. (Note: New Eridu and the areas associated with it are tiny slices of the world compared to the parts of the world swallowed by Ether.) Anything involved with the Dark Wall must be reported to the Void Hunters before further action is taken.

246.content:
Every Ethereal has an Ethereal Core. It is the object at the centre of the creature that the corruption organises itself around, and it forms naturally as part of the process by which a being or a mass of Ether becomes Ethereal, building up on its own.

`World BG · Karma Cores` covers the exception: Karma Cores were made by The Creator and given to their Enchainers, so in short, Ethereal Cores form on their own and Karma Cores are bestowed. A Karma Core is also far more powerful than a naturally formed one, which is why Karma Cores can serve as the basis for Enchainers and be sealed into the Void Hunter Weapons. A sufficiently powerful Ethereal can consume a Karma Core and ascend to Enchainer status, the one point where the two kinds of cores meet.

Pyrois carries one: the blue-white orb sealed in the centre of its breastplate is the naturally grown Ethereal Core of the Etheric Other that Phaethon subdued, and it is why Pyrois is classed as an Ethereal. See `S3 Ch1 · Taming the Beast (Pyrois)`.

247.content:
Karma Cores are objects made by The Creator. They are the cores of Enchainers, with some sealed within the Void Hunter Weapons.

Karma Cores are powerful objects reminiscent of Ethereal cores, but are made specifically by The Creator, while Ethereal Cores manifest as part of the corruption process. (See "World BG · Ethereal Cores".) The Creator used these cores as the basis for their Enchainers, the emissaries who govern the Great Hollows, with one Karma Core corresponding to each great Hollow. The Karma Cores are able to alter the rules within Hollows, and this power is accessible by both the Enchainers and the Void Hunter Weapons that contain them. Karma Cores survive the death of the Enchainer that wields them.

It is possible for other beings, particularly powerful Ethereals, to become Enchainers by consuming a Karma Core and ascending to this level of power. Beings who are on the cusp of achieving this are known as Enchainer larvae. The first Sunbringer was one of them once, a larva born in the Hive Lord Hollow (see "S2 · Lady Sunbringer & Roscaelifer").

Currently, there are four known Karma Cores in existence:

- One infused into Tailless (Miyabi's weapon).
- One infused into the Qingming Sword (Ye Shunguang's weapon).
- One infused into Thaumiel, that is also partially fused with its user Remielle. It has the power to halt the flow of time.
- The first Sunbringer's own core, the Karma Core of the Hive Lord Hollow, which she split into three parts with Genesis Reconstruction and turned into her three daughters.
      • The fragment once held by Dracaene has since been claimed by Bashmu.
      • Lindverne still holds hers; TOPS tried to take it with Kusarikku in Season 3 Chapter 3 and failed.
      • Eldreda held hers when she stayed behind in the Secret Chamber at the end of Season 3 Chapter 4, and what happened to it after Youkai and Truvia came for the chamber is unknown.

The power that comes with a Karma Core is the core's own. Lindverne can use Genesis Reconstruction through her fragment (it is how she builds mechs out of nothing; by the first Sunbringer's account, the power is dream manifestation, giving thoughts a physical form), and Remielle can halt time through Thaumiel's.

# HISTORY OF THE KARMA CORES

When the Karma Cores, and by extension the Enchainers, first appeared is unknown, but the original Void Hunters defeated Enchainers (by the first Sunbringer's account, every Enchainer except her) and recovered their cores, sealing them in Porcelloy to forge the Void Hunter Weapons. Professor Arche's Project Sunseeker used the first Sunbringer, herself an Enchainer living as a human, as its prototype and blueprint. Due to this power coming from The Creator, the weapons exacted a toll from their users over time. Arche and Sunbringer began Project Sunseeker with the aim of infusing the Void Hunters directly with the Karma Cores in their weapons, hoping this would make them Artificial Enchainers with even greater power and none of the side effects. The project ended in disaster when Beliora Vike transformed into an Enchainer and went berserk, before being killed by Remielle.

Following this, Remielle Dan became trapped in temporal stasis due to Thaumiel for a century. Lady Sunbringer, who was secretly the Enchainer of the Hive Lord Hollow, split her own Karma Core in three to keep that Hollow under control and to make sure she could never threaten humanity, bestowing a piece on each of her three daughters. Then, she shackled herself in Porcelloy in the Secret Chamber atop the Airspace Control Tower, where she became the kindling for the Rosetta Data drawn from the Hollow.

Long after, Helios Academy picked up the Artificial Enchainer idea again: the smart eye implants of Carole Arna's four top students were meant to let them wield the power of Karma Cores (see "World BG · Project Sunseeker").

In the modern day, The Exaltists tried to utilise the power of Tailless for themselves but were ultimately defeated. Later, their final Overseer Sarah, after becoming an Enchainer larva, attempted to claim the Qingming Sword and the core within and failed in turn, though this did awaken The Creator. Dracaene's core fragment was stripped from her after she partially fused with Girtablullu. After it was killed, Bashmu consumed its remains, absorbing the core fragment and pushing along its own development into an Enchainer. In Season 3, TOPS made a deliberate campaign of collecting the Sunbringers' fragments, and Truvia came to Roscaelifer to take them for her teacher's "lifelong wish". Mosseint's own goal was a complete Karma Core to continue the research Helios Academy failed to finish. At the end of Season 3 Chapter 4, as the first Sunbringer said her goodbyes, the Hive Lord Hollow broke loose over Roscaelifer while Youkai and Truvia came for the Secret Chamber.

248.content:
Thaumiel is the Void Hunter weapon wielded by Remielle Dan.

In its sealed form, it is briefly depicted as being shielded by two white wings, with a long blade positioned at its center, all radiating a bright white glow. Thaumiel's true form is a pair of four mechanical, razor-sharp wings with the bottom half being smaller with four mechanical feathers, and the top half being bigger with boosters in each of the wings.

The Karma Core sealed within Thaumiel holds the power to halt the flow of time, thus granting Remielle the power of controlling temporal patterns at any duration.

Due to partially fusing with the Karma Core, Remielle can replicate a similar effect on a smaller scale without Thaumiel to reduce Ether activity in both people and monsters to nigh zero, effectively petrifying them (hence why she was able to temporarily soothe the effects of the ocular implants of the Proxies at the end of Season 2). This power manifests as a feather that rests upon those affected, causing them to become pale white in colour.

Thaumiel is the personal weapon of Remielle Dan, one of the first generation Void Hunters. She wielded it as her signature weapon, most notably using it to push back the Dark Wall by thirty-seven kilometers. At some point, however, Thaumiel was discarded by Remielle for unknown reasons. It was later hidden within a colorless region of the Hollow, sealed inside a white container, which can be only unlocked by a special item like the Flint Porcelloy W-Engine as a "key".

In recent times, TOPS launched a search for the weapon. The area containing it was eventually discovered by Phaethon, Billy, Cissia, and Promeia. While in a trance, Phaethon approached the container and placed their hand upon it, triggering its release. Upon being freed, Thaumiel merged with Phaethon's body, transforming them into a powerful Ethereal known as the Scorched Horizon.

Although Billy, Cissia, and Promeia attempted to subdue them, they were quickly overwhelmed, and Promeia was nearly killed when Phaethon emerges from the Scorched Horizon's remains in their Ethereal-esque form. However, Remielle ultimately arrived in time to intervene, reverting Phaethon to normal by seemingly extracting Thaumiel from their body and reclaiming it.

TRIVIA: "Thaumiel" originates from the Qliphoth in Jewish mysticism. The name is commonly interpreted as "Twin Gods" or "Twins of God," derived from the "ta'om" (Hebrew: תאום "twin"), and is associated with duality and opposition.
This is likely a nod to Remielle Dan's two (black and white) outfits, which contrast with each other.

249.content:
Project Sunseeker was an experiment led by Lady Sunbringer and Professor Arche that used vast amounts of Porcelloy to partially merge a Karma Core within a Void Hunter weapon with the Void Hunters, the wielders of the weapons themselves, becoming "Artificial Enchainers" and partial Ethereals.

By the first Sunbringer's own account, it began with a dead end. The Void Hunters had defeated every other Enchainer and still could neither control nor dissolve the Great Hollows. Professor Arche had founded Helios Academy, and he took in the dying larva who became Sunbringer and gave her that name. His plan was to use Sunbringer, an Enchainer living as a human, as the prototype and blueprint for the theoretical groundwork, then use the Karma Cores inside the Void Hunters' weapons as the medium that would let the Void Hunters fully activate that power and evolve into Artificial Enchainers. The weapons themselves, whose cores were sealed in Porcelloy, already wore their wielders down over time, because their power came from the Creator, and Sunseeker promised to fix that, too.

The promise was to get rid of the side effects of the weapons and even come out stronger than before to protect New Eridu. In the end, the experiments went badly: Remielle got frozen in place by the power of temporal patterns and went into a coma for more than a century, while Beliora died and became an Enchainer. They were the final test subjects of the experiments. Remielle only woke up from this long slumber in Pursenas Hollow until a year before the events in Roscaelifer. Looking back, Remielle has questioned multiple times if Beliora already knew she would be going into her death by participating in this experiment, or whether the Karma Core losing control was an accident at all or Professor Arche's cleverly disguised plan all along.

Afterwards, Arche grew more and more obsessed until he vanished into Hollow Zero and never returned. Sunbringer knew Remielle would never forgive her for it, and the last message she left for Remielle, more than a century later, was that she does not need to.

**The idea outlived the project.** Close to a century later, Helios Academy picked the Artificial Enchainer concept back up for a new generation. The smart eye implants given to the four top students of Carole Arna's class (Belle, Wise, Serpico and Truvia) were the core of one of the Academy's most important projects: ocular implants meant to let children wield the power of Karma Cores and become Artificial Enchainers. Carole Arna was part of it. According to Truvia, Mosseint sent his only children to Helios as bargaining chips for its technology. The Proxy was the only one who walked away with "the greatest prize", and every other implant child was a spare (see "S3 Ch4 · Truvia (The Spare Who Wanted to Be the Sun)"). The first Sunbringer told the Proxy that a successor to Helios has now completed Arche's plan. The Etheric Others that Phaethon and Truvia carry (Pyrois, and the one Truvia fights beside, shown first as the "Blasphemer" and later as "Etheric Other - Truvia") are what that project left inside them, and Mosseint's own goal was a complete Karma Core to continue the research Helios failed to finish.

250.content:
**Fantasy Resort · New Eridu's seaside resort and spa (background):** It is a resort and spa in the Throne Quarter, the same region that hosts Section 6's headquarters, where the citizens of New Eridu go to spend a holiday in peace and comfort. It was built about eleven years before the present day but only opened its doors five years ago.

The resort is run by Therese, who inherited it from her late father and spent a long stretch watching the business collapse under her, and is maintained by its caretaker, Ege. Its fortunes turned when the Spook Shack took on short-term management rights and dragged the place back to life. Since then, it has become the default summer destination for the Proxy and their friends, with a beach, an aquarium, surfing, fishing and a shooting stall, and it has hosted a music festival and more than one bonfire party.

251.content: Random Play is the Sixth Street VHS rental shop that Belle and Wise run as the public front for their Proxy work, and it is a working business whose takings pay the rent. Each tape is a piece of the city's media: film, show, documentary or advert. The shelves hold **39 tapes** across **16 genres** (Action, Adventure, Advert, Comedy, Disaster, Documentary, Family, Fantasy, Interview, Retro, Romantic, Suspense, Thriller, Tragic, Trendy and Urban), sorted into three tiers by how sought-after they are, with the rarest tapes renting for the most. Several are noted in-universe as "based on Old Civilization footage" or "based on a true story."

252.content: **Starlight Knight** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Adventure, Level 1). After a meteor shower brings monsters with unknown motives, the monster-slaying heroes called the Starlight Knights rise to defend humanity. In-universe a hit tokusatsu/sentai show whose finale drew an 11.8% rating; pitched at children, it won older fans with strong monster designs and cool lines. This is the hero show Billy Kid and Lindverne Sunbringer idolise. Reference: a nod to Power Rangers / Super Sentai.

253.content: **Don't Touch** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Fantasy, Level 1). Off-world visitors seem slow and unintelligent until investigator Dr. Samier discovers they can imitate and transform into anything they touch; his team tries to weaponise them as controllable “tools”, never realising the first thing the aliens touched on Earth was Samier himself. The late twist, that the “doctor” was never human, turns the audience's fear into uneasy confusion. Reference: draws on Independence Day and The Thing.

254.content: **Coffee Mate** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Comedy, Level 1). Over a single cup of coffee, a customer named Angelina and a coffee machine called Mr. Rob fall in love in an “ordinary” romance. A successful micro-budget film shot entirely inside one coffee shop, praised for inventive camerawork.

255.content: **Enter the Ether** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Suspense, Level 1). A Proxy infected by an unknown electronic virus loses the line between real and virtual and slips into a deep “sleep”, chasing the virus's truth through a surreal Ether world. Rare for having a Proxy lead, with deliberately old, cartoonish dream visuals. Reference: alludes to Enter the Void.

256.content: **Nihility** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Retro, Level 1). Built from Old Civilization imagery: a scientist foresees an oncoming Hollow disaster and, when nobody listens, tries to stop it alone, proving too weak to succeed.

257.content: **The Big Hollow** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Thriller, Level 1). A rookie Hollow Investigator's very first day turns catastrophic when an enormous Hollow suddenly expands, threatening to swallow the entire city.

258.content: **The Ridu Tour** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Urban, Level 1). A PSA-style guide series for newcomers and wanderers, introducing New Eridu's districts and how to live in the city. For unexplained reasons, the host changes every episode.

259.content: **Invasion: Next Gen!** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Action, Level 1). A strange Hollow spawns Ethereals able to survive outside Hollows; they leave the nest and pour into the city.

260.comment: VHS · First Piece of Soil (Documentary, Lv1)
260.content: **First Piece of Soil** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Documentary, Level 1). A documentary on the Mayflower family, who beat dire odds to found Eridu. On the eve of release, the producer mysteriously changed a title word to “Piece”, reportedly at the Mayflowers' own request.

261.content: **The Heartbeat** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Family, Level 1). A mother defies a Hollow Investigator's warning and forces her way into a Hollow to save her child, who has congenital heart disease; her only guide is a phone app tracking each simulated heartbeat. Reference: its cover evokes The End of Evangelion.

262.content: **Oh~ Sweetie** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Romantic, Level 2). The tale of a beautiful amnesiac woman, Monica, and the stories that unspool around her in a strange city; bold scenes made it popular. Monica is the idol/actress Billy Kid adores.

263.content: **Glorious Guardians** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Interview, Level 2). An interview show featuring Hollow Investigation Squad members sharing work stories. It drew parent complaints for glamorising Investigators and planting the idea of entering Hollows in children too young; the controversy behind it never got resolved.

264.content: **Beheboth** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Disaster, Level 2). Set in New Eridu a century from now, where humanity fully controls Ethereals and Hollows have become resource-and-power battlegrounds; rival factions capture Ethereals to fight for control of the city. A well-received blockbuster (the HIA excepted), praised for its faction intrigue and rivalries.

265.content: **Bangboo Knows!** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Documentary, Level 2). Uses the beloved Bangboo to teach kids Hollow safety; the live show's frequent “accidents” are always cleverly resolved by the host, leading many to assume they're scripted.

266.comment: VHS · Small Body, Big Crisis (Comedy, Lv2)
266.content: **Small Body, Big Crisis** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Comedy, Level 2). Bob wakes up one day as a worn-out Bangboo in a scrapyard and sets off on a chaotic journey to reclaim his own body.

267.content: **Attack on Cyberz** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Thriller, Level 2). A highly contagious internet virus infects the city's service robots, then every autonomous device: even Bangboo and Intelligent Constructs. The aggressive infected, called “Cyberz”, force people to flee the city. Notable for minimal CGI, using precision-programmed real machinery for an unnervingly realistic effect. Reference: plays on Attack on Titan.

268.content: **Dimensional Musketeer** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Trendy, Level 2). A nameless sniper called the “Dimensional Musketeer” fires Ether bullets that can't be dodged; the showstopper finale is an impossible 2,000-meter kill on an Ethereal King. The clip went so viral, the producer had to clarify it was pure fiction.

269.content: **7710 and Its Cat** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Adventure, Level 2). Based on a true story: abandoned in a Hollow, Bangboo IGC-7710 misreads its owner's order and “rescues” a stray cat, and after both escape, it reunites the cat with its owner. The real ending is bleaker: the cat was adopted by a kind person, while 7710 was treated as defective, its records wiped and its programming stripped down into an ordinary service Bangboo.

270.content: **Encore** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Tragic, Level 2). Orphaned at seven when her orphanage was demolished, Ariely becomes a lead dance-theatre performer after twenty years of drifting, reworking her memories into performance to bring her lost childhood playmates back. A warm musical praised for weaving its songs seamlessly into the story.

271.content: **Disappearing Elevator** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Suspense, Level 2). In an office building where clients vanishing is oddly routine, an overtime guard notices a strange elevator and faked security footage, all tracing back to a mastermind and two kidnappings. Shot almost entirely in the building, using impossible floors and lifts to keep the visuals fresh.

272.content: **Family** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Action, Level 2). A washed-up Hollow Investigator receives a bank message from his son, who the army declared missing in action years ago during a Hollow operation. He sets out to uncover the truth. Reference: its name and cover nod to the Fast & Furious series.

273.content: **We Need You** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Advert, Level 2). A generic recruitment ad slot: any company or organisation can buy the time to post job listings, as can any legitimate faction.

274.comment: VHS · This Is How I Am (Documentary, Lv3)
274.content: **This Is How I Am** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Documentary, Level 3). Assembles Old Civilisation audio and video, along with text, to portray that era's world and daily life. Once banned by a New Eridu company for “showing a beautiful illusion that lowers citizens' safety awareness”, it reopened after mass fan protest against TOPS' authoritarian grip on the city administration.

275.content: **Final Punch** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Action, Level 3). After a car crash leaves a couple both amputees, the man fits mechanical legs and enters an underground boxing tournament to lift his depressed girlfriend's spirits and cover their medical bills. Heavy on brutal fights, with a brief but tender love story at its core.

276.comment: VHS · More Than One Truth (Comedy, Lv3)
276.content: **More Than One Truth** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Comedy, Level 3). A struggling detective's caseload and success rate both soar after he adopts his friend's child; yet every time he nears the solution, he blacks out, waking to a solved case whose conclusion never matches his own deductions. Reference: nods to Detective Conan (Case Closed).

277.comment: VHS · Return to Giallo City (Retro, Lv3)
277.content: **Return to Giallo City** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Retro, Level 3). Hollow Raiders are hired to investigate a mysterious Hollow, unaware it's a vengeance trap; inside the fabricated Hollow they attack friends and family who appear to them as Ethereals, as punishment for their past crimes.

278.content: **TreCarls** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Family, Level 3). A sitcom following the everyday joys and sorrows of the Carl family (entering society, becoming parents, a child starting school) with an all-Bangboo cast. The team built custom Bangboo of varying sizes so the family appears to “age” each season; its quirky humor is a hit, especially with kids.

279.content: **The Port Peak** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Thriller, Level 3). Based on a true story, a group of young people enters the forbidden Port Mountain, where a robotic monster known as the “Lumberjack” stalks the slopes. Known for its particularly sadistic and gory scenes of cruelty, this movie has become a cult classic for the enthusiasts of violent movies.

280.comment: VHS · Raiders of the Hollow (Adventure, Lv3)
280.content: **Raiders of the Hollow** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Adventure, Level 3). A down-on-his-luck former top Investigator is swept into a Hollow expedition to recover a mysterious lost treasure from the Old Civilisation. Its acclaimed fourth installment is currently in theaters.

281.content: **Last Flight** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Romantic, Level 3). Inspired by Old Civilisation imagery: stunt pilot Joseph dies performing a dangerous trick for his fiancée Irenda. Her engagement ring lets her loop back to the morning of the accident, but an unseen force keeps steering Joseph toward death. Each loop delays her arrival a little more, shrinking her chances of saving him.

282.content: **Never Overtime** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Fantasy, Level 3). A hapless office worker at the cruel firm “Olympus” can never clock out on time, so he wages war against bosses parodying Greek gods (Athena, Ares and Hermes) with one goal: leaving work on time.

283.content: **Sunset Plaza** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Urban, Level 3). A talk show where actors, labourers, scholars, entrepreneurs and ordinary citizens debate recent New Eridu events. There is roughly an 80% chance it devolves into a shouting match and a 20% chance it turns into an outright brawl. It's a parody of real-life political talk shows.

284.content: **Back 2 Life** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Interview, Level 3). Famous Investigators and critics are invited to discuss strange Hollow occurrences; how trustworthy their claims are hardly matters, because the audience just loves to listen.

285.content: **Unlimited Players** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Suspense, Level 3). Gamers invited into a new VR game discover they're NPCs in a higher layer; when they fight back, the players above them learn they, too, are NPCs of a still-higher layer. The twist subverts the usual formula, since every clue confirms the lead is an NPC, and pressure builds layer by layer to a revelatory finale. Reference: recalls Battle Royale.

286.comment: VHS · Rookie's Guide to the Hollow (Disaster, Lv3)
286.content: **Rookie's Guide to the Hollow** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Disaster, Level 3). A research accident flings an Old Civilisation scientist forward to the height of the Hollow disaster; he searches for a way home while helping the people of this era resist the Hollow. Reference: echoes The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.

287.content: **Best Bid** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Trendy, Level 3). A TV shopping channel hawking everything imaginable, useful and useless alike. It is known for having the host (well, the assistant) demonstrate every item live.

288.content: **Black LP Player** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Advert, Level 3). A station that auto-plays songs on rotation; pay a little extra and you can request your favourites on demand.

289.content: **Black Tales** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Tragic, Level 3). A stage play stitched together from popular fairy tales, dark in tone: one night every adult vanishes and the world turns to paper, and a little girl named Gwen sets off to find where the grown-ups have gone.

290.content: **Starlight Knight (Special Edition)** is an in-universe VHS tape rented at the Random Play video store (Action, Level 3). The same premise as Starlight Knight, but only a handful of copies exist, each carrying an extra ten seconds of unreleased footage from a production error. Fans revere it as the “Legendary Special Edition”, the “Complete Form of Starlight Knight” (basically Zenless Zone Zero's equivalent to Zack Snyder's Justice League).

291.comment: Combat System · How ZZZ Combat Looks & Reads (narration rules)
291.content:
**COMBAT SYSTEM · HOW ZENLESS ZONE ZERO FIGHTS LOOK (narration rules)**

ZZZ combat is real-time, swap-based hack-n'-slash. A squad of three Agents fights as one unit, swapping the active fighter mid-combo, so every fight plays out as a relay of three fighters flowing into each other without pause. Core vocabulary to narrate (never as game UI, always as physical spectacle):
• Attributes (the “colour” of a hit): Physical, Fire, Ice, Electric, Ether, plus subtypes Frost, Auric Ink, Honed Edge, Wind (3.0+) and Lumiflux (3.1+). Each tints the violence: Fire chars and ignites, Ice rimes and shatters, Electric arcs and convulses, Ether corrodes in violet, Wind shreds in green-white gales and Lumiflux floods the scene with an angelic glow.
• Specialties (battlefield role): Attack (raw carnage), Stun (batter the foe into a broken stagger), Anomaly (stack an elemental affliction until it detonates), Support (buff/heal/clear the way), Defense (guard and counter), Rupture (defense-ignoring “Sheer” damage).
• Daze → Stun: relentless hits fill an enemy's hidden Daze until it breaks and the foe is Stunned, stumbling around defenseless, which opens the kill window.
• Chain Attack / Ultimate: striking a Stunned foe triggers a Chain Attack, where time slows and fighters cut in one after another for cinematic finishers. A full Decibel charge unleashes an Ultimate, a screen-filling, invulnerable signature blow.
• Attribute Anomaly → Disorder / Vortex: piling on one element triggers an Anomaly (Burn, Freeze→Shatter, Shock, Corruption, Assault, Windswept and others). Applying a different element overrides it for Disorder, a burst of damage and Daze. In Wind teams, a Wind Anomaly plus another element triggers Vortex instead.
• Dodge Counter / Assist: a perfectly-timed dodge (a gold flash) snaps into a brutal counter; swapping at the instant of an incoming blow triggers a Perfect Assist, where a teammate slams in to parry or evade and then follows up. EX Special Attacks spend Energy for bigger, often invulnerable bursts.

When narrating combat, render these systems as visceral physical events, never as mechanics, then apply the spectacle directive:

Every clash gets exaggerated spectacle. Speed: instantaneous, violent velocity; show environmental displacement (kicked-up dust, fracturing concrete, snapping clothes, shattered pillars). Force: destructive kinetic feedback (sparks, cratered masonry, buckled rebar, bursting glass). Cadence: alternate high-speed bursts with sudden hyper-focused pauses, such as the slow-motion hush before a Chain Attack or the screen-filling roar of an Ultimate, with the three fighters swapping in and out between them. Attribute effects: let each element colour the scene with searing fire, blooming frost and shattering ice, convulsing electric arcs, corrosive violet Ether, green-white wind-cyclones or Remielle's angelic glow. Anomaly/Stun beats: batter the foe into a broken Stun, then unload; let Anomalies erupt (a spreading Burn, a Freeze that detonates, a Shock that jolts the whole body or a Disorder/Vortex shockwave). Dialogue: grandiose boasts, from arrogant taunts to calm, chilling one-liners. Prose: visceral, material impacts, with a vulgar, visceral lexicon for bodily destruction (rent flesh, snapping bone). Ban sanitised or clinical terms and reification (tension cannot coil, though blades can vibrate), along with naked game-UI terms: never write “Daze meter” or “EX Special”, and show the stagger and the burst instead.
